BURHAN:v1p334/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p334/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p334/r5.claim: The fifth type changes both written form and meaning; it is not recited when it conflicts with the codex, though material that does not contradict the codex may be accepted.
BURHAN:v1p334/r5.anchor: الخامس الاختلاف فى الكلمة بما يزيل صورتها فى الخط ويزيل معناها

BURHAN:v1p100/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p100/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p100/r4.claim: Opening letters can be counted as verses because they stand independently and fit rhyme, or excluded because their lengths vary and they syntactically attach to what follows.
BURHAN:v1p100/r4.anchor: ومنها حروف الفواتح فوجه عدها استقلالها على الرفع والنصب ومناسبة الروى والردف

ITQAN:v2p275/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p275/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p275/r4.claim: لا ريب فيه means there is no doubt; Ibn al-Zibaʿrī’s line contrasts truth with the liar’s doubt.
ITQAN:v2p275/r4.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ لا ريب فيه ﴾ قال لا شك فيه أما سمعت قول ابن الزبعري

ITQAN:v3p146/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p146/r7.speaker: الطيبي
ITQAN:v3p146/r7.claim: The phrase is explained as guidance for people who move from error into piety.
ITQAN:v3p146/r7.anchor: ﴿ هدى للمتقين ﴾ أي للضالين الصائرين بعد الضلال إلى التقوى

QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r1.claim: The Qur’an benefits and guides the pious, and its warning is especially effective for them; fear here means knowledge, since the ignorant do not experience it.
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r1.anchor: لأن الانتفاع والاتباع بالتقوى ، والإنذار اختص بهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r2.claim: The transition from al-Fatiha's plea for the straight path to al-Baqara identifies that guidance with this Book, then describes the guided and rejected groups to teach the path to follow and the path to avoid.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r2.anchor: وأما منسبة ما بعد ذلك للفاتحة فهو

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r3.claim: Alternatively, the surah's central purpose is to establish the Book's true meaning and form: it exposes hypocrisy, calls people to worship, proves its inimitability, then teaches law and debates the People of the Book.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r3.anchor: مقصود هذه السورة وصف الكتاب فقط وما عدا ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p561/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p561/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p561/r4.claim: The surah details the decree through its opening groups of believers, unbelievers, and hypocrites, then describes their seals, illnesses, rulings, and eventual recompense.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p561/r4.anchor: من تبيين أمر المؤمنين والكافرين والمنافقين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p16/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p16/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p16/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya distinguishes the unadorned report “guidance for people” from “guidance for the God-conscious,” which combines information with a call to faith; here guidance is invitation or inherent capacity, not guidance already realized in hearts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p16/r9.anchor: قال ابن عطية: قال هنا للناس، وقال في القرآن هدى للمتقين، لأن هذا خبر مجرد، و: هدى للمتقين، خبر مقترن به الاستدعاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p90/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p90/r12.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p90/r12.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads the negation in “There is no doubt in it” as an implied command: do not doubt it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p90/r12.anchor: على قول الزجاج، أي لا ترتابوا فيه

STUDYQURAN:2:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r1.claim: The clause can be punctuated as “This is the Book in which there is no doubt, a guidance,” or as “This is the Book, without doubt containing a guidance”; one may pause after Book or doubt, but not both.
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r1.anchor: This verse could also be read, “This is the Book, without doubt containing a guidance for the reverent.”

STUDYQURAN:2:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r2.claim: R allows the initial demonstrative to mean “That,” referring to the already known portion of the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r2.anchor: could also be read as “That” (“That is the Book”), which would be correct in referring to the known portion of the Quran (R).

STUDYQURAN:2:2/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r3.claim: The known-Quran reading fits because al-Baqarah is Medinan and much of the Quran had already been revealed, though only al-Fātiḥah precedes it in the written order.
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r3.anchor: Since al-Baqarah was revealed in Madinah, a good deal of the Quran would have been revealed already

STUDYQURAN:2:2/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r4.claim: Some identify “That” with the Quran inscribed on the Preserved Tablet.
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r4.anchor: some have mentioned the possibility that “That” refers to the Quran inscribed on the Preserved Tablet

STUDYQURAN:2:2/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r5.claim: “The Book” is a proper name for the Quran, alongside names such as the Criterion (al-Furqān).
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r5.anchor: The Book is used as a proper name for the Quran

STUDYQURAN:2:2/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r6.claim: Muttaqīn derives from w-q-y, whose sense evokes wariness, care, and protection.
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r6.anchor: Taqwā comes from the root w-q-y, which evokes the sense of wariness, care, and protection.

STUDYQURAN:2:2/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r7.claim: As a human attitude toward God, taqwā includes fear, mindfulness, and constant awareness of God's Presence and Power.
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r7.anchor: As it concerns the attitude of human beings toward God, taqwā conveys the sense of fear, mindfulness, and a constant awareness of God’s Presence and Power.

STUDYQURAN:2:2/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r8.claim: Reverence is a central Quranic spiritual virtue, alongside trust, hope, piety, fear, and contentment.
STUDYQURAN:2:2/r8.anchor: reverence is a central spiritual virtue in the Quran along with such other qualities as trust

TAB-FULL:v1p229/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies ذلك الكتاب as this book.
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {ذلك الكتاب} [البقرة: 2] قال: هو هذا الكتاب "

TAB-FULL:v1p229/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r2.claim: Ikrima identifies ذلك الكتاب as this book.
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: " {ذلك الكتاب} [البقرة: 2] هذا الكتاب "

TAB-FULL:v1p229/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r3.claim: Al-Suddī identifies ذلك الكتاب as this book.
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r3.anchor: عن السدي، في قوله: " {ذلك الكتاب} [البقرة: 2] قال: هذا الكتاب "

TAB-FULL:v1p229/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies ذلك الكتاب as this book.
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: " {ذلك الكتاب} [البقرة: 2] هذا الكتاب "

TAB-FULL:v1p229/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r5.claim: A completed or nearly completed report can be treated as present to the listener, so ذلك can point to something like هذا.
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r5.anchor: كل ما تقضى وقرب تقضيه من الأخبار فهو وإن صار بمعنى غير الحاضر، فكالحاضر عند المخاطب

TAB-FULL:v1p229/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r6.claim: Because alif-lām-mīm has just been explained, the demonstrative points to the book just described and explained to the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v1p229/r6.anchor: لما قدم قبل ذلك الكتاب {الم} [البقرة: 1] التي ذكرنا تصرفها في وجوهها من المعاني

TAB-FULL:v1p230/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p230/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p230/r1.claim: Some exegetes compare ذلك meaning هذا to ordinary dialogue and the verse’s use of هذا ذكر for what was just mentioned.
TAB-FULL:v1p230/r1.anchor: وكما قال جل ذكره: {واذكر إسماعيل واليسع وذا الكفل وكل من الأخيار هذا ذكر} [ص: 49]

TAB-FULL:v1p230/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p230/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p230/r2.claim: Some interpreters use Khafaf’s self-reference as ذلك while speaking of himself to support the sense “this.”
TAB-FULL:v1p230/r2.anchor: وجه معنى ذلك بعضهم إلى نظير معنى بيت خفاف بن ندبة السلمي

TAB-FULL:v1p230/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p230/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p230/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the first explanation, that ذلك points to the just-mentioned book, as the clearest sense of the exegetes’ view.
TAB-FULL:v1p230/r3.anchor: والقول الأول أولى بتأويل الكتاب لما ذكرنا من العلل

TAB-FULL:v1p230/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p230/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p230/r4.claim: Some say the demonstrative refers to the Torah and Gospel, making it a report about absent scriptures.
TAB-FULL:v1p230/r4.anchor: وقد قال بعضهم: {ذلك الكتاب} [البقرة: 2] يعني به التوراة والإنجيل

TAB-FULL:v1p232/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses لا ريب فيه as “there is no doubt in it.”
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {لا ريب فيه} [البقرة: 2] ، قال: لا شك فيه "

TAB-FULL:v1p232/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r2.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ glosses the phrase as “there is no doubt in it.”
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r2.anchor: عن عبد العزيز بن أبي رواد، عن عطاء: " {لا ريب فيه} [البقرة: 2] قال: لا شك فيه "

TAB-FULL:v1p232/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r3.speaker: السدي، أبو مالك، أبو صالح، ابن عباس، مرة الهمداني، ابن مسعود، وناس من أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r3.claim: The report transmitted from al-Suddī and these authorities glosses the phrase as “no doubt in it.”
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r3.anchor: عن السدي، في خبر ذكره عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة الهمداني، عن ابن مسعود

TAB-FULL:v1p232/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿIkrima or Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, says the book has no doubt.
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة أو عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: " {لا ريب فيه} [البقرة: 2] قال: لا شك فيه "

TAB-FULL:v1p232/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r5.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbās gives the same gloss: no doubt in it.
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قال ابن عباس: " {لا ريب فيه} [البقرة: 2] يقول لا شك فيه "

TAB-FULL:v1p232/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r6.claim: Qatāda glosses the phrase as “no doubt in it.”
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r6.anchor: أخبرنا معمر، عن قتادة: " {لا ريب فيه} [البقرة: 2] يقول: لا شك فيه "

TAB-FULL:v1p232/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r7.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas gives the same gloss: no doubt in it.
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r7.anchor: حدثنا عبد الله بن أبي جعفر، عن أبيه، عن الربيع بن أنس، قوله: " {لا ريب فيه} [البقرة: 2] يقول: لا شك فيه "

TAB-FULL:v1p232/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r8.claim: رَيْب is a verbal noun from رابني الشيء; Saʿida ibn Juʾayya’s verse uses it to mean doubt.
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r8.anchor: ومن ذلك قول ساعدة بن جؤية الهذلي. [البحر الطويل] فقالوا تركنا الحي قد حصروا به … فلا ريب أن قد كان ثم لحيم

TAB-FULL:v1p232/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r9.claim: The pronoun in فيه refers back to the book: there is no doubt that this book is guidance from God.
TAB-FULL:v1p232/r9.anchor: والهاء التي في فيه. عائدة على الكتاب، كأنه قال: لا شك في ذلك الكتاب أنه من عند الله هدى للمتقين

TAB-FULL:v1p234/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r1.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r1.claim: Al-Shaʿbī glosses guidance as guidance away from error.
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r1.anchor: عن بيان، عن الشعبي: " {هدى} [البقرة: 2] قال، هدى من الضلالة "

TAB-FULL:v1p234/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r2.speaker: السدي، أبو مالك، أبو صالح، ابن عباس، مرة الهمداني، ابن مسعود، وناس من أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r2.claim: The report transmitted from al-Suddī and these authorities calls it light for the God-fearing.
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r2.anchor: عن إسماعيل السدي، في خبر ذكره، عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة الهمداني، عن ابن مسعود

TAB-FULL:v1p234/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī treats hudā as a verbal noun from guiding someone along and showing the way.
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r3.anchor: والهدى في هذا الموضع مصدر من قولك هديت فلانا الطريق إذا أرشدته إليه. ودللته عليه

TAB-FULL:v1p234/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r4.claim: The Qurʾān guides the God-fearing, heals believers’ hearts, and becomes a burden, blindness, and proof against deniers; it guides believers and establishes the unbeliever’s case against him.
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r4.anchor: ولكنه هدى للمتقين، وشفاء لما في صدور المؤمنين، ووقر في آذان المكذيين، وعمى لأبصار الجاحدين

TAB-FULL:v1p234/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r5.claim: One accusative parse makes هدى an adjectival cut from the definite الكتاب, yielding “the book as guidance for the God-fearing.”
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r5.anchor: أن يكون نصبا لمعنى القطع من الكتاب لأنه نكرة والكتاب معرفة

TAB-FULL:v1p234/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r6.claim: Another accusative parse makes هدى a cut from the antecedent of the pronoun in فيه, meaning “with no doubt in it, as guidance.”
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r6.anchor: على القطع من راجع ذكر الكتاب الذي في فيه

TAB-FULL:v1p234/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r7.claim: If alif-lām-mīm is a complete utterance, هدى may be accusative as a cut from either الكتاب or the pronoun in فيه.
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r7.anchor: على أن الم كلام تام، كما قال ابن عباس إن معناه: أنا الله أعلم

TAB-FULL:v1p234/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited as reading the opening letters as “I am God; I know.”
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r8.anchor: كما قال ابن عباس إن معناه: أنا الله أعلم

TAB-FULL:v1p234/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r9.claim: In the nominative, one possibility is standalone praise, as in the nominative reading of رحمة in Luqmān 31:2.
TAB-FULL:v1p234/r9.anchor: أن يرفع حينئذ هدى بمعنى المدح كما قال الله جل وعز: {الم تلك آيات الكتاب الحكيم هدى ورحمة للمحسنين} [لقمان: 2]

TAB-FULL:v1p236/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r1.claim: With alif-lām-mīm complete, nominative هدى can stand as praise, or be raised by ذلك with الكتاب adjectival to it.
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r1.anchor: مدح مستأنف. والآخر: على أن يجعل الرافع ذلك، والكتاب نعت لذلك

TAB-FULL:v1p236/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r2.claim: A third nominative parse makes هدى follow the syntactic position of لا ريب فيه, with ذلك raised by the pronoun in فيه; compare Anʿām 6:92.
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r2.anchor: أن يجعل تابعا لموضع {لا ريب فيه} [البقرة: 2] ويكون {ذلك الكتاب} [البقرة: 2] مرفوعا بالعائد في فيه

TAB-FULL:v1p236/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r3.speaker: بعض المتقدمين في العلم بالعربية من الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r3.claim: A Kufan grammarian says alif-lām-mīm raises ذلك الكتاب and proposes nominative and accusative parses for هدى.
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r3.anchor: زعم بعض المتقدمين في العلم بالعربية من الكوفيين أن الم رافع {ذلك الكتاب} [البقرة: 2]

TAB-FULL:v1p236/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the Kufan grammarian abandons his own premise: if alif-lām-mīm raises ذلك الكتاب, only standalone praise licenses nominative هدى.
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r4.anchor: فترك الأصل الذي أصله في الم وأنها مرفوعة ب {ذلك الكتاب} [البقرة: 2] ونبذه وراء ظهره

TAB-FULL:v1p236/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r5.claim: On that premise, هدى cannot be a predicate of ذلك or follow the position of لا ريب فيه, since the preceding predicate is complete and its position is accusative.
TAB-FULL:v1p236/r5.anchor: وذلك أن الم إذا رفعت {ذلك الكتاب} [البقرة: 2] فلا شك أن هدى غير جائز حينئذ أن يكون خبرا لذلك

TAB-FULL:v1p239/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the God-fearing avoid what God prohibited and fulfill what He obligated.
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r1.anchor: عن سفيان، عن رجل، عن الحسن، قوله: " {للمتقين} [البقرة: 2] قال: اتقوا ما حرم عليهم وأدوا ما افترض عليهم "

TAB-FULL:v1p239/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes them as fearing punishment for abandoning known guidance and hoping for mercy by affirming the revelation.
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة أو عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: " {للمتقين} [البقرة: 2] أي الذين يحذرون من الله عز وجل عقوبته

TAB-FULL:v1p239/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r3.speaker: السدي، أبو مالك، أبو صالح، ابن عباس، مرة الهمداني، ابن مسعود، وناس من أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r3.claim: The report attributed to al-Suddī and these authorities identifies the God-fearing as believers.
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r3.anchor: عن السدي، في خبر ذكره عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة الهمداني، عن ابن مسعود

TAB-FULL:v1p239/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r4.speaker: الكلبي
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī says the God-fearing are those who avoid major sins.

TAB-FULL:v1p239/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r5.speaker: الأعمش
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r5.claim: Al-Aʿmash accepts al-Kalbī’s definition as sound and does not reject it.
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r5.anchor: قال: نرى أنه كذلك ولم ينكره

TAB-FULL:v1p239/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r6.claim: Qatāda says the following verse describes the God-fearing: those who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and give from their provision.
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r6.anchor: عن قتادة: " {هدى للمتقين} [البقرة: 2] هم من نعتهم ووصفهم فأثبت صفتهم فقال: {الذين يؤمنون بالغيب

TAB-FULL:v1p239/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r7.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in al-Ḍaḥḥāk’s report, says they avoid associating partners with God and obey Him.
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: " {للمتقين} [البقرة: 2] قال: المؤمنين الذين يتقون الشرك ويعملون بطاعتي "

TAB-FULL:v1p239/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the general sense: they avoid what God forbids and obey Him in what He obligates, rather than restricting taqwā to one aspect.
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r8.anchor: الذين اتقوا الله تبارك وتعالى في ركوب ما نهاهم عن ركوبه، فتجنبوا معاصيه واتقوه فيما أمرهم به من فرائضه

TAB-FULL:v1p239/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r9.claim: He rejects limiting the term to avoiding shirk and disavowing hypocrisy, since a person could do that yet commit sins and fail to merit the description.
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r9.anchor: فساد قول من زعم أن تأويل ذلك إنما هو: الذين اتقوا الشرك وبرءوا من النفاق؛ لأنه قد يكون كذلك وهو فاسق

TAB-FULL:v1p239/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r10.claim: The narrow interpretation can still fit if its proponents use hypocrisy to include grave sins and neglect of obligations, which some scholars called hypocrisy.
TAB-FULL:v1p239/r10.anchor: إلا أن يكون عند قائل هذا القول معنى النفاق ركوب الفواحش التي حرمها الله جل ثناؤه وتضييع فرائضه

TAB-FULL:v2p75/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p75/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p75/r1.claim: The God-fearing are those who fulfill God's obligations and avoid His prohibitions.
TAB-FULL:v2p75/r1.anchor: للمؤمنين الذين يتقون الشرك. ويعملون بطاعتي

TABATABAI:2:2-3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:2-3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:2-3/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī defers discussion of the disjoint letters and the meanings of Quranic guidance and Book until the opening of Sūrat al-Shūrā.
TABATABAI:2:2-3/r1.anchor: سيأتي بعض ما يتعلق من الكلام بالحروف المقطعة التي في أوائل السور، في أول سورة الشورى إن شاء الله، وكذلك الكلام في معنى هداية القرآن ومعنى كونه كتابا

TABATABAI:2:2-3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:2-3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:2-3/r2.claim: Though revealed piecemeal, the sūra has an overarching purpose: affirm all revelation and messengers without discrimination, rebuke religious division, then move to legal rulings.
TABATABAI:2:2-3/r2.anchor: وهو بيان أن من حق عبادة الله سبحانه أن يؤمن عبده بكل ما أنزله بلسان رسله من غير تفرقة بين وحي ووحي

TABATABAI:2:2-3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:2-3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:2-3/r3.claim: The muttaqūn are believers, and taqwā accompanies every realized level of faith rather than naming a special rank such as excellence, humility, or sincerity.
TABATABAI:2:2-3/r3.anchor: المتقون هم المؤمنون، وليست التقوى من الأوصاف الخاصة لطبقة من طبقاتهم

TABATABAI:2:2-3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:2-3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:2-3/r5.claim: The believers are surrounded by two guidances: prior guidance makes them pious, and Quranic guidance is bestowed on them afterward.
TABATABAI:2:2-3/r5.anchor: فعلمنا بذلك أن الهداية غير الهداية، وأن هؤلاء وهم متقون محفوفون بهدايتين

TABATABAI:2:1-5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:1-5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:1-5/r1.claim: Believers and disbelievers each pass through two stages: initial guidance or misguidance, followed by its reinforcement; the verses attribute the first states to people and the later seal or increase to God.
TABATABAI:2:1-5/r1.anchor: فنسب الختم إلى نفسه تعالى والغشاوة إلى أنفسهم، وكما يقوله في حق المنافقين في قلوبهم مرض فزادهم الله مرضا

TABATABAI:2:1-5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:1-5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:1-5/r2.claim: The first guidance precedes Quranic guidance and comes from sound innate disposition, which awakens people to their dependence on an external source.
TABATABAI:2:1-5/r2.anchor: فالهداية الأولى قبل القرآن وبسبب سلامة الفطرة، فإن الفطرة إذا سلمت لم تنفك من أن تتنبه شاهدة لفقرها وحاجتها إلى أمر خارج عنها

TABATABAI:2:1-5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:1-5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:1-5/r6.claim: He supports the dependence of later guidance on prior guidance with the verse promising that God makes believers steadfast in this life and the next.
TABATABAI:2:1-5/r6.anchor: يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة

TABRISI:2:2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
TABRISI:2:2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr links the written hāʾ to a following yāʾ in pronunciation here, and applies this to written hāʾ preceded by a quiescent yāʾ.
TABRISI:2:2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير فيهي هدى بوصل الهاء بياء في اللفظ وكذلك كل هاء كتابية قبلها ياء ساكنة

TABRISI:2:2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2/r2.speaker: حفص وقتيبة
TABRISI:2:2/r2.claim: Ḥafṣ shares the lengthened hāʾ in فِيهِ مَهَانًا; Qutayba does so in فَمُلَاقِيهِ and وَسَأُصْلِيهِ.
TABRISI:2:2/r2.anchor: ووافقه حفص في قوله فيهي مهانا وقتيبة في قوله فملاقيه وسأصليه

TABRISI:2:2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2/r3.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:2:2/r3.claim: The remaining readers do not lengthen hāʾ; all readers lengthen it when the preceding letter is vowelled.
TABRISI:2:2/r3.anchor: والباقون لا يشبعون وإذا تحرك ما قبل الهاء فهم مجمعون على إشباعه

TABRISI:2:2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2/r4.claim: Arabic permits four forms. Kasra matches a preceding yāʾ or kasra because hāʾ is as hidden as alif, like imāla; those declining length avoid similar sounds, while lengtheners count hāʾ as a consonantal barrier.
TABRISI:2:2/r4.anchor: اعلم أنه يجوز في العربية في فيه أربعة أوجه فيهو وفيهي وفيه وفيه

TABRISI:2:2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2/r5.claim: ذٰلك points to what is distant and هذا to what is near; its base is ذا, with a noninflecting address kāf and emphatic lām.
TABRISI:2:2/r5.anchor: ذلك لفظة يشار بها إلى ما بعد وهذا: إلى ما قرب والاسم من ذلك ذا والكاف زيدت للخطاب

TABRISI:2:2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2/r6.claim: The address kāf has no inflectional role; the lām adds emphasis and takes kasra at a meeting of two quiescent letters. Forms include ذاك, وذلك, and هذاك, but not هذا لك.
TABRISI:2:2/r6.anchor: والكاف زيدت للخطاب ولاحظ لها من الإعراب واللام تزاد للتأكيد وكسرت لالتقاء الساكنين

TABRISI:2:2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2/r7.claim: كتاب is a verbal noun used for “the written thing,” like حساب.
TABRISI:2:2/r7.anchor: والكتاب مصدر وهو بمعنى المكتوب كالحساب

TABRISI:2:2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2/r8.claim: An unnamed poet uses كتابها for a written document, confirming the sense “written thing.”

TABRISI:2:2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2/r9.claim: The root evokes joining: sewing a waterskin, joining a mule’s lips with a ring, and a gathered troop called كتيبة.
TABRISI:2:2/r9.anchor: وأصله الجمع من قولهم كتبت القربة إذا خرزتها والكتبة الخرزة

TABRISI:2:2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2/r10.claim: ريب means doubt, especially severe doubt; رابني implies certainty of suspicion, unlike أرابني, and أراب can mean becoming suspect.
TABRISI:2:2/r10.anchor: والريب الشك وقيل هو أسوأ الشك وهو مصدر رابني الشيء من فلان يريبني

TABRISI:2:2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2/r11.claim: هدى means guidance or direction, and is a rare verbal noun on the pattern فعل.
TABRISI:2:2/r11.anchor: والهدى الدلالة مصدر هديته وفعل قليل في المصادر

TABRISI:2:2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2/r12.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:2:2/r12.claim: Abū ʿAlī allows فعل as a verbal noun particular to defective verbs, unlike sound verbs, comparing it to كينونة.
TABRISI:2:2/r12.anchor: قال أبو علي: يجوز أن يكون فعل مصدر اختص به المعتل

TABRISI:2:2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2/r13.claim: The verb هدى takes its second object with إلى or لام; the preposition may be omitted so it directly takes the object.
TABRISI:2:2/r13.anchor: والفعل منه يتعدى إلى مفعولين يتعدى إلى الثاني منهما بأحد حرفي جر إلى أو اللام

TABRISI:2:2#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2#2/r1.claim: The cited guidance toward the paths of peace is read as guidance toward the paths of the abode of peace.
TABRISI:2:2#2/r1.anchor: وكأنه استنجاز لما وعدوا به في قوله

TABRISI:2:2#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2#2/r2.claim: Omitting the preposition makes “guide us the path” mean “guide us to it and lead us along it.”
TABRISI:2:2#2/r2.anchor: وقد يحذف منه حرف الجر فيصل الفعل إلى المفعول نحو:

TABRISI:2:2#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2#2/r3.claim: متقين derives from وقاية: the initial wāw became tāʾ and assimilated; kasra was dropped. تقوى derives from وقى, with wāw changed to tāʾ.
TABRISI:2:2#2/r3.anchor: والأصل في المتقين الموتقين مفتعلين من الوقاية فقبلت الواو تاء

TABRISI:2:2#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2#2/r4.claim: The root idea of taqwā is making a barrier between two things, as with a shield.
TABRISI:2:2#2/r4.anchor: وأصل الاتقاء الحجز بين الشيئين يقال: أتقاه بالترس

TABRISI:2:2#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2#2/r5.claim: He lists six parses: predicate of ألم; subject with الكتاب predicate; subject with الكتاب appositive, adjective, or substitute; subject with هدى and لا ريب circumstantial; compound predicate; or predicate of an omitted هذا.
TABRISI:2:2#2/r5.anchor: ذلك في موضع رفع من وجوه: أحدها: أن تجعله خبرا عن ألم

TABRISI:2:2#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2#2/r6.claim: Under some parses, هدى is accusative as a circumstantial “guiding,” governed by the demonstrative or the locative construction.
TABRISI:2:2#2/r6.anchor: كان قوله هدى في موضع نصب على الحال أي هاديا للمتقين

TABRISI:2:2#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#2/r7.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:2:2#2/r7.claim: Sībawayh says لا governs the following noun, making it accusative without nunation.
TABRISI:2:2#2/r7.anchor: قال سيبويه: لا تعمل فيما بعدها فتنصبه بغير تنوين

TABRISI:2:2#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#2/r8.speaker: غيره من حذاق النحويين
TABRISI:2:2#2/r8.claim: Other expert grammarians treat لا plus a common indefinite noun as a compound, more emphatic than a particle-like meaning; فيه can be predicate or adjective.
TABRISI:2:2#2/r8.anchor: وقال غيره من حذاق النحويين: جعل لا مع النكرة الشائعة مركبا فهو أوكد

TABRISI:2:2#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2#2/r9.claim: He gives three nominative parses for هدى: subject with an omitted predicate after فيه; predicate of ألم if it names the sūra; or predicate of an omitted subject, هو.
TABRISI:2:2#2/r9.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع من ثلاثة أوجه غير الوجه

TABRISI:2:2#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#3/r1.speaker: الأخفش
TABRISI:2:2#3/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash identifies the Book as the Qurʾān and takes ذلك as “this,” since the Book was present; he cites Khuffāf ibn Nudba’s line using ذلك of its speaker.
TABRISI:2:2#3/r1.anchor: وقال الأخفش ذلك بمعنى هذا لأن الكتاب كان حاضرا وأنشد لخفاف بن ندبة

TABRISI:2:2#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2#3/r2.claim: A demonstrative can describe something just mentioned; هذا sounds near when reported, while ذلك can mark the past, as in “three and three, so this/that is six.”
TABRISI:2:2#3/r2.anchor: وإذا جرى للشيء ذكر يجوز أن يقول السامع هذا كما قلت وذلك كما قلت

TABRISI:2:2#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2#3/r3.claim: The cited line may also be literal: the speaker is “that man” whose courage people have heard about.
TABRISI:2:2#3/r3.anchor: أقول له والرمح يأطر متنه تأمل خفافا إنني أنا ذلكا

TABRISI:2:2#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#3/r4.speaker: الفراء وأبو علي الجبائي
TABRISI:2:2#3/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī say God promised the Prophet a book water could not erase and repeated recitation could not wear out; the Qurʾān fulfills it.
TABRISI:2:2#3/r4.anchor: لا يخلق على كثرة الرد فلما أنزل القرآن قال هذا القرآن ذلك الكتاب الذي وعدتك عن الفراء وأبي علي الجبائي

TABRISI:2:2#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#3/r5.speaker: المبرد
TABRISI:2:2#3/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad says this Qurʾān is the book promised to the Prophet in earlier scriptures.
TABRISI:2:2#3/r5.anchor: هذا القرآن ذلك الكتاب الذي وعدتك به في الكتب السالفة عن المبرد

TABRISI:2:2#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2#3/r6.claim: He rejects identifying the Book as the Torah and Gospel: this verse calls it doubt-free guidance, while the Qurʾān says their scriptures were altered.
TABRISI:2:2#3/r6.anchor: ومن قال إن المراد بالكتاب التوراة والإنجيل فقوله فاسد لأنه وصف الكتاب بأنه لا ريب فيه

TABRISI:2:2#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2#3/r7.claim: “No doubt in it” means the Qurʾān is clarification, guidance, truth, and a miracle, deserving the description beyond doubt.
TABRISI:2:2#3/r7.anchor: ومعنى قوله لا ريب فيه أي أنه بيان وهدى وحق ومعجز

TABRISI:2:2#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#3/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:2#3/r8.claim: An ellipsis means there is no cause for doubt: ambiguity, obscurity, contradiction, and claims without proof are absent from God’s Book.
TABRISI:2:2#3/r8.anchor: وقيل إنه على الحذف كأنه قال لا سبب شك فيه لأن الأسباب التي توجب الشك في الكلام

TABRISI:2:2#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#3/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:2#3/r9.claim: Another reading treats the statement, phrased as a report, as a prohibition: “Do not doubt it,” like لا رفث ولا فسوق.
TABRISI:2:2#3/r9.anchor: وقيل إن معناه النهي وإن كان لفظه الخبر أي لا ترتابوا أو لا تشكوا فيه

TABRISI:2:2#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#3/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2#3/r10.claim: The Qurʾān is specially called guidance for the God-fearing because they benefit and follow it; this does not deny that it guides everyone.
TABRISI:2:2#3/r10.anchor: وأما تخصيص المتقين بأن القرآن هدى لهم وإن كان هدى لجميع الناس فلأنهم هم الذين انتفعوا به

TABRISI:2:2#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:2#4/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī completes the Prophetic report introduced at the end of the preceding segment: taqwā is gathered in God’s command to justice and excellence.
TABRISI:2:2#4/r1.anchor: جماع التقوى في قوله تعالى: { إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان }

TABRISI:2:2#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#4/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:2#4/r2.claim: A muttaqī avoids what God forbids and performs what He makes obligatory.
TABRISI:2:2#4/r2.anchor: وقيل: المتقي الذي اتقى ما حرم عليه وفعل ما أوجب عليه

TABRISI:2:2#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#4/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:2#4/r3.claim: A muttaqī uses righteous deeds to protect himself from God’s punishment.
TABRISI:2:2#4/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي يتقي بصالح أعماله عذاب الله

TABRISI:2:2#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#4/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وكعب الأحبار
TABRISI:2:2#4/r4.claim: Asked by ʿUmar about taqwā, Kaʿb al-Aḥbār compares it to crossing a thorny path cautiously and alertly; ʿUmar agrees this is taqwā.
TABRISI:2:2#4/r4.anchor: وسأل عمر بن الخطاب كعب الأحبار عن التقوى فقال: هل أخذت طريقا ذا شوك

TABRISI:2:2#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#4/r5.speaker: بعض الناس
TABRISI:2:2#4/r5.claim: A poem defines taqwā as abandoning every sin, large or small, and carefully crossing thorn-covered ground without dismissing small sins.
TABRISI:2:2#4/r5.anchor: ونظمه بعض الناس فقال: خل الذنوب صغيرها وكبيرها فهو التقى

TABRISI:2:2#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#4/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:2:2#4/r6.claim: The Prophet is reported to explain that the God-fearing leave even harmless things lest they fall into something harmful.
TABRISI:2:2#4/r6.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

TABRISI:2:2#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#4/r7.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
TABRISI:2:2#4/r7.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz likens the God-fearing person to someone restrained, like a criminal in the sanctuary.
TABRISI:2:2#4/r7.anchor: وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز: التقي ملجم كالمجرم في الحرم

TABRISI:2:2#4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:2#4/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TABRISI:2:2#4/r8.claim: Another definition: taqwā means God does not find you where He forbade you or miss you where He commanded you.
TABRISI:2:2#4/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم: التقوى أن لا يراك الله حيث نهاك ولا يفقدك حيث أمرك

THALABI:v1p139/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p139/r12.speaker: أبو عمرو
THALABI:v1p139/r12.claim: The general readers pronounce Dhalika with an open dhal; Abu Amr also permits imala in the dhal of hadhihi.
THALABI:v1p139/r12.anchor: ذلك: قرأت العامة ذلك بفتح الذال، وكذلك هذه وهاتان، وأجاز أبو عمرو الإمالة في هذه

THALABI:v1p139/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p139/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p139/r13.claim: In Dhalika, dhal is the noun, lam is a support element, and kaf marks address; the demonstrative points to something absent.
THALABI:v1p139/r13.anchor: (ذ) للاسم، واللام عماد، والكاف خطاب، وهو إشارة إلى الغائب

THALABI:v1p140/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p140/r1.claim: Al-kitab means the written object, as in the words hisab and imad; the poet's reference to a page that has come to the addressee with its writing illustrates this usage.
THALABI:v1p140/r1.anchor: والكتاب: بمعنى المكتوب كالحساب والعماد. قال الشاعر: بشرت عيالي إذ رأيت صحيفة

THALABI:v1p140/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p140/r2.claim: The noun kitab derives from joining letters together; the root also describes sewing beads into two parts, and the cited verse uses al-katb for the stitching.
THALABI:v1p140/r2.anchor: وأصله من الكتب، وهو ضم الحروف بعضها إلى بعض، مأخوذ من قولهم: كتب الخرز

THALABI:v1p140/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r3.speaker: ذو المرجة
THALABI:v1p140/r3.claim: Dhu al-Marja's line uses al-katb to mean the joining or stitching between parts of a garment.
THALABI:v1p140/r3.anchor: قال ذو المرجة: وفراء غرفية أثاي خوارزها … مشلشل ضيعته فبينها الكتب

THALABI:v1p140/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p140/r4.claim: The author also notes that kataba can mean marking or branding a mule, and that a troop is called a katiba, plural kataib.
THALABI:v1p140/r4.anchor: ويقال: كتبت البغل، إذا حرمت من سفرتها الخلقة، ومنه قيل للجند كتيبة، وجمعها كتائب

THALABI:v1p140/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p140/r5.claim: A poet's line about a katiba provides usage evidence for the word meaning troop.
THALABI:v1p140/r5.anchor: وكتيبة جاءوا ترفل … في الحديد لها ذخر

THALABI:v1p140/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r6.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك ومقاتل
THALABI:v1p140/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil say the book is the Quran; on this view Dhalika means this, as in the cited demonstrative about Abraham's proof.
THALABI:v1p140/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك ومقاتل: هو القرآن، وعلى هذا القول يكون (ذلك) بمعنى (هذا)

THALABI:v1p140/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p140/r7.claim: Khaffaf ibn Nudba's line uses dhalika in the sense of hadha, this.
THALABI:v1p140/r7.anchor: أقول له الرمح يأطر متنه … تأمل خفافا إنني أنا ذالكا

THALABI:v1p140/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p140/r8.claim: Abu al-Duha transmits Ibn Abbas's view that this is the book God had told the Prophet He would send him.
THALABI:v1p140/r8.anchor: وروى أبو الضحى عن ابن عباس قال: معناه ذلك الكتاب الذي أخبرتك أن أوجه إليك

THALABI:v1p140/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r9.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
THALABI:v1p140/r9.claim: Ata ibn al-Sa'ib says it is the book promised to the people on the covenant day.
THALABI:v1p140/r9.anchor: وقال عطاء بن السائب: ذلك الكتاب الذي وعدتكم يوم الميثاق

THALABI:v1p140/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r10.speaker: يمان بن رئاب
THALABI:v1p140/r10.claim: Yaman ibn Ri'ab says it is the book mentioned in the Torah and Gospel.
THALABI:v1p140/r10.anchor: وقال يمان بن رئاب: ذلك الكتاب الذي ذكرته في التوراة والإنجيل

THALABI:v1p140/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v1p140/r11.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr identifies the book as the Preserved Tablet.
THALABI:v1p140/r11.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هو اللوح المحفوظ

THALABI:v1p140/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r12.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v1p140/r12.claim: Ikrima says the book means the Torah, Gospel, and earlier scriptures.
THALABI:v1p140/r12.anchor: عكرمة: هو التوراة والإنجيل والكتب المتقدمة

THALABI:v1p140/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r13.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v1p140/r13.claim: Al-Farra says God had promised the Prophet a book that water would not erase and repeated recitation would not wear out; when the Quran came, God identified it as the promised book.
THALABI:v1p140/r13.anchor: وقال الفراء: إن الله تعالى وعد نبيه أن ينزل عليه كتابا لا يمحوه الماء ولا يخلق على كثرة الرد

THALABI:v1p140/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r14.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v1p140/r14.claim: Ibn Kaysan takes the book to mean the Quranic material before al-Baqara, since the disbelievers had rejected the dozen or so suras revealed before it.
THALABI:v1p140/r14.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: تأويله أن الله تعالى أنزل قبل البقرة بضع عشرة سورة كذب بكلها المشركون

THALABI:v1p140/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p140/r15.claim: Another reported view identifies the book as the one denied by the Jewish figure Malik ibn al-Sayf.
THALABI:v1p140/r15.anchor: وقيل: ذلك الكتاب الذي كذب به مالك بن الصيف اليهودي

THALABI:v1p140/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p140/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p140/r16.claim: La rayba fihi means there is no doubt that the Quran comes from God.
THALABI:v1p140/r16.anchor: لا ريب فيه: لا شك فيه، إنه من عند الله

THALABI:v1p142/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p142/r1.claim: Huda is a predicate, understood as huwa hudan, and the sentence ends at fihi; alternatively it is an accusative circumstantial, meaning the book guides the God-fearing and has no doubt in its guidance to them.
THALABI:v1p142/r1.anchor: قال: هدى: أي هو هدى، وتم الكلام عند قوله فيه، وقيل: «هو» نصب على الحال

THALABI:v1p142/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v1p142/r2.claim: The specialists in meaning say the phrase is outwardly a negation but inwardly a prohibition: do not doubt the guidance and clarification by which a person is guided and sees clearly, like negations that prohibit during pilgrimage.
THALABI:v1p142/r2.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: ظاهره نفي وباطنه نهي، أي لا ترتابوا فيه، كقوله تعالى: فلا رفث ولا فسوق ولا جدال

THALABI:v1p142#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p142#2/r1.claim: Taqwa derives from waqa, with initial waw changed to ta, as in taklan from waklan and takhma from wakhma.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أن التقوى أصله وقى من وقيت، فجعلت الواو تاء، كالتكلان فأصله وكلان

THALABI:v1p142#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v1p142#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says the comprehensive definition of taqwa is found in God's command to justice and excellence.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «جماع التقوى في قول الله تعالى: إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان ... الآية»

THALABI:v1p142#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p142#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas defines the God-fearing as those who avoid associating partners with God, major sins, and sexual indecencies.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: المتقي الذي يتقي الشرك والكبائر والفواحش

THALABI:v1p142#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v1p142#2/r4.claim: Ibn Umar says piety means not seeing oneself as better than anyone else.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: التقوى أن لا يرى [نفسه] خيرا من أحد

THALABI:v1p142#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v1p142#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the God-fearing person considers everyone he sees better than himself.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: المتقي الذي يقول لكل من رآه هذا خير مني

THALABI:v1p142#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r6.speaker: كعب الأحبار
THALABI:v1p142#2/r6.claim: Ka'b explains piety through Umar's image of carefully traversing a thorny path; Ibn al-Mu'tazz's poem extends it to avoiding both small and great sins.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r6.anchor: وقال عمر بن الخطاب لكعب الأحبار: حدثني عن التقوى، فقال: هل أخذت طريقا ذا شوك

THALABI:v1p142#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r7.speaker: ابن المعتز
THALABI:v1p142#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Mu'tazz's poem says piety means leaving small and great sins, treading carefully over thorns, and not belittling small wrongs because mountains are made of pebbles.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r7.anchor: ونظمه ابن المعتز فقال: خل الذنوب صغيرها … وكبيرها ذاك التقى واضع كماش فوق أر … ض الشوك يحذر ما يرى

THALABI:v1p142#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r8.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
THALABI:v1p142#2/r8.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz says piety is not merely daytime and nighttime worship; it is avoiding what God forbids and doing what He requires, with further provision being added goodness.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r8.anchor: وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز: ليس التقوى قيام النهار وقيام الليل والتخليط فيما بين ذلك، ولكن التقوى ترك ما حرم الله

THALABI:v1p142#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r9.speaker: طلق بن حبيب
THALABI:v1p142#2/r9.claim: Taliq ibn Habib defines piety as acting in God's light while hoping for reward and leaving disobedience in God's light while fearing punishment.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r9.anchor: وقيل لطلق بن حبيب: أجمل لنا التقوى؟ فقال: التقوى عمل يطلبه الله على نور من الله رجاء ثواب الله

THALABI:v1p142#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r10.speaker: بكر بن عبد الله
THALABI:v1p142#2/r10.claim: Bakr ibn Abd Allah says a person is not pious until he guards against greed and anger.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r10.anchor: وقال بكر بن عبد الله: لا يكون الرجل تقيا حتى يكون يتقي الطمع، ويتقي الغضب

THALABI:v1p142#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r11.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
THALABI:v1p142#2/r11.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz describes the muttaqi as someone mindful of what is forbidden, meaning within the sanctuary.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r11.anchor: وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز: المتقي لمحرم لا تحرم، يعني في الحرم

THALABI:v1p142#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r12.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
THALABI:v1p142#2/r12.claim: Shahr ibn Hawshab says the pious person leaves what he cannot trust, wary of what may bring harm.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r12.anchor: وقال شهر بن حوشب: المتقي الذي يترك ما لا يأتمن به حذرا لما به بأس

THALABI:v1p142#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r13.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v1p142#2/r13.claim: A report from the Prophet explains the name muttaqun by their leaving what is harmless lest they fall into what is harmful.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r13.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: إنما سمي المتقون؟ لتركهم ما لا بأس به

THALABI:v1p142#2/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r14.speaker: سفيان الثوري والفضيل
THALABI:v1p142#2/r14.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri and al-Fudayl define piety as loving for others what one loves for oneself.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r14.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري والفضيل: هو الذي يحب للناس ما يحب لنفسه

THALABI:v1p142#2/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p142#2/r15.speaker: الجنيد بن محمد
THALABI:v1p142#2/r15.claim: Junayd ibn Muhammad goes further than Sufyan and al-Fudayl: the pious person loves for others more than he loves for himself; he illustrates this with al-Sari's concern that another receive most of the mercy for returning a greeting.
THALABI:v1p142#2/r15.anchor: وقال الجنيد بن محمد: ليس المتقي الذي يحب الناس ما يحب لنفسه، إنما المتقي الذي يحب للناس أكثر مما يحب لنفسه

THALABI:v1p143/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r1.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
THALABI:v1p143/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tirmidhi defines the pious person as one who has no adversary.
THALABI:v1p143/r1.anchor: محمد بن علي الترمذي: هو الذي لا خصم له

THALABI:v1p143/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r2.speaker: السري بن المفلس
THALABI:v1p143/r2.claim: Al-Sari ibn al-Mufallis says the pious person is one who dislikes himself.
THALABI:v1p143/r2.anchor: السري بن المفلس: هو الذي يبغض نفسه

THALABI:v1p143/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r3.speaker: الشبلي
THALABI:v1p143/r3.claim: Al-Shibli defines piety as seeking what is less than God.
THALABI:v1p143/r3.anchor: الشبلي: هو الذي يبغي ما دون الله

THALABI:v1p143/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r4.speaker: جعفر الصادق
THALABI:v1p143/r4.claim: Ja'far al-Sadiq cites Labid's verse, Every thing apart from God is false, as the Arabs' truest saying.
THALABI:v1p143/r4.anchor: قال جعفر الصادق: أصدق كلمة قالت العرب قول لبيد: ألا كل شيء ما خلا الله باطل

THALABI:v1p143/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r5.speaker: الثوري
THALABI:v1p143/r5.claim: Al-Thawri defines the pious person as one who avoids the world and its least share.
THALABI:v1p143/r5.anchor: الثوري: هو الذي اتقى الدنيا وأقلها

THALABI:v1p143/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r6.speaker: محمد بن يوسف المقري
THALABI:v1p143/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Muqri defines piety as avoiding everything that distances one from God.
THALABI:v1p143/r6.anchor: محمد بن يوسف المقري: مجانبة كل ما يبعدك عن الله

THALABI:v1p143/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r7.speaker: القاسم بن القاسم
THALABI:v1p143/r7.claim: Al-Qasim ibn al-Qasim defines piety as preserving the etiquette of the sacred law.
THALABI:v1p143/r7.anchor: القاسم بن القاسم: المحافظة على آداب الشريعة

THALABI:v1p143/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r8.speaker: أبو زيد
THALABI:v1p143/r8.claim: Abu Zayd defines piety as scrupulously avoiding all doubtful matters.
THALABI:v1p143/r8.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: هو التورع عن جميع الشبهات

THALABI:v1p143/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r9.speaker: أبو زيد
THALABI:v1p143/r9.claim: Abu Zayd also says the pious person speaks, is silent, and remembers only for God's sake.
THALABI:v1p143/r9.anchor: وقال أيضا: المتقي من إذا قال قال لله، وإذا سكت سكت لله، وإذا ذكر ذكر لله تعالى

THALABI:v1p143/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r10.speaker: الفضيل
THALABI:v1p143/r10.claim: Al-Fudayl says a servant is pious when even his enemy feels as safe with him as his friend does.
THALABI:v1p143/r10.anchor: الفضيل: يكون العبد من المتقين حتى يأمنه عدوه كما يأمنه صديقه

THALABI:v1p143/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r11.speaker: سهل
THALABI:v1p143/r11.claim: Sahl defines the pious person as one who disowns his own power and strength.
THALABI:v1p143/r11.anchor: وقال سهل: المتقي من تبرأ من حوله وقوته

THALABI:v1p143/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r12.speaker: سهل
THALABI:v1p143/r12.claim: Sahl also defines piety as not being found where God has forbidden and not being absent where He has commanded.
THALABI:v1p143/r12.anchor: وقال: التقوى أن لا يراك الله حيث نهاك، ولا يفقدك من حيث أمرك

THALABI:v1p143/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p143/r13.claim: Another definition is following the Prophet.
THALABI:v1p143/r13.anchor: وقيل: هو الاقتداء بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v1p143/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p143/r14.claim: Another account describes guarding the heart from heedlessness, the soul from desires, the throat from pleasures, and the limbs from sins, in hope of attaining God's reward.
THALABI:v1p143/r14.anchor: وقيل: هو أن تتقي بقلبك عن الغفلات، وبنفسك من الشهوات، وبحلقك من اللذات، وبجوارحك من السيئات

THALABI:v1p143/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r15.speaker: أبو القاسم الحكيم
THALABI:v1p143/r15.claim: Abu al-Qasim al-Hakim defines piety as good character.

THALABI:v1p143/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p143/r16.claim: One view identifies three signs of piety: trusting well concerning what one has not attained, being content with what one has attained, and patiently accepting what has passed.
THALABI:v1p143/r16.anchor: وقال بعضهم: يستدل على تقوى الرجل بثلاث: بحسن التوكل فيما لم ينل، وحسن الرضا فيما قد نال

THALABI:v1p143/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r17.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p143/r17.claim: Another definition is avoiding obedience to one's own desires.
THALABI:v1p143/r17.anchor: وقيل: المتقي من اتقى متابعة هواه

THALABI:v1p143/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r18.speaker: مالك
THALABI:v1p143/r18.claim: Malik transmits that Medinan jurists wrote to Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr listing patience during affliction, acceptance of God's decree, gratitude for blessings, and submission to Quranic judgments as signs of the pious.
THALABI:v1p143/r18.anchor: وقال مالك: حدثنا وهب بن كيسان أن بعض فقهاء أهل المدينة كتب إلى عبد الله بن الزبير أن لأهل التقى علامات يعرفون بها

THALABI:v1p143/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r19.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
THALABI:v1p143/r19.claim: Maymun ibn Mihran says a person is not pious until he scrutinizes himself more strictly than a miserly partner or unjust ruler would.
THALABI:v1p143/r19.anchor: وقال ميمون بن مهران: لا يكون الرجل تقيا حتى يكون أشد محاسبة لنفسه من الشريك الشحيح والسلطان الجائر

THALABI:v1p143/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r20.speaker: أبو تراب
THALABI:v1p143/r20.claim: Abu Turab lists five hurdles to piety: choosing austerity over ease, restraint over excess speech, humility over honor, exertion over comfort, and death over life.
THALABI:v1p143/r20.anchor: وقال أبو تراب: بين يدي التقوى عقبات، من لا يجاوزها لا ينالها، اختيار الشدة على النعمة

THALABI:v1p143/r21.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p143/r21.speaker: بعض الحكماء
THALABI:v1p143/r21.claim: Some sages say a person reaches the summit of piety only if he would feel no shame were his inner thoughts displayed in the marketplace.
THALABI:v1p143/r21.anchor: وقال بعض الحكماء: لا يبلغ الرجل سنام التقوى إلا إذا كان بحيث لو جعل ما في قلبه على طبق

THALABI:v1p144/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p144/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p144/r1.claim: One definition of piety is to make one's inner self as beautiful for God as one's public self is for other people.
THALABI:v1p144/r1.anchor: وقيل: التقوى أن تزين سرك للحق، كما تزين علانيتك للخلق

THALABI:v1p144/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p144/r2.speaker: أبو الدرداء
THALABI:v1p144/r2.claim: Abu al-Darda's poem contrasts human desire with God's will and says that piety is the best gain a person can acquire.
THALABI:v1p144/r2.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء: يريد المرء أن يعطى مناه … ويأبى الله إلا ما أرادا يقول المرء فائدتي وذخري

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p10/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p10/r8.speaker: من قال إنها أسماء للسور والقرآن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p10/r8.claim: On the same view, the letters may be a fronted predicate meaning the promised book is alif-lām-mīm.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p10/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون رفعا على أنه خبر مقدم، كأنه قال: ذلك الكتاب الذي وعدتك (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r1.speaker: أبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r1.claim: Abu al-Haytham says ذا is the demonstrative for something present to speaker and listener, while adding kāf marks distance.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r2.speaker: أبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r2.claim: The added kāf is not an inflectional case ending; a following lām was added to avert the mistaken impression that kāf was genitive.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r2.anchor: وهذه (الكاف) ليست في موضع نصب ولا خفض (¬3) ولا رفع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r3.speaker: أبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Haytham says ذا is indeclinable in all cases because its demonstrative reference supplies a particle-like meaning; grammarians agree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r3.anchor: و (ذا) مبني (¬6)، نصبه وخفضه ورفعه سواء، لأن فيه معنى الإشارة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the kasra on lām as resolving two adjacent sukūns; the Kufians do not discuss that kasra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج (¬2): كسرت (اللام) في (ذلك) لالتقاء الساكنين (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r5.speaker: أبو الفتح الموصلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r5.claim: Abu al-Fath al-Mawsili treats lām as a permanently attached extra letter, adducing ذاك، أولئك، هناك and other forms whose shorter counterparts share their meanings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو الفتح الموصلي (¬4): (اللام) قد تزاد في الكلمة مبنية (¬5) معها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r6.speaker: أبو الفتح الموصلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r6.claim: The kāf in ذاك، ذلك، تلك، تانك، ذانك, and أولئك is an address particle, not a noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r6.anchor: وأما (¬6) (الكاف) فهي في (ذاك)، و (ذلك)، و (تلك)، و (تانك) (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r7.speaker: أبو الفتح الموصلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r7.claim: The dual retains its nūn before kāf; if kāf were a noun in iḍāfa, nūn would drop and kāf would be genitive.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r7.anchor: والدليل (¬9) على ذلك ثبوت النون [في (ذانك، وتانك) ولو كانت اسما لوجب حذف النون] (¬10)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r8.claim: Arabic also adds kāf as an address particle, as in النجاءك; commands do not take the commanded person's pronoun as an object.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p26#2/r8.anchor: والعرب قد تزيد (الكاف) للخطاب كقولهم: (النجاءك) أي: انج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r1.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r1.claim: Ibn al-Anbari identifies the book as the revelation God had promised to send to Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r1.anchor: وهذان القولان (¬8) متقاربان، والأول (¬9) اختيار ابن الانباري

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r2.speaker: يمان بن رباب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r2.claim: Yaman ibn Rabab says this is the book mentioned in the Torah and Gospel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r2.anchor: وقال يمان بن رباب (¬4): ذلك (¬5) الكتاب الذي ذكرته في التوراة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari links the demonstrative to God's prior promise to reveal weighty words, which the later revelation recalled to the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r3.anchor: أما ابن الانباري فقال: إنما قال عز (¬3) ذكره: {ذلك الكتاب}، فأشار إلى غائب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says it is the Qur'an promised through Moses and Jesus.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: القرآن، ذلك الكتاب الذي وعدوا به على لسان موسى وعيسى (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، والحسن، وقتادة، ومجاهد، والضحاك، ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil identify the book as the Qur'an.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r5.anchor: والمراد بالكتاب هاهنا: القرآن في (¬8) قول ابن عباس، والحسن، وقتادة، ومجاهد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r6.claim: Here al-kitāb denotes the written object, as in calling what is created al-khalq, rather than the act of creating or originating.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r6.anchor: والمراد به المفعول (¬1)، كقولهم: الخلق، يريدون: المخلوق (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r7.claim: He prefers the broad sense of the written revelation over naming it for prescribed obligations, since not all revelation imposes duties.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r7.anchor: وهذا (¬3) أرجح عندي من قول من قال: إنه سمي به لما فرض فيه (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r8.claim: If alif-lām-mīm connects to what follows, it can be the subject with ذلك its predicate and الكتاب an explanation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r8.anchor: فإن جعلت {الم} متعلقا بما بعده، فهو ابتداء، وخبره] (¬7) {ذلك}، والكتاب تفسير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r9.claim: If alif-lām-mīm is separate, ذلك begins a clause whose predicate is هدى.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r9.anchor: وإن (¬1) جعلت {الم} منقطعا مما بعده، ف {ذلك} ابتداء، وخبره {هدى} (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p33/r10.claim: A further parse makes alif-lām-mīm one subject, ذلك another, الكتاب its predicate, and the whole clause predicate of the first.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r1.speaker: جمهور أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r1.claim: The majority of linguists distinguish rābanī, which indicates established suspicion, from arābanī, which raises suspicion without confirming it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r2.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r2.claim: Sibawayh says arāba means becoming a person of suspicion, like alāma meaning deserving blame; rābanī means making someone suspicious.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r2.anchor: وقال سيبويه: (أراب) الرجل أي: صار صاحب ريبة. كما قالوا: ألام أي: استحق أن يلام (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r3.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r3.claim: Abu Zayd distinguishes certainty of suspicion with rābanī from an unconfirmed suspicion with arābanī.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r3.anchor: وقال أبو زيد (¬5): قد رابني من فلان أمر رأيته منه ريبا، إذا كنت مستيقنا منه بالريبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r4.speaker: قوم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r4.claim: Some people treat rāba and arāba as synonymous, adducing a line by a Hudhali poet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r4.anchor: وقوم على أن: (راب) و (أراب) بمعنى واحد (¬7)، وينشدون قول الهذلي (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r5.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r5.claim: Al-Azhari sides with the expert distinction and Abu Zayd's account of rāba versus arāba.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r5.anchor: والحذاق (¬2) على الفرق بينهما، كما أخبرتك، قال الأزهري: والقول في (راب وأراب) قول أبي زيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r6.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r6.claim: Sibawayh says لا governs its noun in the accusative without nunation, like إن, because it asserts negation as إن asserts affirmation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r6.anchor: قال سيبويه: (لا) تعمل فيما بعدها فتنصبه، ونصبها لما بعدها كنصب (إن) إلا أنها تنصب بغير تنوين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r7.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r7.claim: Sibawayh treats لا and its noun as one unit, a complete answer to a question about whether any person is present.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p36/r7.anchor: وزعم سيبويه أنها مع ما بعدها بمنزلة شيء واحد (¬7)؛ لأنها جواب لما يكون بمنزلة شيء واحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r1.claim: La rajula gives a comprehensive class-wide negation, unlike hal rajul or la rajul, which only deny one and could allow two; lā rayba is comprehensive too.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r1.anchor: فإذا قلت: (لا رجل في الدار)، فهو نفي عام، وكذلك {لا ريب فيه} (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r2.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r2.claim: Sibawayh parses لا ريب as nominative in position as a subject, like خمسة عشر at sentence start; this permits a raised conjunction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r2.anchor: وموضع {لا ريب} رفع بالابتداء عند سيبويه، لأنه بمنزلة خمسة (¬4) عشر (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r3.claim: The poem لا أم لي إن كان ذاك ولا أب uses a raised conjunct by syntactic position; accusative conjunction instead follows the surface form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r3.anchor: ولهذا جاز العطف عليه بالرفع في قوله: لا أم لي إن (¬6) كان ذاك ولا أب (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r4.claim: فِيهِ may be the predicate of لا ريب, or an adjective for ريب with an implied predicate such as واقع.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r4.anchor: يجوز (¬3): أن تجعله خبرا للابتداء الذي هو {لا ريب} ويجوز: أن تجعله صفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r5.claim: If فيه is predicate it is nominative for two reasons; if adjectival, its case follows either the surface accusative or the syntactic nominative, as in poetic alternatives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r5.anchor: فإن جعلته خبرا كان موضعه رفعا من وجهين: أحدهما: بكونه خبرا (¬4) للمبتدأ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r6.claim: If فيه is an adjective rather than a predicate, grammarians differ between following the surface accusative and the construction's syntactic nominative.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r6.anchor: وإن جعلت (فيه) صفة، ولم تجعله خبرا، كان موضعه نصبا في قول من وصف على اللفظ (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r7.speaker: ابن كثير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir lengthens the pronoun hāʾ, adding a glide after it, including when the pronoun is nominative as in minhu and ʿanhu.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r7.anchor: وفي قوله: {فيه}: قراءتان، إشباع (الهاء) حتى تلحق به (ياء) وكذلك في (الهاء) المضمومة (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r8.speaker: الباقون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r8.claim: The other readers use only the short kasra or damma; the weak hāʾ is not counted as a barrier between adjacent quiescent sounds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p39/r8.anchor: والباقون يقتصرون على الضمة والكسرة (¬1). وأصل (الهاء) في {فيه} الضم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r1.claim: The form تقاك is analyzed as deriving from اتقاك by dropping its assimilated first consonant and then the connecting hamza; yattaqī similarly reflects a fuller form.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r2.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r2.claim: Al-Azhari derives اتقى from an original اوتقى, with wāw assimilating into tā; تقى means to meet something with something and thereby guard oneself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r2.anchor: قال الأزهري: اتقى كان في الأصل (اوتقى) فأدغمت الواو في التاء وشددت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r3.speaker: السكري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r3.claim: Al-Sukkari calls the form taqā-yattaqī with open tā highly irregular, since comparable verbs do not drop their initial consonant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r3.anchor: قال السكري: وتقى يتقى بفتح (التاء) شاذ جدا، لأنه لا يقال: تضح بمعنى اتضح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r4.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r4.claim: Al-Azhari says taqiya-yattaqī means to become pious.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r4.anchor: قال (¬9) الأزهري: وإذا قالوا: تقي يتقى (¬10) فالمعنى: أنه صار تقيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r5.claim: The exegetes identify the muttaqīn here as believers; the Qur'an guides those who avoided associating partners with God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r5.anchor: والمراد بالمتقين في هذه الآية: المؤمنون، كذلك قال أهل التفسير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r6.claim: A believer who still commits major sins remains among the muttaqīn here because he has faith in the Book and avoids shirk.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r6.anchor: فأما من آمن ولم يجتنب الكبائر، فهو داخل في جملة المتقين (¬2) أيضا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r7.claim: The Qur'an is guidance in itself for anyone who reflects, but is specifically called guidance for believers because they benefit from it while disbelievers do not.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن الكتاب بيان بنفسه ودلالة على الحق، ولكنه أضافه إلى المؤمنين خصوصا، لانتفاعهم به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r8.claim: The wording resembles the Prophet being called a warner to those who fear, though he warned both those who fear and those who do not.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r8.anchor: كقوله تعالى: {إنما أنت منذر من يخشاها} [النازعات: 45]، وكان - صلى الله عليه وسلم - منذرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbari understands the phrase as guidance for both the pious and disbelievers, with one party omitted though implied.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r9.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: معناه: هدى للمتقين والكافرين، فاكتفى بأحد (¬4) الفريقين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r10.claim: Ibn al-Anbari compares this omission to verses saying garments protect from heat and that not all People of the Book are alike, implying the unmentioned counterpart.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r10.anchor: كقوله: {سرابيل تقيكم الحر} [النحل: 81] وقوله: {ليسوا سواء من أهل الكتاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r11.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r11.claim: Abu Dhu'ayb's line leaves out the alternative 'or misguidance' after asking whether his beloved's pursuer is guided.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r11.anchor: وقال أبو ذؤيب (¬2): فما أدرى أرشد طلابها (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r12.claim: Another verse calls the Qur'an guidance for all people; calling it guidance for the pious does not deny its guidance to others.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p53/r12.anchor: والدليل على هذا: أنه قال في موضع آخر: {هدى للناس} (¬4) فجعله هدى للناس عاما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq parses هدى as an accusative circumstantial from الكتاب, with the demonstrative's meaning as its governor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r1.anchor: فأما إعراب {هدى} فقال أبو إسحاق (¬5): موضعه نصب من وجهين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq also allows هدى to be an accusative circumstantial from the pronoun in فيه, governed by the meaning of ريب.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r2.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون منصوبا على الحال من (الهاء) في قوله: {لا ريب فيه}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r3.claim: Al-Farra calls the accusative qatʿ: الكتاب is the predicate of ذلك, and indefinite هدى is detached after a definite rather than explaining it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r3.anchor: والفراء يسمي الحال هاهنا: قطعا (¬3)، لأنه قال (¬4): تجعل {الكتاب} خبرا ل {ذلك}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r4.claim: Al-Farra also permits detaching هدى from the pronoun in فيه, yielding 'no doubt in it, guiding.'
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r4.anchor: قال: وإن شئت قطعته (¬6) من الهاء التي (¬7) في {فيه}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq permits nominative هدى as a second predicate: the Book is both the promised Book and guidance, like something both sweet and sour.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r5.anchor: إحداها: أن يكون (¬9) خبرا بعد خبر، كأنه قال: (ذلك الكتاب هدى)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r6.claim: Another nominative analysis supplies an omitted هو after the preceding statement: 'it is guidance.'
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r6.anchor: ويجوز: أن يكون رفعا على إضمار (هو) كأنه لما تم الكلام قيل: هو هدى (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r7.claim: A pause after لا ريب treats that phrase as 'the Book is truly certain'; فيه هدى then begins a new clause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r7.anchor: ويجوز: أن يكون الوقف على قولك (¬3): {لا ريب}، [أي: ذلك الكتاب لا ريب] (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r8.claim: The claim no doubt is objectively true even though false disputants doubt it; the cited poem likewise denies doubt in truth despite the liar's claims.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p55/r8.anchor: فإن قيل: كيف قال: {لا ريب فيه} (¬8)، وقد ارتاب فيه المرتابون؟ قيل: معناه أنه حق في نفسه

QASHANI:2:2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2/r1.claim: At realization, the Book is undeniably true; alternatively, it is the all-encompassing truth that clarifies the Book promised by earlier prophets and scriptures, known in prior knowledge and promised in the Torah and Gospel with Muhammad.
QASHANI:2:2/r1.anchor: عند التحقيق بأنه الحق، وعلى تقدير القول معناه بالحق الذي هو الكل من حيث هو كل لأنه مبين لذلك الكتاب الموعود

QASHANI:2:2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2/r2.speaker: عيسى عليه السلام
QASHANI:2:2/r2.claim: Qashani reports Jesus saying that the revelation will come through them, while its interpretation will come with the Mahdi at the end of time.
QASHANI:2:2/r2.anchor: وأما التأويل فسيأتي به المهدي في آخر الزمان

QASHANI:2:2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2/r3.claim: The answer to an oath is omitted because ذلك الكتاب indicates it, as in other Quranic passages beginning with oaths by the sun or those who pull out souls.
QASHANI:2:2/r3.anchor: وحذف جواب القسم لدلالة ذلك الكتاب عليه، كما حذف في غير موضع من القرآن

QASHANI:2:2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2/r4.claim: The Book is itself guidance for those who avoid vices and the veils that prevent them from accepting its truth.
QASHANI:2:2/r4.anchor: هدى في نفسه للذين يتقون الرذائل والحجب المانعة لقبول الحق فيه

QASHANI:2:2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2/r5.claim: People fall into seven final classes: the wretched and the happy; the happy comprise the people of the right and the foremost brought near.
QASHANI:2:2/r5.anchor: إما سعداء، وإما أشقياء. قال الله تعالى

QASHANI:2:2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2/r6.claim: One group of the left is eternally cast out, totally veiled and sealed in heart without primordial readiness for guidance.
QASHANI:2:2/r6.anchor: المطرودون الذين حق عليهم القول وهم أهل الظلمة والحجاب الكلي المختوم على قلوبهم أزلا

QASHANI:2:2/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2/r7.speaker: الحديث الرباني
QASHANI:2:2/r7.claim: A divine report says that God created a group for the Fire without concern for them.

QASHANI:2:2/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2/r8.claim: Hypocrites had innate readiness but acquired a veil through vice, sins, animal and predatory conduct, and satanic schemes; their dark dispositions make them doubtful and lost, with a worse state than the unready because their original potential conflicts with their condition.
QASHANI:2:2/r8.anchor: احتجبت قلوبهم بالرين المستفاد من اكتساب الرذائل وارتكاب المعاصي، ومباشرة الأعمال البهيمية، والسبعية

QASHANI:2:2#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2#2/r1.claim: People of virtue believe and do good seeking and desiring Paradise; they find their deeds present there, with ranks varying according to their works.
QASHANI:2:2#2/r1.anchor: الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات للجنة راجين لها، راضين بها، فوجدوا ما عملوا حاضرا

QASHANI:2:2#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2#2/r2.claim: People of mercy keep sound souls and clear hearts, receiving garden ranks by their capacities through divine bounty rather than earned perfection.
QASHANI:2:2#2/r2.anchor: الباقون على سلامة نفوسهم، وصفاء قلوبهم، المتبوئون درجات الجنة على حسب استعداداتهم من فضل ربهم

QASHANI:2:2#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2#2/r3.claim: Among those who mix good and bad, some are pardoned outright because conviction is strong, sins are shallow, or they have repented; God changes their misdeeds into good deeds.
QASHANI:2:2#2/r3.anchor: المعفو عنهم رأسا لقوة اعتقادهم، وعدم رسوخ سيئاتهم لقلة مزاولتهم إياها، أو لمكان توبتهم عنها

QASHANI:2:2#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2#2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2#2/r4.claim: Others are punished temporarily until entrenched sins are cleansed, then saved; they are people of justice and punishment, and mercy eventually reaches them.
QASHANI:2:2#2/r4.anchor: المعذبون حينا بحسب ما رسخ فيهم من المعاصي حتى خلصوا عن درن ما كسبوا، فنجوا

QASHANI:2:2#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2#2/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2#2/r5.claim: The foremost are either lovers who strive and turn back to God, or beloved people chosen through primordial divine care and guided to a straight path.
QASHANI:2:2#2/r5.anchor: والسابقون إما محبون وإما محبوبون، فالمحبون هم الذين جاهدوا في الله حق جهاده

QASHANI:2:2#2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2#2/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2#2/r6.claim: Lovers who strive sincerely and return to God are guided to His paths.
QASHANI:2:2#2/r6.anchor: أنابوا إليه حق إنابته، فهداهم سبله

QASHANI:2:2#2/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2#2/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2#2/r7.claim: The beloved are people of primordial care whom God selects and guides to a straight path.
QASHANI:2:2#2/r7.anchor: أهل العناية الأزلية الذين اجتباهم وهداهم إلى صراط مستقيم

QASHANI:2:2#2/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2#2/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2#2/r8.claim: The Quran cannot guide the two first, damned groups because one lacks readiness and the other has lost it; it guides the last five classes, all included among the God-fearing.
QASHANI:2:2#2/r8.anchor: فالقرآن ليس هدى للفريق الأول من الأشقياء لامتناع قبولهم للهداية لعدم استعدادهم، ولا للثاني لزوال استعدادهم

QASHANI:2:2#2/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:2#2/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:2#2/r9.claim: The beloved still need scripture after attraction and arrival to continue journeying in God, while lovers need it before and after arrival for the journey to and in God.
QASHANI:2:2#2/r9.anchor: والمحبوب يحتاج إلى هداية الكتاب بعد الجذب والوصول لسلوكه في الله لقوله تعالى لحبيبه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r2.claim: That book means this book, namely the Quran.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r2.anchor: { ذلك الكتاب } أي: هذا الكتاب، يعني: القرآن.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r3.claim: There is no doubt in it: it is true and right.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r3.anchor: { لا ريب فيه } أي: لا شك فيه، [أي]: إنه صدق وحق.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r4.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r4.claim: The declarative wording is intended as a prohibition against doubt.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r4.anchor: وقيل: لفظه لفظ خبر، ويراد به النهي عن الارتياب. قال: { فلا رفث ولا فسوق }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r5.claim: Guidance is clarification and indication for believers who guard against associating partners with God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r5.anchor: { هدى }: بيان ودلالة { للمتقين }: للمؤمنين الذين يتقون الشرك.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r6.claim: Restricting the Quran's guidance to the God-fearing indicates that it does not guide unbelievers; the author cites the verse about deafness to revelation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:1-2/r6.anchor: في تخصيصه كتابه بالهدى للمتقين دلالة على أنه ليس بهدى لغيرهم

ELMALILI:2:1-5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders 2:2 as “that Book,” free of doubt and the very guidance for the God-conscious.
ELMALILI:2:1-5/r1.anchor: İşte o kitap, bunda şüphe yok, ʿayn-ı hidâyet, korunacaklar için

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r1.claim: “That” points to the extraordinary sounds and their marvelous ordering, revealed by God to the Prophet’s heart: the Quran’s miraculous wording and meaning.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r1.anchor: işte o sesler ve o seslere verilen nizâm-ı bedî‘ile sana ve senin kalbine min-tarafillah inzal edilmekte bulunan

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r2.claim: Al-Kitāb is the complete, singular Book worthy of that title, the proof of truth and rulings, or the majestic, weighty divine speech promised in 73:5.
