ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r2.anchor: tam kitap, yegâne “kitap” ıtlâkına sezâ olan o burhân-ı hakk u ahkâm, yahut اِنَّا سَنُلْق۪ي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلاً ثَق۪يلَاً

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r3.claim: Among Muslims, “the Book” comes to mean the Quran alone; prophetic reports are customarily called Sunna rather than “Book.”
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r3.anchor: Müslümanlar beyninde “kitap” denilince ancak Kur’an anlaşılır. Hatta ehâdîs-i nebeviyeye bile “kitap” denilmez de “sünnet” tâbir olunur

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r4.claim: The Quranic Book is what was revealed to Muhammad, each sūra of which is inimitable, transmitted to us by mass transmission, written in muṣḥafs, and named as a whole or in part.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r4.anchor: Peygamberimiz Muhammed Mustafa sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Efendimiz’e inzal edilmiş olup her bir sûresi i‘câz ifade eden ve ondan bize tevâtüren menkul

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r5.claim: The root of kitāb is ketb/kitābet, joining or collecting letters in writing; customary usage then extends it from writing to what is written.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r5.anchor: asl-ı lügatta “ketb” ve “kitabet” gibi bir zamm u cem‘mânasını mutazammın olarak, hurûfu birbirine zammetmek, yani yazmak mânasına masdar iken

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r6.claim: “Book” can refer to a written collection or to the verbal expression conveyed by writing; in either case, its intended meaning is understood through the wording.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r6.anchor: Evvelkinde “kitap” bir yere yazılmış olan yazı

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r7.claim: A book or Quran cannot consist of meaning alone: meaning is neither read nor written, so the reality of the Book comprises wording that signifies meaning, or wording and meaning together.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r7.anchor: Hakīkat-i kitâb, o mânaya dâll olan nazm ve nihâyet nazm ve mâna mecmû‘udur

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r8.claim: Wording helps thinkers grasp and distinguish meaning; removing linguistic forms would leave no firmness in ideas, so a Quran or book consisting only of meaning is inconceivable.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r8.anchor: nazım yalnız âhara değil, mütefekkirin kendi kendisine bile tefhîm ve temyîz-i ma‘nâda mühim bir vâsıtadır

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r9.claim: God distinguished Adam by teaching the names, not merely their meanings; the revelation to the Prophet likewise includes both Quranic wording and meaning.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r9.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak meleklere karşı Âdem’e verdiği imtiyâzı sade

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r10.claim: The Quran as revealed to the Prophet is not meaning alone, but both its wording and meaning.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r10.anchor: Peygamberimize münzel olan da Kur’ân’ın yalnız mânası değil, hem nazmı ve hem mânasıdır

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r11.claim: The Book is wholly free of doubt and accusation: no other book’s divine truth and guidance of the straight path is known with equal certainty.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r11.anchor: Hadd-i zâtında her türlü şekten ârî ve her töhmetten müberrâdır. Kitaplar içinde hak kitâbullah olduğu bunun kadar kat‘iyyet ve yakīn ile mâlum olan

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r12.claim: There is no doubt in how the Quran was revealed or accusation in its delivery; the Prophet witnessed Gabriel’s revelations and his truthfulness and trustworthiness are established.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r12.anchor: Bunun ne keyfiyyet-i vahy ve inzâlinde bir şüphe ne de teblîğinde bir töhmet vardır

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r13.claim: Knowledge rests first on full observation and adequate experience, then on truthful reports and historical testimony where direct experience is impossible, and finally on sound rational inference.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r13.anchor: evvelâ şuhûd-i tâm ve tecribe-i kâfiye, sâniyen

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r14.claim: For those without direct witnessing or experience, the Quran’s inimitability leaves a lasting path to sound inference, guaranteed by God.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r14.anchor: Şuhûd ve tecribeye eremeyenler için de ilelebed delâlet-i i‘câz ile hüsn-i istidlâl tarîki açıktır

ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r15.claim: Those who doubt the Quran’s perfection and truth fall into two groups: self-interested, stubborn disbelievers with compounded ignorance, or hypocritical skeptics whose suspicion and moral blindness extinguish insight.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#4/r15.anchor: Bunlar ya cehl-i mürekkebe boyanmış, ağrâz-ı mahsûsalarından başka hiçbir şeye hiss-i iltifâtı kalmamış olan mahtûmu’l-kulûb mu‘ânidîn-i keferedir

ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r1.claim: Reyb originally means distress or uncertainty in the self, then commonly came to mean doubt; it also carries suspicion or accusation beyond mere doubt.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r1.anchor: örf-i lügatta bu ıztırâba başlıca bir sebep olan şekk ü şüphe

ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r2.claim: The comprehensive negation removes both intellectual doubt and moral suspicion or accusation, affirming the Book’s perfection on both fronts.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r2.anchor: Burada reyb bütün cinsi ile nefyedilmiş olduğundan reyb-i ilmî ve reyb-i ahlâkî diye tefrik olunabilecek olan şek ve töhmet haysiyetlerinin ikisi de selb edilmiş

ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r3.claim: “That is the Book” could be the second predicate of “no doubt in it,” but Elmalılı prefers an independent sentence, most eloquently read as an answer to an implied question.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r3.anchor: ذٰلِكَ,لاَ رَيْبَ ف۪يهِ’nin ikinci haberi olabilirse de bir cümle-i müstakille olması daha muhtâr ve bir suâl-i mukadder mülâhazasıyla bir cümle-i istînâfiye olması ise daha beliğdir

ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r4.claim: The assurance answers the Prophet’s imagined concern that humanity might accuse him of composing the Quran himself and falsely attributing it to God; it certifies both Quran and messenger as beyond suspicion.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r4.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah böyle bir suâle meydan bırakmamak için “bu babda hiçbir vechile irtiyâba mahal yoktur” diye sarâhaten te’mînât-ı mutlaka bahşetmiştir

ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r5.claim: Elmalılı says the Quran will argue these points in detail through its challenge to doubters and its condemnation of falsely claiming revelation.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r5.anchor: Kur’an bu noktaları ber-tafsil müdafaa ve isbat edecektir

ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r6.claim: This opening addresses epistemology: clear revelation ends philosophical dispute over certainty, reflecting creed’s affirmation that realities are established and knowable and its refutation of skeptical sophists.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r6.anchor: ve “sofestâiyye” denilen ehl-i reyb ve ‘inâdın reddi

ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r7.claim: Even as sciences advance, theoretical and moral skepticism periodically spreads, showing that doubt remains a central problem for humanity.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r7.anchor: ulûm ve fünûnun terakkiyâtına rağmen âlemde gerek nazarî ve gerek ahlâkî reybîliğin vakit vakit tevessü‘etmekte olduğu dahi inkâr olunamaz

ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r8.claim: The Quran identifies doubt as humanity’s greatest intellectual and moral heart-disease, then progressively explains the straight path, certainty about unseen and seen realities, God's unity, and ethical practice; al-Baqara’s opening is a general preface to the Quran after al-Fātiḥa.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r8.anchor: Sûre-i Bakara’nın başı Fâtiha’dan sonra bütün Kur’ân’ın bir dîbâce-i umûmiyesi demek olduğundan tertîb-i süverin ne kadar tabîî ve ne kadar ilmî ve derin esbâbı ihtivâ ettiği tezahür edeceği

ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r9.claim: Comparing these teachings with the Prophet’s human surroundings makes it necessarily clear that the Quran is purely divine revelation.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r9.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber’in muhît-i beşerîsi ile bu hakāik-i ilmiye teemmül ve mukayese edildiği zaman da Kur’ân’ın mücerred vahy-i ilâhî olduğunda zerre kadar iştibâha mahal olmadığı

ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r10.claim: The Quran is guidance itself for the God-fearing: proof that teaches right rulings and shows the straight path to those able to leave error and enter God's protection.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r10.anchor: müttakīlere ‘ayn-ı hidâyettir. Dalâletten çıkıp vikāye-i hakka girmek

ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r11.claim: In essence the Book guides all humanity, as 2:185 says; its gracious direction and invitation are universal, but actual attainment is granted to those who have or will acquire taqwā.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r11.anchor: Gerçi bu kitap esas itibariyle هُدًی لِلنَّاسِ’dır

ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r12.claim: Those who have lost their innate capacity will not benefit from guidance and may instead face loss, as 17:82 describes the Quran as healing and mercy for believers but increasing wrongdoers in loss.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#5/r12.anchor: kābiliyyet-i fıtriyelerini zâyi‘etmiş olanlar bundan müstefid olamayacak

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r1.claim: Huda can be used both intransitively and transitively; guidance may indicate the road or bring someone to the intended destination.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r1.anchor: “Hüdâ”, hem lâzım ve hem müte‘addî olur. Fâtiha’da beyan olunduğu üzere hidâyet, irâe-i tarîk ve îsâl-i matlûb

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r2.claim: He calls the two senses non-conveying guidance and conveying guidance, and says both are used in the Qur’an.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r2.anchor: ki birine “hidâyet-i gayr-i mûsile”, diğerine “hidâyet-i mûsile” tâbir olunur.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r3.claim: As applied to God, guidance can be direction and instruction, or the creation of a person’s guidance and success (tawfiq).
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r3.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hakk’a nazaran biri tarîk-i mûsile delâlet u irşad, diğeri halk-ı ihtidâ ve tevfik demektir.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r4.claim: Although the phrase may suggest enabling success, Elmalılı concludes that Qur’anic guidance here is instruction, since tawfiq and creating guidance are attributes of action, not speech.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r4.anchor: Kur’ân’a muzâf olan hidâyetin hidâyet-i irşâdiye olacağı tebeyyün eder. Çünkü tevfik ve halk-ı ihtidâ sıfat-ı kelâma değil sıfat-ı fiile râci‘dir.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r5.claim: The qualification ‘for the God-fearing’ signals that effective guidance and its joining with divine success ordinarily depend on a voluntary human choice.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r5.anchor: insanların bir fi‘l-i ihtiyârîsi ile âdeten meşruttur.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r6.claim: The Qur’an addresses all humanity, but some will not choose its guidance; those whose capacity to respond has been ruined by bad habits may react adversely to it.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r6.anchor: Kur’an herkese tarîk-i hakkı sûret-i umûmiyede göstermek için nâzil olmuş olmakla beraber herkes bunu kabul ve ihtiyarda müsâvî olmayacak

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r7.claim: The benefit of the address belongs first to people capable of good choice and taqwa, but taqwa is acquired and so can eventually include all humanity, without ethnic restriction.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r8.claim: Ittiqa literally means accepting or entering protection; wiqaya is strong safeguarding against things that cause pain or harm.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r8.anchor: “İttikā” vikāyeyi kabul etmek, ta‘bîr-i âharla vikāyeye girmek.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r9.claim: Taqwa therefore means taking strong protection and is also used for fear, avoidance, and caution; tevakkī suggests effort, while ittiqa is simpler.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r10.claim: God’s protection is the fullest protection, because human beings cannot control all future outcomes or even all present harms; true taqwa is entering God’s protection.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r10.anchor: En şâmil ve en kuvvetli vikāye ise ancak Allah’ın vikāyesidir. Zira vikāye-i beşer istikbâle ve âkıbete tamamen hâkim olamadığı gibi

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r11.claim: Everyone receives an involuntary, natural share of divine protection, but under divine mercy and voluntary action a person must consciously choose to enter it; its full manifestation depends on concern for the hereafter.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r11.anchor: insanın bu vikāyeye şuur ve ihtiyârıyla girmesi, yani ittikāsı dahi şart olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r12.claim: In religious usage, taqwa is placing oneself under God’s protection from afterlife harms: avoiding evil and committing to good, with both a positive and a negative aspect joined to fear and love.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r12.anchor: ‘ale’l-ıtlâk “ittikā” veya “takva”: İnsanın kendisini Allah’ın vikāyesine koyarak âhirette zarar ve elem verecek şeylerden iyice koruması

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r13.claim: It is mistaken to reduce religious taqwa to negative abstinence or mere ascetic restraint.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r13.anchor: takvâ-yı şer‘îyi sırf menfî ve mücerred perhizkârlıktan ibaret zannetmek hatadır.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r14.claim: Depending on context, the Qur’an also uses taqwa for fear, faith, repentance, obedience, avoiding sin, or sincerity.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r14.anchor: Kur’an’da “ittikā” ve “takva” üç mertebe üzerine zikrolunmuştur ki birincisi azâb-ı muhalledden tevakkī için şirkten teberrî ile iman

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r15.claim: The first level of taqwa is faith that renounces associating partners with God to escape everlasting punishment, illustrated by 48:26.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r15.anchor: birincisi azâb-ı muhalledden tevakkī için şirkten teberrî ile iman

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r16.claim: The second, conventional legal level avoids major sins and persistence in minor sins while fulfilling obligations, as in 7:96.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r16.anchor: kebâiri irtikâbdan ve sağāirde ısrardan ictinab ile ferâizi edâ etmektir ki şer‘an müte‘âref olan takva budur.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r17.claim: The highest level empties the heart of distractions from God and turns the whole person toward Him; this true taqwa is commanded in 3:102 and has degrees.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r17.anchor: sırr-ı kalbini Hak’tan işgal edecek her şeyden tenezzüh ve bütün mevcûdiyeti ile Hak teâlâ’ya teveccüh ve incizabdır

ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r18.claim: Prophets unite leadership in prophethood and sainthood; worldly duties do not interrupt their spiritual absorption, which is a special divine grace rather than an acquired result.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#6/r18.anchor: nübüvvet ve hem velâyet riyâsetlerini cem‘etmişler

ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r1.claim: Elmalılı says 5:93 combines the three levels of taqwa and reports a hadith calling 16:90 comprehensive of taqwa.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r1.anchor: âyetinin de câmi‘u’t-takvâ olduğu bir hadîs-i şerîfte vârid olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r2.claim: Qur’anic guidance includes every level of taqwa, and ‘the God-fearing’ should be understood broadly as anyone who practices taqwa in any degree.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r2.anchor: Kur’ân’ın hidâyeti bu merâtib-i takvâdan her birine şâmildir ve هُدًى لِلْمُتَّق۪ينَ hepsinden e‘am olan mutlak ittikā mefhûmuyla tefsir olunmak iktizâ eder.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r3.claim: He raises the apparent circularity: if Qur’anic guidance requires taqwa, while taqwa is itself learned from Qur’anic guidance, the condition seems circular.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r3.anchor: Burada hidâyet-i Kur’ân’ın ittikā ile meşrut olduğu anlaşılıyor. Hâlbuki ittikā da hidâyet-i Kur’an’dan müstefâd olan bir netice olacağına göre meselede bir devir lâzım gelmiyor mu?

ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r4.claim: The initial taqwa means a capacity for taqwa: sound-natured people of sound reason who can avoid obstinacy, hypocrisy, and total doubt and are candidates for certainty.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r4.anchor: burada ibtidâen takvâdan murad mebde’-i takvâ, yani kābiliyyet-i takvâdır. Ve “müttakīn” demek inad ve nifaktan, reyb-i küllîden ictinab edebilecek

ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r5.speaker: مفسرین
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r5.claim: The exegetes gloss the initial muttaqin as people approaching or prepared for taqwa (مشارفون للتقوى).
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r5.anchor: müfessirîn bunu مُشَارِفُونَ لِلتَّقْوَى diye tefsir ederler.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r6.claim: Guidance also raises a person to higher degrees, so taqwa includes people at earlier levels; Elmalılı calls this ‘generalization by metaphor.’
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r6.anchor: Hidâyet ziyâde-i mertebeye de şâmil olduğundan takva, kābiliyyet-i takvâ ile merâtib-i mütekaddime erbâbından e‘amdır ki buna “umûm-i mecaz” tesmiye edilir.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r7.claim: Taqwa is a means to salvation, not the ultimate goal; the desired result of guidance is reaching divine blessings safely from wrath and error, which exceeds taqwa itself.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r7.anchor: takva, gāye-i kusvâ değil vesîle-i felâh u sa‘âdettir. Hidâyet-i Kur’an’dan müstefâd olacak netîce-i matlûbe, gazab u dalâlden sâlim olarak ni‘am-i ilâhiyeye vusul

ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r8.claim: Thus Qur’anic guidance starts with those capable of taqwa, carries them through its levels, and reaches eternal happiness, so there is no actual circle.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r8.anchor: hidâyet-i Kur’an kābil-i ittikā olan ve henüz dalâlette bulunanlardan başlayarak merâtib-i takvânın hepsinden geçerek sa‘âdet-i ebediyeye kadar varacağından mütâla‘a-i merâtib ile iştirât-ı takvâda emâre-i devr asla melhuz değildir.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r9.claim: The Qur’an is guidance at both the beginning and the end of spiritual progress, so no one at any rank can dispense with it; it addresses ordinary people and elites, worldly life, and eternal aims.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r9.anchor: Kur’an, hem mebde’ ve hem müntehâ itibariyle hidâyettir. Bunun için insan ne kadar yükselirse yükselsin hidâyet-i Kur’an’dan asla müstağnî olamayacaktır.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r10.claim: Islam teaches necessities of worldly life and the acquisition of eternal ends; the Qur’an also supports the unlimited development of advanced civilizations, not only the spiritual needs of primitive people.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r10.anchor: terakki etmiş medeniyetlerin de nâmütenâhî yükselmesi için damân-ı tekâmül olmak üzere nâzil olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r11.claim: Society remains in crisis because humanity has not established a life order grounded in God’s unity or generally attained divine protection and certainty about the hereafter.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r11.anchor: beşeriyyet-i âmme vikāyetullâha girmemiş ve âkıbet ve âhiretine îkān hâsıl edecek mertebe-i ittikāya yükselememiş olduğundan âlemde buhrân-ı ictimâ‘î ber-devam bulunmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r12.claim: The opening presents the Qur’an’s eternal quality, witnessed reality, epistemic and ethical property, and practical purpose in four linked, uncoordinated sentences; it answers al-Fatiha’s ‘guide us’ prayer.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r12.anchor: kemâl-i ittisâl hasebiyle hurûf-ı ‘atf gibi revâbit-i lafziyeden bile müstağnî dört cümle-i mütenâsikadan mürekkeb bir nazm-ı veciz olarak Fâtiha’daki اهدنا duasının cevâbı olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r13.claim: The composition expands from three simple letters to three nouns and three concise clauses, then three verses and stories, continuing with the general address at 2:21; this unfolding exemplifies Qur’anic coherence.
ELMALILI:2:1-5#7/r13.anchor: evvelâ hattan üç harf-i basîtten, lafzan üç ism-i müfrede inkişaf ediyor. Sâniyen, bunların her birine mütenâzır gibi üç cümle-i vecîze inbisat eyliyor.

QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r1.speaker: النبي
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r1.claim: The Prophet says he was given comprehensive expressions, so his speech was made concise.

QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r2.speaker: بعضهم
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r2.claim: An unnamed Sufi renders the opening letters as a compressed exchange between a lover and his master, ending in lam-alif.

QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r3.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r3.claim: One explanation takes “that Book” to mean this very Book.
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r3.anchor: قيل ذلك الكتاب أي هذا الكتاب

QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r4.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r4.claim: Another explanation makes the phrase point to the discourse revealed earlier.
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r4.anchor: وقيل إشارة إلى ما تقدم إنزاله من الخطاب

QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r5.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r5.claim: Another view identifies the Book as the revelation God promised the Prophet on the Day of the Covenant.
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r5.anchor: وقيل ذلك الكتاب الذي وعدتك إنزاله عليك يوم الميثاق

QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r6.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r6.claim: One view identifies the Book as the writing in which God promised mercy for Muhammad’s community; its certainty calls for trust in that promise.
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r6.anchor: وقيل ذلك الكتاب الذي كتبت فيه الرحمة

QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r7.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r7.claim: Another view reads the Book as God’s prior decree, fixed from eternity for those destined for felicity or misery.
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r7.anchor: وقيل الكتاب الذي هو سابق حكمي

QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r8.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r8.claim: A further view says the certain divine decree is that God’s mercy preceded His wrath.
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r8.anchor: حكمي الذي أخبرت أن رحمتي سبقت على غضبي

QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r9.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r9.claim: The Book can signify faith, gnosis, love, and beneficence inscribed in the hearts of God’s friends; their absent beloved’s letters console and heal them.
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r9.anchor: وقيل إشارة إلى ما كتب في قلوب أوليائه

QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r10.speaker: أنشدوا
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r10.claim: Anonymous verses portray letters from beloveds as a cure for concealed pain and a source of joy, illustrating the friends’ comfort in their written message.
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r10.anchor: وفي معناه أنشدوا : وكتبك حولي لا تفارق

QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r11.claim: Guidance means clarification, proof, light, and a clear path for those God protects from ignorance, enlightens with reason, and chooses for the realities of union.

QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r12.claim: The Book heals God’s friends but blinds and afflicts His enemies.
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r12.anchor: وهذا الكتاب للأولياء شفاء ، وعلى الأعداء عمى

QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p17/r13.claim: The Godfearing person does not rely on seeing his own piety and recognizes that salvation comes only through his Lord’s grace.

ELMALILI:v1p103/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p103/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p103/r1.claim: Elmalılı says unbelievers refused to accept that the Qur'an was revealed by God and called it Muhammad's fabrication, a poem, or a soothsayer's speech.
ELMALILI:v1p103/r1.anchor: Lâkin kâfirler Kur’ân’ın Allah tarafından nâzil olduğuna inanmak istemediklerinden

ELMALILI:v1p103/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p103/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p103/r2.claim: He says many Qur'anic verses refute these accusations, citing 6:93, 46:8, 69:44–47, and 36:69.
ELMALILI:v1p103/r2.anchor: Onun için Kur’an’da bunları reddeden birçok âyetler nâzil olmuştur

ELMALILI:v1p103/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p103/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p103/r3.claim: Tanzīl is another Qur'an name because it was sent down in successive portions, as 56:80 states.
ELMALILI:v1p103/r3.anchor: Yine bundan dolayı Kur’ân’ın bir ismi de “Tenzîl”dir

ELMALILI:v1p103/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p103/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p103/r4.claim: Al-Kitāb is another name for the Qur'an; Elmalılı sends readers to 2:1–2 for its definition.

ELMALILI:v1p103/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p103/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p103/r5.claim: Furqān literally means separation; the Qur'an is named al-Furqān because it distinguishes truth from falsehood and lawful from unlawful, with 3:4 cited.
ELMALILI:v1p103/r5.anchor: “Furkān” da esasen ayırmak mânasına masdardır. Kur’ân’ın hak ile bâtılı, helâl ile haramı ayırması itibariyle bir ismi de “el-Furkān” olmuştur

ELMALILI:v1p103/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p103/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p103/r6.claim: Hudā is a masdar meaning to guide or to receive guidance; by extension it denotes a guide and the guided straight path, and the Qur'an is guidance for the God-fearing.
ELMALILI:v1p103/r6.anchor: Esasen hidâyet etmek mânasına masdardır. Hidâyet almak mânasına da gelir. Sonra hidâyet eden rehbere ve hidâyet olunan doğru yol mânasına da ıtlak olunur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r1.claim: Because al-Baqara was revealed in Medina after many earlier surahs, it was apt to call the text, already substantially complete, a Book.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r1.anchor: Bakara sûresi Medine’de nâzil olduğuna göre daha önce birçok sûrenin gelmiş olması gerekir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r2.claim: The declaration of no doubt covers both the Quran's divine origin and clarity, and its role as guide, mentor, and light.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r2.anchor: hem kitabın Allah’tan geldiği, anlatmak istediğini açıkça anlatabildiği hem de onun bir kılavuz, rehber, ışık olmasıyla ilgilidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r3.claim: Huda, rendered “guidance,” shares a root with hidaya and means divine direction toward a God-approved life of faith, worship, and morality; benefiting from it requires the consciousness described above.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r3.anchor: Bu rehberlikten yararlanabilmek için kişide yukarıdaki âyetlerde nitelikleri açıklanan bilincin bulunması gerekir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r4.claim: The lexical meaning of muttaqin is people who avoid what ought to be avoided.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r4.anchor: Müttakiler kelimesinin lügat mânası, “sakınılması gereken şeylerden sakınanlar” demektir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r5.claim: The following verses define the God-fearing through five qualities: faith in the unseen, steadfast prayer, spending for God's approval, belief in the Quran and earlier scriptures, and certainty about the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r5.anchor: Buna göre takvâ sahibi kimselerde şu beş vasıf vardır: Gayba iman etmek, namazı doğru ve devamlı kılmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r6.speaker: hadith
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r6.claim: A hadith says one cannot attain taqwa without avoiding even permissible things for fear of falling into what is prohibited; it is cited to Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r6.anchor: Kul, sakıncalı olana düşmemek için sakıncasız olandan da çekinmedikçe takvâ sahibi olamaz” (Tirmizî, “Kıyâme”, 19; İbn Mâce, “Zühd”, 24).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r7.speaker: hadith
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r7.claim: A hadith says a servant does not reach taqwa until leaving what troubles the conscience; it is cited to Bukhari's Book of Faith.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r7.anchor: Kul, vicdanını rahatsız eden şeyi terketmedikçe takvâ derecesini elde edemez (Buhârî, “Îmân”, 1).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r8.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra likens taqwa to carefully avoiding thorns on a path: living without becoming entangled in evils God has forbidden.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r8.anchor: Ebû Hüreyre’ye nisbet edilen bir benzetme, “Yolda yürürken dikenler görürsen ya yolu değiştirirsin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:2/r9.claim: The commentary also directs readers to its discussion of taqwa at 2:197.

BAQILLANI:v1p22/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r1.claim: If the opponents could match the Qur’an, rational custom makes their abandoning an easy decisive reply for harder hostility implausible.
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r1.anchor: فكيف يجوز أن يقدروا على معارضته القريبة السهلة عليهم وذلك يدحض حجته

BAQILLANI:v1p22/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r2.claim: Their eloquence and expertise, together with repeated public taunts about their incapacity, should have driven them to answer if able.
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r2.anchor: وهم على ما هم عليه من الذرابة والسلاقة والمعرفة بوجوه الفصاحة

BAQILLANI:v1p22/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r3.claim: Repeated declarations of the Qur’an’s stature summon its opponents to hasten to a challenge, even where a passage is not itself a direct challenge.
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r3.anchor: مما يدعوهم إلى المبادراة ويحضهم على المعارضة وإن لم يكن متحديا إليه

BAQILLANI:v1p22/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r4.claim: He includes the Qur’an’s description as guidance for the God-fearing among its declarations magnifying its status.

BAQILLANI:v1p22/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r5.claim: Arab poets competed in eloquence and oratory, holding familiar contests and boasting of their skill, which makes their failure to answer significant.
BAQILLANI:v1p22/r5.anchor: وكانوا يتنافسون على الفصاحة والخطابة والذلاقة ويتبجحون بذلك ويتفاخرون بينهم

BURHAN:v3p354/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.claim: The four broken plural forms of paucity and the two sound plurals are inherently paucity forms; other plurals may indicate few or many as context determines, as Qur'anic examples show.
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.anchor: واعلم أن جموع التكثير الأربعة وجمعى التصحيح أعنى جمع التأنيث وجمع التذكير كل ذلك للقلة

BURHAN:v1p50/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p50/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p50/r9.claim: Grammarians differ: some parse فيه هدى as an independent subject and predicate; others make فيه the predicate of لا and هدى a circumstantial accusative meaning هاديا.
BURHAN:v1p50/r9.anchor: وقوله ﴿ فيه هدى للمتقين ﴾ منهم من قضى باستئنافه على أنه مبتدأ وخبر ومنهم من قضى بجعل ﴿ فيه ﴾ خبر ﴿ لا ﴾

BURHAN:v1p348/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p348/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p348/r7.claim: Following the Prophetic practice of stopping at verse endings is preferable even when syntax continues; al-Akhfash likewise recommended a stop after هدى للمتقين because it ends a verse.
BURHAN:v1p348/r7.anchor: وحكى النحاس عن الأخفش على بن سليمان أن يستحب الوقوف على قوله ﴿ هدى للمتقين ﴾ لأنه رأس آية

BURHAN:v3p119/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p119/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
BURHAN:v3p119/r10.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says guidance for the God-fearing also implies guidance for disbelievers; the author cites guidance for mankind as support.
BURHAN:v3p119/r10.anchor: وقوله ﴿ هدى للمتقين ﴾ 12 أي والكافرين قاله ابن الأنباري ويؤيده قوله ﴿ هدى للناس ﴾ 13

BURHAN:v3p154/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p154/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p154/r1.claim: An adjective can stand without its noun only when it uniquely identifies that noun and the context is focused on the adjective; Sibawayh and Aristotle state the first condition.
BURHAN:v3p154/r1.anchor: أحدهما كون الصفة خاصة بالموصوف حتى يحصل العلم بالموصوف فمتى كانت الصفة عامة امتنع حذف الموصوف نص عليه سيبويه

BURHAN:v3p154/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p154/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p154/r2.claim: In praise or blame, context can focus on the adjective alone, allowing omission of the described noun; guidance for the pious means guidance for the pious people.
BURHAN:v3p154/r2.anchor: الثاني أن يعتمد على مجرد الصفة من حيث هي لتعلق غرض السياق كقوله تعالى

BURHAN:v3p154/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p154/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p154/r6.claim: The omitted noun in هدى للمتقين is القوم: guidance for the God-fearing people.
BURHAN:v3p154/r6.anchor: وقوله ﴿ هدى للمتقين ﴾ 4 أي القوم المتقين

BURHAN:v3p299/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p299/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p299/r6.claim: In لا ريب فيه هدى للمتقين, the disputed analysis may omit and imply one repeated element, or leave it unaccounted for.
BURHAN:v3p299/r6.anchor: وقد يحذف أحدها ويضمر أولا يلاحظ 4 على الخلاف في قوله تعالى ﴿ لا ريب فيه هدى للمتقين ﴾ 5

BURHAN:v4p104/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p104/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p104/r2.claim: The rhetoricians say no conjunction is needed when a following clause is so closely joined that it restates or emphasizes the first, as predicate, explanation or equivalent meaning.
BURHAN:v4p104/r2.anchor: وقال البيانيون للجملة ثلاثة أحوال فالاول إن يكون ما قبلها بمنزلة الصفة من الموصوف والتاكيد من المؤكد فلا يدخلها عطف

BURHAN:v1p170#2/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p170#2/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p170#2/r3.claim: A complete pause is allowed after an opening when it has an independent meaning, such as a surah name or a predicate of an omitted subject.
BURHAN:v1p170#2/r3.anchor: الثالث أنه يوقف على جميعها وقف التمام إن حملت على معنى مستقل غير محتاج إلى ما بعده

SULAMI:v1p47#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r1.claim: One reading makes the Book the decree written for creation concerning felicity, wretchedness, lifespan, and provision; no one can alter it.
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r1.anchor: قيل : ذلك الكتاب الذي كتبت على الخلق بالسعادة والشقاوة والأجل والرزق

SULAMI:v1p47#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r2.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r2.claim: Another reading makes the Book God's love and knowledge inscribed in the hearts of His friends, with contentment toward the events of His decree.
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : ذلك الكتاب الذي كتبت في قلوب أوليائي من محبتي ومعرفتي

SULAMI:v1p47#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r3.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r3.claim: The Book is the covenant to the Beloved and place of the secret; the Prophet knows revelation's mysteries, and saints and truthful ones after him love its subtleties.
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : ذلك الكتاب الذي كتبت في قلوب أوليائي من محبتي ومعرفتي في الرضا بموارد قضائي ، والكتاب هو العهد إلى الحبيب وموضع السر

SULAMI:v1p47#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r4.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r4.claim: A further reading is the pre-eternal divine pledge that God's mercy preceded His wrath.
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : ذلك الكتاب الذي كتبت على نفسي في الأزل ' إن رحمتي سبقت غضبي '

SULAMI:v1p47#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r5.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r5.claim: There is no doubt for the person whose secret God opens and whose heart He adorns with understanding from Him.
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r5.anchor: وقيل لا ريب فيه : لا شك فيه لمن فتحت سره وزينت قلبه

SULAMI:v1p47#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r6.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r6.claim: There is no doubt for the person whose secret is purified by the light of insight into the text's subtle meanings.
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r6.anchor: وقيل لا ريب فيه : لمن طهرت سره بنور الاطلاع على لطائف معانيه

SULAMI:v1p47#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r7.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r7.claim: For the people of gnosis, the Book is true guidance and an added clarification.
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r7.anchor: حقا لأهل المعرفة وزيادة بيان وهدى

SULAMI:v1p47#2/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r8.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r8.claim: Sahl calls it clarification for someone who magnifies his own affairs, power, and strength.
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r8.anchor: وقال سهل : بيان لمن تكبر أمر حوله وقوته

SULAMI:v1p47#2/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r9.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r9.claim: Junayd reads the guidance as connection for those cut off from created entities.
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r9.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : هدى للمتقين ، وصلة للمنقطعين عن الأعيان

SULAMI:v1p47#2/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r10.speaker: أبو يزيد
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r10.claim: Abu Yazid defines the God-fearing person as one who speaks and acts for God.
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r10.anchor: وقال أبو يزيد رحمه الله : المتقي من إذا قال : قال لله

SULAMI:v1p47#2/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r11.speaker: الداراني
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r11.claim: Al-Darani defines the God-fearing as those whose hearts have been stripped of love for desires.
SULAMI:v1p47#2/r11.anchor: وقال الداراني : المتقون الذين نزع من قلوبهم حب الشهوات

ITQAN:v1p227/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p227/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p227/r1.claim: The stopping point at “guidance for the God-fearing” can be good if what follows is an adjective, sufficient if an implied predicate or object is understood, or complete if “those” begins a new clause.
ITQAN:v1p227/r1.anchor: وقد يكون الوقف حسنا على تقدير وكافيا أو تاما على آخر نحو ﴿ هدى للمتقين ﴾ حسن إن جعل ما بعده نعتا كاف إن جعل خبر مقدر أو مفعول مقدر على القطع

ITQAN:v1p227/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p227/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p227/r4.claim: A stop may be good, sufficient, or complete depending on the grammatical attachment; its category can therefore vary with the chosen analysis.
ITQAN:v1p227/r4.anchor: حسن إن جعل ما بعده نعتا كاف إن جعل خبر مقدر أو مفعول مقدر على القطع تام إن جعل مبتدأ خبره

ITQAN:v4p382#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r4.claim: A referent may remain unnamed when famous: Adam's wife is left unnamed because he had no other wife, while the famous opponent of Abraham is identified as Nimrod.
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r4.anchor: أن يتعين لإشتهاره كقوله ﴿ وقلنا يا آدم اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة ﴾ ولم يقل ( حواء ) لأنه ليس له غيرها

ITQAN:v4p382#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r5.claim: A report says the Qur'an names Pharaoh but not Nimrod because Pharaoh was clever, as his replies to Moses show, while Nimrod's claim that he gives life and death exposed his stupidity.
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r5.anchor: قيل وقد ذكر الله فرعون في القرآن باسمه ولم يسم نمروذ لأن فرعون كان أذكى منه

ITQAN:v4p382#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r6.claim: Names may be omitted where identifying a person or place adds no significant benefit, as in the passerby at a town and the town the Israelites were told to ask about.
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r6.anchor: الرابع ألا يكون في تعيينه كبير فائدة نحو

ITQAN:v4p382#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r7.claim: Keeping a person unnamed can signal that the rule is general rather than restricted to one individual.
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r7.anchor: الخامس التنبيه على العموم وأنه غير خاص بخلاف ما لو عين

ITQAN:v4p382#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r8.claim: A person can be elevated by a worthy description instead of a name; the descriptions in the cited passages refer to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r8.anchor: السادس تعظيمه بالوصف الكامل دون الإسم

ITQAN:v4p382#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r9.claim: An enemy may instead be demeaned through a deficient description, as in calling the Prophet's hater “cut off.”
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r9.anchor: السابع تحقيره بالوصف الناقص نحو ﴿ إن شانئك هو الأبتر ﴾

ITQAN:v1p284/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p284/r6.speaker: النووي
ITQAN:v1p284/r6.claim: Al-Nawawi recommends lowering the voice when reciting verses that attribute false claims about God to Jews; al-Nakha'i practiced this etiquette.
ITQAN:v1p284/r6.anchor: قال النووي ومن الآداب إذا قرأ نحو ﴿ وقالت اليهود عزير ابن الله ﴾ ﴿ وقالت اليهود يد الله مغلولة ﴾ أن يخفض بها صوته كذا كان النخعي يفعل

ITQAN:v1p256/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p256/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p256/r1.claim: Nun sakin and tanwin have four recitation rules: clear pronunciation, assimilation, conversion, and concealment.
ITQAN:v1p256/r1.anchor: ولهما أحكام أربعة إظهار وإدغام وإقلاب وإخفاء

ITQAN:v1p256/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p256/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p256/r2.claim: Clear pronunciation applies before the six throat letters hamza, ha, ʿayn, ha, ghayn, and kha; some reciters conceal the nun before ghayn and kha.
ITQAN:v1p256/r2.anchor: فالإظهار لجميع القراء عند ستة أحرف وهي حروف الحلق الهمزة والهاء والعين والحاء والغين والخاء

ITQAN:v1p256/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p256/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p256/r3.claim: Assimilation occurs before six letters: lam and ra without nasalization, and nun, mim, ya, and waw with nasalization; some reciters omit nasalization before waw and ya.
ITQAN:v1p256/r3.anchor: والإدغام في ستة حرفان بلا غنة وهما اللام والراء

ITQAN:v1p256/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p256/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p256/r4.claim: Conversion occurs only before ba, changing nun or tanwin to a hidden mim with nasalization.
ITQAN:v1p256/r4.anchor: والإقلاب عند حرف واحد وهو الباء

ITQAN:v1p256/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p256/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p256/r5.claim: Concealment applies before the remaining fifteen letters: ta, tha, jim, dal, dhal, zay, sin, shin, sad, dad, ta, za, fa, qaf, and kaf.
ITQAN:v1p256/r5.anchor: والإخفاء عند باقي الحروف وهي خمسة عشر التاء والثاء والجيم والدال والذال والزاي والسين

ITQAN:v2p531/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p531/r1.speaker: ابن هشام
ITQAN:v2p531/r1.claim: Ibn Hisham says an inflection may have no available analysis except a weak one; he gives three disputed parses of the reading نجي المؤمنين, each with a grammatical objection.
ITQAN:v2p531/r1.anchor: قال ابن هشام وقد يكون الموضع لا يتخرج إلا على وجه مرجوح فلا حرج على مخرجه

ITQAN:v2p531/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p531/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p531/r2.claim: A sound analysis should enumerate the apparent options: الأعلى may modify either “Lord” or “name”; الذين after “guidance for the God-fearing” may be attached or independently accusative or nominative.
ITQAN:v2p531/r2.anchor: الخامس أن يستوفي جميع ما يحتمله اللفظ من الأوجه الظاهرة فتقول في نحو

ITQAN:v2p531/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p531/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p531/r3.claim: Parsing must respect each category's constraints: Zamakhshari wrongly called “King of people, God of people” apposition; they are adjectives because a modifier must be derived.
ITQAN:v2p531/r3.anchor: ومن ثم خطئ الزمخشري في قوله تعالى

ITQAN:v2p531/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p531/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p531/r4.claim: Zamakhshari's analysis of نصب تخاصم as an adjective of the demonstrative is rejected: demonstratives take an adjective with a definite article, so تخاصم is an appositive instead.
ITQAN:v2p531/r4.anchor: بنصب تخاصم إنه صفة للإشارة لأن اسم الإشارة إنما ينعت بذي اللام الجنسية والصواب كونه بدلا

ITQAN:v2p531/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p531/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p531/r5.claim: Zamakhshari wrongly treats الصراط and سيرتها as place adverbials; place adverbs must be indefinite, and these accusatives instead involve an omitted preposition, “to.”
ITQAN:v2p531/r5.anchor: إن المنصوب فيهما ظرف لأن ظرف المكان شرطه الإبهام والصواب أنه على إسقاط الجار توسعا وهو فيهما إلى

ITQAN:v2p531/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p531/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p531/r6.claim: Zamakhshari's claim that أن عبد الله is a source clause in apposition to the pronoun in به is untenable because apposition, like adjectival modification, cannot attach to a pronoun.
ITQAN:v2p531/r6.anchor: إن أن مصدرية وهي وصلتها عطف بيان على الهاء لامتناع عطف البيان على الضمير كنعته

ITQAN:v2p531/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p531/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p531/r7.claim: A construction should be parsed in a way consistent with analogous constructions; in “brings the dead out of the living,” the parallel verbal wording favors coordination with the preceding verb, not the noun.
ITQAN:v2p531/r7.anchor: بالفعل فيهما يدل على خلاف ذلك

ITQAN:v2p531/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p531/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p531/r8.claim: The proposed stop after “doubt” with فيه as the predicate of “guidance” is rejected; the parallel wording in al-Sajda shows فيه belongs with لا ريب فيه.
ITQAN:v2p531/r8.anchor: ومن ثم خطئ من قال في ﴿ ذلك الكتاب لا ريب فيه ﴾ إن الوقف على ريب وفيه خبر هدى ويدل على خلاف ذلك قوله في سورة السجدة

ITQAN:v3p163/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p163/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ITQAN:v3p163/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says “guidance for the God-fearing” omits “and the unbelievers”; “guidance for people” elsewhere supports the broader implied wording.
ITQAN:v3p163/r2.anchor: ومنها ﴿ هدى للمتقين ﴾ أي وللكافرين قاله ابن الأنباري ويؤيده قوله ﴿ هدى للناس ﴾

ITQAN:v3p163/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p163/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p163/r3.claim: Iḥtibāk is a subtle, rarely noticed rhetorical omission: the first clause drops what is expressed in the second, and the second drops what is expressed in the first; al-Zarkashi calls it reciprocal ellipsis.
ITQAN:v3p163/r3.anchor: الاحتباك وهو من ألطف الأنواع وأبدعها وقل من تنبه له أو نبه عليه من أهل فن البلاغة

ITQAN:v3p163/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p163/r4.speaker: الأندلسي
ITQAN:v3p163/r4.claim: Al-Andalusi defines iḥtibāk as reciprocal omissions and reconstructs the parable as comparing prophets and unbelievers to the caller and the one called.
ITQAN:v3p163/r4.anchor: قال الأندلسي في شرح البديعية من أنواع البديع الاحتباك وهو نوع عزيز وهو أن يحذف من الأول ما أثبت نظيره في الثاني

ITQAN:v3p163/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p163/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p163/r5.claim: In the command to put a hand into one's bosom and have it emerge white, “not white” and “take it out” are understood but omitted by reciprocal implication.
ITQAN:v3p163/r5.anchor: التقدير تدخل غير بيضاء وأخرجها تخرج بيضاء

ITQAN:v3p163/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p163/r6.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v3p163/r6.claim: Al-Zarkashi defines iḥtibāk as omitting each of two opposites' counterparts because the other indicates it; the cited response to “he fabricated it” implies guilt and innocence are distributed between speaker and addressees.
ITQAN:v3p163/r6.anchor: قال الزركشي هو أن يجتمع في الكلام متقابلان فيحذف من كل واحد منهما مقابله لدلالة الآخر عليه

ITQAN:v3p163/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p163/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p163/r7.claim: The phrase about punishing hypocrites or accepting their repentance implies the alternatives: if God does not forgive, He punishes; if He forgives, He does not punish.
ITQAN:v3p163/r7.anchor: وقوله ﴿ ويعذب المنافقين إن شاء أو يتوب عليهم ﴾ التقدير ( ويعذب المنافقين إن شاء فلا يتوب عليهم أو يتوب عليهم فلا يعذبهم )

ITQAN:v3p304/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p304/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p304/r1.claim: The author notes a tradition of works on Qur’anic parallels, naming al-Kisa’i, al-Sakhawi, al-Kirmani, al-Razi, Ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn Jama‘a, and his own collection.
ITQAN:v3p304/r1.anchor: أفرده بالتصنيف خلق أولهم فيما أحسب الكسائي ونظمه السخاوي

ITQAN:v3p304/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p304/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p304/r2.claim: The parallels science shows one story in varied forms, endings, word orders, additions, definiteness, number, particles, and assimilation; it overlaps the science of coherence.
ITQAN:v3p304/r2.anchor: والقصد به إيراد القصة الواحدة في صور شتى وفواصل مختلفة بل تأتي في موضع واحد مقدما وفي آخر مؤخرا

ITQAN:v3p304/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p304/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p304/r3.claim: The wording ‘guidance for the God-fearing’ suits this passage because it has just mentioned the totality of faith; Luqman adds ‘mercy’ and suits the doers of good.
ITQAN:v3p304/r3.anchor: لأنه لما ذكر هنا مجموع الإيمان ناسب ( المتقين ) ولما ذكر ثم الرحمة ناسب ( المحسنين )

ITQAN:v1p114/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p114/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p114/r5.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits Ibn Abbas's report that only the Prophet received the seven long suras, while Moses received two of them.
ITQAN:v1p114/r5.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي في الشعب عن ابن عباس قال السبع الطوال لم يعطهن أحد إلا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأعطي موسى منها اثنتين

ITQAN:v2p339#7/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p339#7/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p339#7/r6.claim: The God-fearing are believers who avoid associating partners with God and obey Him.
ITQAN:v2p339#7/r6.anchor: 2106 ﴿ للمتقين ﴾ المؤمنين الذين يتقون الشرك ويعملون بطاعتي

ITQAN:v1p231/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p231/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p231/r1.claim: Some stop markers permit either of two mutually exclusive pauses: one who pauses at لا ريب cannot pause at فيه, and vice versa.
ITQAN:v1p231/r1.anchor: قد يجيزون الوقف على حرف ويجيز آخرون الوقف على آخر ويكون بين الوقفين مراقبة على التضاد

ITQAN:v2p500/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p500/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p500/r1.claim: Negative lā can work like inna when it emphatically denies the whole genus; its noun is visibly accusative when annexed or similar, otherwise it combines with the noun.
ITQAN:v2p500/r1.anchor: أن تعمل عمل إن وذلك إذا أريد بها نفس الجنس على سبيل التنصيص وتسمى حينئذ تبرئة

ITQAN:v4p328/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p328/r4.speaker: البارزي
ITQAN:v4p328/r4.claim: Al-Barizi prefers لا ريب فيه to لا شك فيه because assimilation makes the alternative heavier, accounting for the Quran’s frequent use of rayb.
ITQAN:v4p328/r4.anchor: ﴿ لا ريب فيه ﴾ أحسن من ( لاشك فيه ) لثقل الإدغام ولهذا كثر ذكر الريب

ITQAN:v3p173#3/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p173#3/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p173#3/r5.claim: “No doubt in it” categorically denies doubt although some people doubt; their doubt is treated as absent because compelling proofs should remove it.
ITQAN:v3p173#3/r5.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى ﴿ لا ريب فيه ﴾

TUSTARI:2:1-2/r9.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:1-2/r9.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:1-2/r9.claim: “There is no doubt in it” means there is no uncertainty in the Book.

TUSTARI:2:1-2/r10.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:1-2/r10.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:1-2/r10.claim: He glosses the Quran as clarification for the God-fearing.

TUSTARI:2:1-2/r11.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:1-2/r11.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:1-2/r11.claim: The God-fearing disown any claim to independent power and take refuge in need of God's power in every state; God aids them, provides unexpectedly, and gives relief from trials.
TUSTARI:2:1-2/r11.anchor: والمتقون هم الذين تبرؤوا من دعوى الحول والقوة دون الله تعالى

TUSTARI:2:1-2/r12.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:1-2/r12.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:1-2/r12.claim: God's power is His action, which proceeds from His knowledge; His knowledge is an attribute of His essence. A servant's power is only a claim, since no moment belongs to anyone but God.
TUSTARI:2:1-2/r12.anchor: قال سهل: حول الله وقوته فعله، وفعله بعلمه، وعلمه من صفات ذاته.

TUSTARI:2:1-2/r13.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:1-2/r13.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:1-2/r13.claim: The God-fearing believe in the unseen, disown power over commands and prohibitions in belief, speech, and action, and ask God for protection from sin and help to obey.
TUSTARI:2:1-2/r13.anchor: أن يؤمنوا بالغيب وأن يتبرؤوا عن الحول والقوة فيما أمروا به ونهوا عنه

AKHFASH:v1p24/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p24/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p24/r2.claim: An indefinite noun immediately negated by lā is accusative without tanwīn; lā acts like a verb, its predicate is nominative, and the noun is built as one unit with lā.
AKHFASH:v1p24/r2.anchor: وذلك ان كل اسم منكور نفيته ب"لا" وجعلت "لا" الى جنب الاسم

AKHFASH:v1p24/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p24/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p24/r3.claim: For lā khawfun, rafʿ is the proper form because the coordinated phrase must also be nominative.
AKHFASH:v1p24/r3.anchor: فالوجه فيه الرفع لان المعطوف عليه لا يكون الا رفعا

AKHFASH:v1p24/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p24/r4.speaker: قوم
AKHFASH:v1p24/r4.claim: Some readers instead put khawf in the accusative and parse the following clause as a new nominal sentence.
AKHFASH:v1p24/r4.anchor: وقد قرأها قوم نصبا وجعلوا الآخر [رفعا] على الابتداء

AKHFASH:v1p28/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p28/r1.speaker: بعض القراء
AKHFASH:v1p28/r1.claim: Some readers assimilate the first hāʾ in fīhi into the hāʾ of hudā because identical consonants meet.
AKHFASH:v1p28/r1.anchor: قد قرأ بعض القراء {فيه هدى} فادغم الهاء الأولى

AKHFASH:v1p28/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p28/r2.speaker: العرب
AKHFASH:v1p28/r2.claim: Some Arabs treat hudā as feminine.
AKHFASH:v1p28/r2.anchor: وزعموا ان من العرب من يؤنث "الهدى"

AKHFASH:v1p28/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p28/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p28/r3.claim: Some Arabs silence the masculine pronominal hāʾ; the cited line, a usage said to be common among Asad al-Sarāt, has silent hāʾ in lahu.
AKHFASH:v1p28/r3.anchor: ومنهم من يسكن هاء الاضمار للمذكر قال الشاعر: [من الطويل وهو الشاهد التاسع] : فظلت لدى البيت العتيق أخيله

DAMGHANI:v1p212/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p212/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p212/r8.claim: Rayb means doubt, as in “no doubt in it” and other verses denying doubt.
DAMGHANI:v1p212/r8.anchor: فوجه منها : الريب الشك قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r3.claim: The first Qur’anic use of fī retains its basic locative sense, described as the general use in the Qur’an.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r3.anchor: أحدها : وقوعها على أصلها . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة :

FARRA:v1p11/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p11/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p11/r1.claim: This and that may both point back to recently mentioned speech: what has just been said is near like the present, yet completed like the absent.
FARRA:v1p11/r1.anchor: ولو قيل في مثله من الكلام في موضع «ذلك» : هذا» أو فى موضع «هذا» : «ذلك» لكان صوابا

FARRA:v1p11/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p11/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p11/r4.claim: For a visibly present person, the demonstratives cannot be exchanged: one asks who this person beside you is, not who that person is.
FARRA:v1p11/r4.anchor: من هذا الذي معك؟ ولا يجوز هاهنا: من ذلك؟ لأنك تراه بعينه.

FARRA:v1p11/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p11/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p11/r5.claim: If al-kitāb is an appositive to dhālika, hudan is nominative as the predicate of the demonstrative: that is guidance with no doubt.
FARRA:v1p11/r5.anchor: إذا أردت ب «الكتاب» أن يكون نعتا ل «ذلك» كان الهدى في موضع رفع لأنه خبر ل «ذلك»

FARRA:v1p11/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p11/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p11/r6.claim: If lā rayba fīhi is the predicate, hudan may also be nominative as following the syntactic position of that clause.
FARRA:v1p11/r6.anchor: وإن جعلت لا ريب فيه خبره رفعت أيضا (هدى) تجعله تابعا لموضع «لا ريب فيه»

FARRA:v1p11/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p11/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p11/r7.claim: Hudan may be nominative as a fresh sentence after the preceding clause is complete, as in the cited Qurʾanic and variant examples.
FARRA:v1p11/r7.anchor: وفيه وجه ثالث من الرفع: إن شئت رفعته على الاستئناف لتمام ما قبله

FARRA:v1p11/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p11/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p11/r8.claim: If al-kitāb is the predicate of dhālika, hudan may be accusative as a detached indefinite after the definite predicate is complete.
FARRA:v1p11/r8.anchor: فأما النصب في أحد الوجهين فأن تجعل «الكتاب» خبرا ل «ذلك» فتنصب «هدى» على القطع

FARRA:v1p11/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p11/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p11/r9.claim: Alternatively, hudan may be accusative as detached from the pronoun in fīhi, meaning ‘with no doubt in it, as guidance.’
FARRA:v1p11/r9.anchor: وإن شئت نصبت «هدى» على القطع من الهاء التي في «فيه» كأنك قلت: لا شك فيه هاديا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p39#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p39#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p39#2/r1.claim: He glosses the phrase as meaning that there is no doubt in the Book.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p39#2/r1.anchor: لا ريب فيه} لا شك فيه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p39#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p39#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p39#2/r2.claim: Guidance for the God-fearing means direction to right guidance.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p39#2/r2.anchor: هدى للمتقين} أي: رشدا لهم إلى الحق.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r3.claim: The detached opening letters function as oaths for the Qur’an: for example, Alif Lām Mīm means ‘By the letters, this is surely the Book’; other openings are read similarly.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r3.anchor: كأنه قال: وحروف المعجم، لهو الكتاب لا ريب فيه

MAJAZ:v1p28/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p28/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p28/r1.claim: Alif, Lām, Mīm take sukūn because they are letter names; hijāʾ letters do not inflect. Abū al-Najm’s line spelling out lām alif illustrates this.
MAJAZ:v1p28/r1.anchor: سكنت الألف واللام والميم، لأنه هجاء، ولا يدخل فى حروف الهجاء إعراب، قال أبو النجم العجلى

MAJAZ:v1p28/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p28/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p28/r2.claim: Alif, Lām, Mīm serve as an opening, the beginning of speech, and a marker for the sūra.
MAJAZ:v1p28/r2.anchor: ومعنى «الم» : افتتاح، مبتدأ كلام، شعار للسورة

MAJAZ:v1p28/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p28/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p28/r3.claim: The phrase means this Qur’an; Arabs may address someone present with wording that treats him as absent. Khafaf’s poem uses dhalika in this way.
MAJAZ:v1p28/r3.anchor: «ذلك الكتاب» (2) معناه: هذا القرآن وقد تخاطب العرب الشاهد فتظهر له مخاطبة الغائب

MAJAZ:v1p28/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p28/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p28/r4.claim: The poetic witness is Khafaf b. Nadba al-Sulami, whose mother was Abyssinian; he was counted among the pre-Islamic Arab crows. Malik is Malik b. Hammad al-Shamkhi; the poem’s horse was Muʿawiya, killed by Duraid and Hashim b. Harmala.
MAJAZ:v1p28/r4.anchor: قال خفاف بن ندبة السلمى، وهى أمه، كانت سوداء، حبشية. وكان من غربان العرب فى الجاهلية

MAJAZ:v1p29/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p29/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p29/r1.claim: La rayba means no doubt. Abū ʿAmr al-Hudhali recites Saʿida b. Juʾayya al-Hudhali’s line as evidence for this usage.
MAJAZ:v1p29/r1.anchor: «لا ريب فيه» (2) لا شك فيه، وأنشدنى أبو عمرو الهذلى لساعدة بن جؤية الهذلى

MAJAZ:v1p29/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p29/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p29/r2.claim: In Saʿida’s cited line, ḥasaru bihi means they surrounded him and laḥīm means a slain man; laḥima means was killed.
MAJAZ:v1p29/r2.anchor: أي قتيل، يقال: فلان قد لحم، أي قتل، وحصروا به: أي أطافوا به

MAJAZ:v1p29/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p29/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p29/r3.claim: Hudan lil-muttaqīn means guidance or clarification for the God-fearing.

NAHHAS:v1p177/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p177/r7.claim: One parse takes dhālika to mean “this,” with “the Book” as its predicate.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r7.anchor: يكون بمعنى هذا ذلك الكتاب فيكون خبر هذا

NAHHAS:v1p177/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r8.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p177/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the opening letters as a reference to the alphabet: some letters stand for the whole, followed by “that is the Book.”
NAHHAS:v1p177/r8.anchor: ويكون بمعنى الم ذلك هذا قول الفراء أي حروف المعجم ذلك الكتاب واجتزىء ببعضها من بعض

NAHHAS:v1p177/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r9.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v1p177/r9.claim: The Kūfans parse “this” as the subject and “the Book” as its predicate, with each raised by the other.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r9.anchor: الكتاب خبره والكوفيون يقولون رفعنا هذا بهذا وهذا بهذا

NAHHAS:v1p177/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p177/r10.claim: Another parse makes “the Book” an appositional clarification functioning like an adjective, and “guidance” the predicate.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r10.anchor: ويكون الكتاب عطف البيان الذي يقوم مقام النعت و هدى خبرا

NAHHAS:v1p177/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p177/r11.claim: One analysis makes “in it is no doubt” the predicate; the Kūfans instead identify the returning pronoun as the predicate.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r11.anchor: ويكون لا ريب فيه الخبر والكوفيون يقولون الهاء العائدة الخبر

NAHHAS:v1p177/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p177/r12.claim: The sixth analysis makes “no doubt in it” the predicate because the phrase means that it is true beyond doubt; the pause then falls after “no doubt.”
NAHHAS:v1p177/r12.anchor: والوجه السادس أن يكون الخبر لا ريب فيه لأن معنى لا شك حق ويكون التمام على هذا لا ريب

NAHHAS:v1p177/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p177/r13.claim: Tamīm uses dhāk instead of dhālika; neither dhālika nor hādhā inflects because neither remains fixed on its referent.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r13.anchor: ويقال ذلك ولغة تميم ذاك ولم تعرب ذلك ولا هذا لأنها لا يثبتان على المسمى

NAHHAS:v1p177/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r14.speaker: البصريون
NAHHAS:v1p177/r14.claim: The Basrans take the lām in dhālika as an emphatic letter.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r14.anchor: قال البصريون اللام في ذلك توكيد

NAHHAS:v1p177/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r15.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
NAHHAS:v1p177/r15.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ say the lām prevents the mistaken parsing of dhā as annexed to the attached kāf.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r15.anchor: وقال الكسائي والفراء جيء باللام في ذلك لئلا يتوهم أن ذا مضاف إلى الكاف

NAHHAS:v1p177/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p177/r16.claim: A further view treats the lām as replacing a hamza, which accounts for its kasra.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r16.anchor: وقيل جيء باللام بدلا من الهمزة ولذلك كسرت

NAHHAS:v1p177/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r17.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v1p177/r17.claim: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān says the lām signals great distance.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r17.anchor: وقال علي بن سليمان جيء باللام لتدل على شدة التراخي

NAHHAS:v1p177/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r18.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v1p177/r18.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the lām has kasra to distinguish it from the preposition lām.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r18.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق كسرت فرقا بينها وبين لام الجر

NAHHAS:v1p177/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r19.speaker: البصريون
NAHHAS:v1p177/r19.claim: The Basrans identify dhā as the noun in dhālika; al-Farrāʾ instead identifies the noun as dhāl.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r19.anchor: ولا موضع للكاف والاسم عند البصريين ذا وعند الفراء الذال

NAHHAS:v1p177/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r20.speaker: البصريون
NAHHAS:v1p177/r20.claim: The Basrans make lā accusative by analogy with inna; it governs an indefinite because it answers an indefinite with an implied min, and it fuses with the noun.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r20.anchor: لأنها جواب نكرة فيها معنى من بنيت مع النكرة فصيرا شيئا واحدا

NAHHAS:v1p177/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r21.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v1p177/r21.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says an indefinite normally precedes its predicate; with the predicate delayed in negation, it takes an incomplete accusative without tanwīn.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r21.anchor: وقال الكسائي سبيل النكرة أن يتقدمها أخبارها فتقول قام رجل فلما تأخر الخبر في التبرئة نصبوا ولم ينونوا

NAHHAS:v1p177/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r22.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p177/r22.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats lā as meaning ghayr; since it does not mean ghayr here, the noun is accusative without tanwīn to prevent the adjective from standing for its noun.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r22.anchor: وقال الفراء سبيل لا أن تأتي بمعنى غير تقول مررت بلا واحد ولا اثنين

NAHHAS:v1p177/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r23.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p177/r23.claim: Another explanation derives the accusative and absent tanwīn from the sense “I find no doubt,” with the governing verb omitted.
NAHHAS:v1p177/r23.anchor: وقيل إنما نصبت لأن المعنى لا أجد ريبا فلما حذفت الناصب حذفت التنوين

NAHHAS:v1p177/r24.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p177/r24.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p177/r24.claim: Lā may instead be parsed as laysa, with the phrase meaning “there is no doubt in it.”
NAHHAS:v1p177/r24.anchor: تجعل لا بمعنى ليس وأنشد سيبويه

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r1.claim: One parse makes dhalika a second subject with al-kitab as its predicate, and the full clause the predicate of Alif Lam Mim, linked by the demonstrative.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r1.anchor: أن يكون مبتدأ ثانيا والكتاب خبره، والجملة خبر

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r2.claim: Another parse makes Alif Lam Mim the subject and dhalika its predicate, with al-kitab as adjective, appositive, or explanatory substitute.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r2.anchor: مبتدأ و " ذلك " خبره و " الكتاب " صفة ل " ذلك " أو بدل منه

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r3.claim: A further parse makes Alif Lam Mim the subject and dhalika a second subject, with al-kitab modifying or explaining dhalika.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r3.anchor: مبتدأ ثان، و " الكتاب ": إما صفة له أو بدل منه أو عطف بيان

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r4.claim: La rayba fihi can predicate the second subject, with that clause then predicating the first.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r4.anchor: { لا ريب فيه } خبر عن المبتدأ الثاني، وهو وخبره خبر عن الأول

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r5.claim: Alif Lam Mim may instead complete an implied sentence meaning “these are Alif Lam Mim”; dhalika is then a subject with al-kitab as predicate or modifier, and la rayba predicates dhalika.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r5.anchor: خبر مبتدأ مضمر، تقديره: هذه ألم، فتكون جملة مستقلة بنفسها

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#2/r6.claim: Al-kitab may predicate dhalika and la rayba may be a second sentential predicate; the author accepts this despite a concern about multiple predicates, citing Taha 20 if tasʿa is a predicate.

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r1.claim: La is the genus-negating particle, patterned on inna; a singular indefinite noun is indeclinable on its accusative form because it implies the comprehensive min, as a poem makes explicit.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r1.anchor: سبب بنائه تضمنه معنى الحرف، وهو " من " الاستغراقية يدل على ذلك ظهورها

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r2.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says la rajul has an inflected case ending with only tanwin omitted for lightness; the author rejects his poetic evidence, reading it as an omitted interrogative construction.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r2.anchor: وزعم الزجاج أن حركة " لا رجل " ونحوه حركة إعراب

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r3.claim: When the noun is annexed or quasi-annexed rather than singular, la governs it in the accusative; la does not govern a definite noun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r3.anchor: فإن لم يكن مفردا - وأعنى به المضاف والشبيه به- أعرب نصبا

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r4.claim: Apparent uses of genus-negating la with a definite name, including the prophetic saying about Quraysh and Khosrow, require interpretation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r4.anchor: وقوله عليه السلام: " لا قريش بعد اليوم، إذا هلك كسرى فلا كسرى بعده "

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r5.claim: The predicate of la rayba may be fihi, but since Banu Tamim often omit it, the preferable analysis supplies ka'in; the pause after rayb is then complete.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r5.anchor: تقديره: لا ريب كائن، ويكون الوقف على " ريب " حينئذ تاما

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r6.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r6.claim: Sibawayh treats la with its noun as a nominative subject and says it does not govern the predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r6.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه أنها واسمها في محل رفع بالابتداء ولا عمل لها في الخبر

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r7.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash instead makes the noun nominative while allowing la to govern its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r7.anchor: ومذهب الأخفش أن اسمها في محل رفع وهي عاملة في الخبر

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r8.claim: La can negate a genus or an individual, prohibit or supplicate by jussive verb, and sometimes function as an augmentative particle.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#3/r8.anchor: واعلم أن " لا " لفظ مشترك بين النفي، وهي فيه على قسمين

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r1.claim: Dhalika consists of the demonstrative dha, a distance lām, and an address kāf; demonstratives have near, middle, and far degrees, though some grammarians count only two.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r1.anchor: واللام للبعد والكاف للخطاب وله ثلاث رتب: دنيا ولها المجرد

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r2.claim: Basrans take dha as triliteral; they differ whether its middle and final radicals were ya's or waw then ya, while the author notes such derivation is only an exercise for an indeclinable form.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r2.anchor: الأول قول البصريين. ثم اختلفوا: هل عينه ولامه ياء فيكون

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r3.claim: The far demonstrative may honor the referent; other proposed reasons are its descent from heaven, its prior promise to the Prophet, or its decree in the Preserved Tablet. The author says the referent is mentally or physically present.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r3.anchor: وإنما جيء هنا بإشارة البعيد تعظيما للمشار إليه

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r4.claim: Kitab is originally a verbal noun, but can mean the written object; its root signifies gathering, as in an army unit and stitching a waterskin, and writing joins letters.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#4/r4.anchor: والكتاب في الأصل مصدر، قال تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r1.claim: In established usage, writing means joining some letters of the alphabet to others.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r1.anchor: والكتابة عرفا: ضم بعض حروف الهجاء إلى بعض.

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r2.claim: Rayb is doubt accompanied by suspicion, more specific than doubt in general; al-Zamakhshari describes its essence as agitation and unease, supported by a hadith about leaving what troubles you.

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r3.speaker: ابن الزبعرى
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zibara uses rayb in the sense of doubt, saying there is no rayb in the truth.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r3.anchor: قال ابن الزبعرى: 105 ليس في الحق يا أميمة ريب

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r4.speaker: جميل بثينة
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r4.claim: Jamil Buthayna uses rayb in the sense of suspicion or accusation between two people.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r4.anchor: قال جميل بثينة: 106 بثينة قالت: يا جميل أربتني

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#5/r5.claim: A further reported sense of rayb is need, illustrated by a line about satisfying every need of Tihama and Khaybar.

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r1.claim: Hudan may be a subject with fihi as preceding predicate if la has no predicate; if fihi predicates la, hudan has an omitted predicate inferred from it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r1.anchor: مبتدأ وخبره " فيه " متقدما عليه إذا قلنا:

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r2.claim: Hudan may predicate an omitted subject huwa, or be a second or third predicate of dhalika under alternative parses of al-kitab and la rayba.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r2.anchor: وأن يكون خبر مبتدأ مضمر تقديره هو هدى

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r3.claim: Hudan may be an accusative circumstantial phrase from dhalika or al-kitab, or from the pronoun in fihi; its nominal source can function emphatically as guidance itself, by an omitted noun, or as an active participle.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r3.anchor: وأن يكون منصوبا على الحال من " ذلك " أو من " الكتاب "

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r4.claim: Fihi may modify rayb or be governed by rayb, though the latter creates an extended la-noun; it is tenable if governed by what rayb implies rather than by rayb itself.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r4.anchor: صفة لريب فيتعلق بمحذوف، وأن يكون متعلقا بريب

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r5.claim: Huda is a verbal noun on faʿla; although only sara, baka, and huda were said to occur in this pattern, laqiyahu laqan supplies another example.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r5.anchor: مصدر على فعل، قالوا: ولم يجىء من هذا الوزن

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r6.speaker: اللحياني
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r6.claim: Al-Lihyani reports the masculine form huda as the only gender, while al-Farra reports that some Banu Asad feminize it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r6.anchor: والهدى فيه لغتان: التذكير، ولم يذكر اللحياني غيره

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r7.claim: Fi primarily marks literal or figurative location, and can also indicate accompaniment, cause, equivalence to ʿala or bi, and comparison.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#6/r7.anchor: معناها الظرفية حقيقة أو مجازا، نحو: زيد في الدار

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r1.claim: Hamza reads the hāʾ in li-ahlihi imkuthu with kasra after a preceding yāʾ; Hafs similarly reads ʿāhada ʿalayhi Allāha and wa-mā ansānīhi follows the Hijazi form.

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r2.claim: For fihi or minhu, the usual form when preceded by a consonant is shortened, but Ibn Kathir reads the hāʾ with full length; other forms are also attested.
