SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r2.anchor: ويجوز الإشباع، وبه قرأ ابن كثير

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r3.claim: Lilmuttaqin attaches to hudan, though it may instead modify hudan with an implied predicate; best overall is to read the clauses independently and closely linked without conjunction.

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says fronting fihi in the wine verse suggests worldly wine has gall, whereas fronting it here would wrongly suggest other scriptures contain doubt; the author says the explanation can be disputed.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#7/r4.anchor: وكأن هذا الذي ذكره أبو القاسم الزمخشري بناء منه على أن التقديم يفيد الاختصاص

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r1.claim: A poetic counterexample attributed in the preceding segment to Alqama describes worldly wine as not causing headache or heaviness, but the author says it is no valid rebuttal because the poet's description carries no authority.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r1.anchor: تشفي الصداع ولا يؤذيك صالبها ولا يخالطها في الرأس تدويم

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r2.claim: The best answer is that the Quran is not a proper object of doubt: fair-minded readers find decisive evidence, while negligent doubt is disregarded.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r2.anchor: أن المنفي كونه متعلقا للريب، بمعنى أن معه من الأدلة

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r3.claim: A second answer restricts the negation to believers: there is no doubt in the Quran for them.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنه مخصوص، والمعنى: لا ريب فيه عند المؤمنين

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r4.claim: A third answer takes the declarative statement as a prohibition meaning do not doubt the Quran.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r4.anchor: والثالث: أنه خبر معناه النهي، أي لا ترتابوا فيه

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r5.claim: Muttaqin derives from muttaqiyin; the first of two yāʾs is deleted under the weight of the kasra, then one of the adjacent sukūns is removed; the word is an iftiʿāl form from protection.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r5.anchor: وأصله متقيين بياءين، الأولى لام الكلمة والثانية علامة الجمع

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r6.claim: In iftiʿāl, an initial wāw or yāʾ changes to tāʾ when followed by the infix tāʾ, as in ittaʿada and ittasara; analogous hamza changes are rare.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r6.anchor: إلا أنه يطرد في الواو والياء إذا كانا فاءين ووقعت بعدهما تاء الافتعال

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r7.claim: Iftiʿāl has twelve uses, including adoption, causation, reflexive action, selection, snatching, passive counterparts, reciprocal or intensive equivalents, equivalence to a simple verb, and replacing an unattested simple form.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r7.anchor: ولافتعل اثنا عشر معنى: الاتخاذ نحو: اتقى، والتسبب نحو:

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r8.claim: Wiqaya means intense protection and caution against harm, illustrated by a horse that protects its hoof; another view says its original sense is little speech.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r8.anchor: والوقاية: فرط الصيانة وشدة الاحتراس من المكروه، ومنه: فرس واق

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#8/r9.claim: The saying al-muttaqi muljam presents the God-fearing person as restrained; the cited poetry illustrates shielding or covering oneself with the hand.

SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#9/r1.claim: A second poem uses ittaqat in the sense of shielding oneself behind joined hands and forearm.
SAMIN-DURR:2:1-2#9/r1.anchor: فألقت قناعا دونه الشمس واتقت بأحسن موصولين كف ومعصم

ZAJJAJ:v1p65/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p65/r4.speaker: الأخفش وأبو عبيدة
ZAJJAJ:v1p65/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash and Abū ʿUbayda take dhālika al-kitāb to mean this book, supported by a poetic use of dhālika for hādhā.
ZAJJAJ:v1p65/r4.anchor: زعم الأخفش وأبو عبيدة أن معناه هذا الكتاب

ZAJJAJ:v1p65/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p65/r5.speaker: غيرهما من النحويين
ZAJJAJ:v1p65/r5.claim: Other grammarians identify it as the Qurʾān promised through Moses and Jesus, citing earlier scripture-holders recognizing it and concealing the truth.
ZAJJAJ:v1p65/r5.anchor: وقال غيرهما من النحويين: إن معناه القرآن ذلك الكتاب الذي وعدوا به على لسان موسى وعيسى

ZAJJAJ:v1p65/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p65/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p65/r6.claim: Dhālika can point back to something already mentioned just as hādhā can; Zajjāj illustrates the alternation with arithmetic and Qurʾānic examples.
ZAJJAJ:v1p65/r6.anchor: انفقت ثلاثة وثلاثة فذلك ستة وإن شئت قلت هذا ستة

ZAJJAJ:v1p70/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p70/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p70/r1.claim: Hudan can be a second predicate, giving the sense that this is both the promised Book and guidance, like something combining two qualities.
ZAJJAJ:v1p70/r1.anchor: إحداها أن يكون خبرا بعد خبر كأنه قال: هذا ذلك الكتاب هدى

ZAJJAJ:v1p70/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p70/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p70/r2.claim: Hudan may be nominative with an omitted huwa after the sentence about the Book is complete.
ZAJJAJ:v1p70/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكلون رفعه على إضمار هو

ZAJJAJ:v1p70/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p70/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p70/r3.claim: Hudan may also be parsed as a confirmation of the Book's being true, followed by the separate statement that it contains guidance.
ZAJJAJ:v1p70/r3.anchor: كأنك قلت ذلك الكتاب حقا، لأن لا شك فيه بمعنى حق

ASAD-NOTES:2:2#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:2#n2/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:2#n2/r1.claim: Asad reads muttaqī as awareness of God's all-presence and the wish to shape one's life by it; 'God-fearing' is too narrow, while guarding against evil captures only one aspect.
ASAD-NOTES:2:2#n2/r1.anchor: the awareness of His all-presence and the desire to mould one's existence in the light of this awareness

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p178/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p178/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p178/r1.claim: The author dates the beginning of Madinan revelation, after the Hijra, to Sūrat al-Baqara.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p178/r1.anchor: وبدأ الوحي في العهد المدني، بعد الهجرة، بسورة "البقرة" مفتتحة بِـ:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r3.speaker: القرطبي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r3.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says lā rayba fīhi is a universal negation, which is why rayb is in the accusative.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r3.anchor: وقال القرطبى: (لا ريب فيه) ، نفى عام ولذلك نصب الريب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p766/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p766/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p766/r1.claim: Across surahs, the opening designation tends to recur more: al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān favor Kitāb, while Ṭā Hā and Qāf favor Quran; Ṣād balances them.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p766/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p766/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p766/r2.claim: Al-Hijr puts Kitāb before Quran because the next verse mentions a town's appointed book; al-Naml reverses them before verses describing Quran-guided believers.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p766/r2.anchor: وفي هاتين السورتين أي الحجر والنمل: قدم (الكتاب) على (القرآن) في سورة الحجر وأخره في سورة النمل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p852/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p852/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p852/r1.claim: The opening denial of doubt is echoed by the challenge to those who are in doubt to produce a surah like the revelation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p852/r1.anchor: فكأنما هذه الآية جاءت مباشرة بعد الآية في بداية السورة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p852/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p852/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p852/r3.claim: The distant demonstrative suits an unreachable challenge; the proximal هذا in 17:9 suits guidance, which should be accessible to people's understanding.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p852/r3.anchor: أما في التحدي فيستعمل "ذلك" لأنه صعب الوصول إليه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p861/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p861/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p861/r1.claim: The author sets up a comparison of verses pairing guidance with mercy and/or good news for different audiences, asking whether revelation's purpose is limited to resolving disagreements.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p861/r1.anchor: قال تعالى في سورة البقرة: (ذلك الكتاب لا ريب فيه هدى للمتقين (2)) وقال في سورة لقمان: (هدى ورحمة للمحسنين (3))

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p862/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p862/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p862/r1.claim: A muttaqī protects himself, whereas a muḥsin benefits himself and others; because helping others includes mercy, God adds mercy for muhsins and rewards them with further good.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p862/r1.anchor: المتّقي: هو الذي يحفظ نفسه؛ فمتقي النار هو الذي يحمي نفسه منها، أما المحسن فيُحسن إلى نفسه وإلى الآخرين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p862/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p862/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p862/r3.claim: Faith is broader than ihsan, and a person cannot be muttaqī without being a believer; each surah's audience label follows its context.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p862/r3.anchor: الإيمان أعمّ من الإحسان ولا يمكن للإنسان أن يكون متقياً حتى يكون مؤمناً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p953/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p953/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p953/r1.claim: The author says surahs tend to repeat their opening label more: al-Baqara has Kitāb 47 times and Quran once, Āl ʿImrān Kitāb 33 times and no Quran; Ṭā Hā, al-Hijr, and al-Naml show the inverse pattern, while Ṣād balances them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p953/r1.anchor: هذا النسق لم يختلف في جميع السور التي تبدأ بالأحرف المقطعة وهي مقصودة وليست اعتباطية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p953/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p953/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p953/r2.claim: When both labels occur, their surah-wide counts generally differ by no more than one, and the dominant opening word explains the surah's phrasing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p953/r2.anchor: وإذا اجتمع اللفظان في آية يتردد ذكرهما بصورة متقابلة بحيث لا يزيد أحدهما عن الآخر إلا بلفظة واحدة في السورة كلها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p851/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p851/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p851/r3.claim: He sees Baqara’s challenge as built around generality through no doubt, the open-ended comparison, possible ellipsis, and the call for witnesses.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p851/r3.anchor: ومما سبق نلاحظ أن الآية في سورة البقرة بُنيت على العموم أصلاً (لا ريب، من مثله، الحذف قد يكون للعموم، ادعوا شهداءكم)

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f1.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f1.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f1.claim: The study situates al-Khuli in the post-1919 Arab intellectual awakening, driven by colonialism, underdevelopment, and the wish to join modern progress while affirming identity; thinkers pursued varied reformist, scientific, and secular paths.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f1.anchor: إذ شهد شهر مايو (١٩٩٥) مرور مائة عام على ميلاد أمين الخولي، يتبدى أمامنا قرن من تاريخ الحضارة العربية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f2.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f2.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f2.claim: Al-Khuli joins mastery of foundational tradition to an active present and dialogue between past and present as the route to a hoped-for future.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f2.anchor: إيمانًا منه بالماضي كركيزة، والحاضر كحياة متوثبة، وبالحوار الدائم بينهما ليتفاعلا ويتلاقحا

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f3.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f3.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f3.claim: Renewal begins by understanding, researching, and studying the old; ignorant destruction and mockery amount to dissipation, not renewal. He applied this method to language, literature, Qur'anic interpretation, religious thought, and biography.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f3.anchor: أول التجديد قتل القديم فهمًا وبحثًا ودراسة

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f4.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f4.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f4.claim: For al-Khuli, scientific renewal requires deep Qur'anic understanding and Arabic taste; he says Orientalist scholarship cannot reach the Qur'an's core, making renewal a Muslim duty and right.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f4.anchor: النظر العلمي الذي لا يستقيم بغير الفهم العميق للقرآن الكريم، بل وجاهر الخولي بأن هذا الفهم ليس سهلًا

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f5.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f5.speaker: محمد عبده
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f5.claim: Abduh presents Islam as a religion of reason that awakens thought and invites its use; rational inquiry attains faith, and reason takes priority over the apparent sense of revelation if they conflict.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f5.anchor: الأصل الأول من أصول الإسلام عند محمد عبده هو النظر العقلي لتحصيل الإيمان، والأصل الثاني هو تقديم العقل

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f6.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f6.speaker: محمد عبده
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f6.claim: Abduh regards religious feeling as innate but says religion develops with humanity; beliefs need continuing renewal to fit changing realities and advancing science. He rejects halting social life to preserve old legal books and urges free examination of inherited views.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f6.anchor: ضرورة تجديد بناء عقائدنا تجديدًا موصولًا كي تلائم تغيرات الموجودات

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f7.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f7.speaker: محمد عبده
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f7.claim: Abduh condemns imitation so strongly that he calls the uncritical imitator an unbeliever, since the imitator has not verified religious fundamentals.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f7.anchor: بلغ بمحمد عبده حد اعتبار المقلد كافرًا؛ لأنه مردد وليس مستيقنًا من الأصول

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f8.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f8.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f8.claim: Al-Khuli's maxim that earlier scholars were men of their own age means learn from them without copying them exactly.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f8.anchor: هم رجال ونحن رجال، لهم عصرهم ولنا عصرنا، نتعلم منهم ولا نحذو حذوهم النعل بالنعل

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f9.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f9.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f9.claim: Al-Khuli's reform continues the rationalist, anti-imitative path opened by Abduh and energized by al-Afghani; renewal protects society from stagnation.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f9.anchor: على أساس من إيقاظ الإسلام للعقل وإبطاله التقليد، انطلقت دعوة التجديد الديني من رحاب الأستاذ الإمام محمد عبده

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f10.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f10.speaker: طيب تيزيني
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f10.claim: Tizini classifies al-Khuli as a documentary, neutralizing approach to heritage that privileges collecting and editing documents and postpones their use.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f10.anchor: يقول تيزيني: «تهيمن على المنتدبين فكرة توثيق التراث بشكل يدعو

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f11.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f11.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f11.claim: The author rejects Tizini's classification as taking a stage for the goal: al-Khuli's documentation is preparatory work for historically informed renewal, not his final position.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f11.anchor: خطأ تيزيني في أخذ الجزء على أنه الكل، والمرحلة على أنها الغاية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f12.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f12.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f12.claim: The author argues that renewal presupposes historical awareness: newness marks a real difference between past and present.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f12.anchor: مجرد مصطلح الجدة لا يتأتى إلا في سياقها. فالجدة تعني التمايز عن القديم واختلاف الحاضر عن الماضي

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f13.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f13.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f13.claim: Both Abduh and al-Khuli worked to reform al-Azhar, clashed with resistant shaykhs, failed to realize their goals there, and turned hopes toward the Egyptian University.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f13.anchor: كلًّا من الأستاذ الإمام محمد عبده، والشيخ المجدد أمين الخولي قد انشغل بقضية إصلاح الأزهر الشريف ورسالته

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f14.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f14.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f14.claim: Abduh's university remained a dream that died with its backers, while al-Khuli's university teaching became his central arena and lasting achievement through his students.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f14.anchor: أما بالنسبة للخولي، كانت الجامعة واقعًا ماثلًا، بل هي واقعه الأول، حلبة كفاحه وساحة نضاله

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f15.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f15.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f15.claim: Though trained at the School of Sharīʿa Judiciary rather than al-Azhar, al-Khuli taught there; his 1934 philosophy lectures were pioneering, and he prioritized forming students over publishing books.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f15.anchor: لم يدرس الخولي في الأزهر — بل في مدرسة القضاء الشرعي — لكن درّس فيه. نذكر من هذا أول ما يدرس من الفلسفة

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f16.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f16.speaker: محمد عبده
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f16.claim: Abduh's suggestion that European religious reform borrowed from Islam developed into al-Khuli's research on Islam's relation to Christian reform.

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f17.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f17.speaker: محمد عبده
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f17.claim: Abduh opposed rhetoric distorted by philosophy and wanted it to cultivate taste and feeling; the author sees this as a precursor to al-Khuli's celebrated lessons in the art of speech.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f17.anchor: رفض محمد عبده البلاغة التي أفسدتها الفلسفة، ورام إصلاحًا فيها يسير بها نحو النمط الذي يربي الذوق

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f18.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f18.speaker: حسين مروة
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f18.claim: Murwa says the Afghani-Abduh school challenged absolute trust in heritage but did not deeply replace traditional methods because it retained their ideological foundations.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f18.anchor: حسين مروة: «على الرغم من أهمية مدرسة الأفغاني/عبده

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f19.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f19.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f19.claim: The author credits al-Khuli with helping develop methods and knowledge beyond what the reform school's founders had imagined.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f19.anchor: أمين الخولي من الذين قاموا بدور كبير في ذلك التطوير للمناهج ومستوى المعارف

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f20.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f20.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f20.claim: The author identifies al-Khuli's emphasis on living reality and vitality as the key to his use of evolution in religious renewal.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f20.anchor: الحياة والحيوية أكثر الكلمات شيوعًا في كتاباته وأحاديثه

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f21.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f21.speaker: كارل بوبر
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f21.claim: Although biologically incomplete, evolution is, in Popper's phrase, an excellent metaphysical research program; the author notes its continuing fertility beyond biology.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f21.anchor: فإنها — بتعبير بوبر نفسه — برنامج بحث ميتافيزيقي ممتاز

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f22.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f22.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f22.claim: The author criticizes al-Khuli for forcing T. H. Green, a neo-idealist opposed to scientific evolutionism, into the evolutionary ethicists.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f22.anchor: حيود الخولي في هذا الاتجاه حدًّا غير مقبول، حين يحشر توماس هل جرين Th. H. Green

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f23.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f23.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f23.claim: Al-Khuli explains biological evolution as gradual change from simpler to more complex forms through natural selection and survival of the fittest; he mocks reducing it to humans originating as monkeys.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f23.anchor: أنواع الأحياء — وعلى رأسها الإنسان — لم تظهر هكذا منذ خلقت، بل هي دائمة التغير من حال إلى حال

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f24.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f24.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f24.claim: Al-Khuli traces evolutionary ideas through Greek thought and Muslim authors including the Brethren of Purity, Ibn Sīnā, Ibn Ṭufayl, al-Qazwīnī, and Ibn Khaldūn.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f24.anchor: ويبين الخولي أصول نظرية التطور في الفكر البشري، عند الإغريق ثم عند الإسلاميين

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f25.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f25.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f25.claim: Al-Khuli says biological evolution does not contradict Islam: the Qur'an guides the God-fearing rather than teaching natural science, and Islam encourages reason without preempting scientific explanations.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f25.anchor: القرآن هدى للمتقين لا درسًا في الفيزياء والكيمياء والأحياء، والإسلام في أصوله وفروعه يحث على عمل العقل

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f26.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f26.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f26.claim: Al-Khuli attributes Western resistance to evolution to conflicts with Torah passages, arguing that this dispute does not belong to Muslims.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f26.anchor: مقاومة نظرية التطور والنزاع الشهير بشأنها في أوروبا وأمريكا، فهذا — كما يؤكد الخولي — لا يخصنا

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f27.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f27.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f27.claim: The author questions al-Khuli's Torah-only explanation by noting ongoing Christian opposition to evolution in the United States and public museum displays of the science-religion dispute.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f27.anchor: فهل هذا الذي لوحظ في شيكاغو يعني أن النزاع مع التطور ليس كما يؤكد الخولي من فعل الإسرائيليات

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f28.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f28.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f28.claim: The author turns to scientist and Anglican priest John Polkinghorne as a figure able to address both scientific and religious perspectives on evolution.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f28.anchor: يتقدم جون بولكين هورن J. Polkinghorne

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f29.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f29.speaker: جون بولكين هورن
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f29.claim: Polkinghorne says Darwinian selection explains adaptation without requiring divine intervention, but does not prove that evolution lacks divine purpose; some biologists assert this without adequate evidence.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f29.anchor: كما يوضح بولكين هورن. فأولًا بعض من رجال الدين رحبوا بالنظرية التطورية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f30.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f30.speaker: تشارلز كنجزلي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f30.claim: Kingsley welcomed evolution as compatible with progressive Protestantism: God created a world capable of continuing development rather than a finished world.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f30.anchor: رجل دين إنجيليًّا بروتستانتيًّا هو تشارلز كنجزلي Ch. Kingsley

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f31.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f31.speaker: أبري مور
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f31.claim: Moore likewise described a shift from sudden creation to continuing creation, an idea later developed by Teilhard de Chardin and Arthur Peacocke.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f31.anchor: أبري مور A. Moore الذي أوضح أن الخلق الفجائي قد حل محله مفهوم الخلق المستمر

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f32.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f32.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f32.claim: The author notes that continuous creation also appears among classical Muslim philosophers, especially Ibn Rushd, so al-Khuli's openness to evolution has precedents.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f32.anchor: فكرة الخلق المستمر ترددت بين جمع من كبار فلاسفة الإسلام في العصر الذهبي للحضارة الإسلامية، خصوصًا ابن رشد

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f33.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f33.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f33.claim: Al-Khuli extends evolutionary development from biology to mental and moral life, where ideas also arise simply, compete, and survive according to fitness.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f33.anchor: فحتى المعنويات العقلية كلها تتطور من أصل بسيط وتتنافس والبقاء للأصلح

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f34.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f34.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f34.claim: He compares idea selection to natural selection: conviction and social conditions help new ideas spread while older ideas lose adherents and disappear.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f34.anchor: ظهور الفكرة الجيدة يشبه في تطور الحي ظهور صفات جديدة في نوع من الأحياء تخالف الصفات القديمة

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f35.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f35.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f35.claim: Al-Khuli likens the victory of teaching modern mathematics and science at al-Azhar, championed by Abduh's small reforming minority, to natural selection; prophetic and reforming struggles follow enduring social laws.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f35.anchor: فكرة تدعو إلى تدريسها تبنتها قلة نابهة غير ذات سلطان يتقدمهم الأستاذ الإمام

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f37.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f37.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f37.claim: Al-Khuli treats renewal as an explicit religious principle expressing a universal, stable social law of development.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f37.anchor: في الدين فكرة صريحة عن التجديد تبين ناموسًا كونيًا، وتنسبه إلى سنن اجتماعية مطردة لا تتبدل

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f38.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f38.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f38.claim: In al-Mujaddidūn fī al-Islām, al-Khuli argues that evolutionary renewal is a means for Islam to preserve its claimed universality and permanence.

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f39.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f39.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f39.claim: For al-Khuli, renewal answers changing life and needs, extends the vitality of texts, and realizes the adaptive purpose of ijtihād without requiring changes to Islamic creed.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f39.anchor: التجديد بهذا انطلاق مع الحياة ووفاء بجديد حاجتها، وما كان أصل الاجتهاد في الدين إلا تقديرًا للحاجة الماسة

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f40.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f40.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f40.claim: Al-Khuli appropriates evolution for religious renewal despite its secular-scientific advocates and Salafi opponents, while also resisting secularists who overreach against truth.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f40.anchor: ها هو ذا أمين الخولي يستفيد منها ويسخرها لخدمة الفكر الديني وضرورة التجديد فيه

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f41.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f41.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f41.claim: Al-Khuli rebutted Ismail Mazhar's derogatory claims about Egyptian and Arab intellectual capacity with historical and scholarly evidence, appealing to a shared love of truth.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f41.anchor: الخولي يتصدى بضراوة للرد على مظهر حين صب وابل اتهامه على الشخصية المصرية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f42.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f42.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f42.claim: Evolution attracts reformers through hope of human improvement and motivates struggle; Darwinian selection makes organisms active competitors, unlike Lamarck's more passive account.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f42.anchor: نظرية دارون في تفسيرها لحدوث التغيرات العضوية وظهور وانقراض أنواع من الحياة، لا تجعل دور الكائن الحي سلبيًّا

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f43.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f43.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f43.claim: Al-Khuli argues evolution need not displace divine creation: Lamarck assigns God the original life and its capacity to develop, Darwin invokes a wondrous power, and Huxley says the theory cannot refute divinity.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f43.anchor: قرر لامارك أن الله هو الذي خلق الأصل وجعل فيه هذه القابلية للتطور. وقال دارون إن وجودها يستبعد المصادفة العمياء

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f44.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f44.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f44.claim: Al-Khuli says the Qur'an gives only a general account of human creation from soil or clay and in stages; scientific laws should responsibly explain that generality instead of childish literal tales.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f44.anchor: القرآن يقرر في إجمال تام خلق الناس من تراب، أو طين، وخلقهم أطوارًا دون أن يذكر في ذلك تفصيلًا

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f45.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f45.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f45.claim: Because the six-day creation of each species and divine rest appear only in Genesis, al-Khuli calls the alleged conflict between Islam and evolution a fabrication of intrusive Israelite traditions.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f45.anchor: تفاصيل مذكورة فقط في سفر التكوين من التوراة، ولم يرد لها ذكر في القرآن

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f46.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f46.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f46.claim: Al-Khuli links religious renewal with linguistic renewal: language expresses collective existence, religion gives it direction, grammar's old foundations rest on jurisprudence, and rhetoric studies the Qur'an's exemplary speech.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f46.anchor: اللغة وسيلة إثبات وجودنا، والدين وسيلة تقويم هذا الوجود واتخاذ هدف له

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f47.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f47.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f47.claim: Al-Khuli says grammarians kept ijtihād open even when jurists closed it; continued linguistic inquiry is necessary to understand and regulate speech.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f47.anchor: وحتى في عصور الانحطاط أغلق الفقهاء باب الاجتهاد، ولم يفعل النحاة مثلهم

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f48.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f48.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f48.claim: Language changes under material, environmental, psychological, intellectual, and social pressures across generations; languages may compete, though al-Khuli does not claim survival of the fittest for language.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f48.anchor: البيئة الطبيعية المادية التي تعيش فيها اللغة، والظروف النفسية والعقلية لمتكلميها، وأنماط الحياة التي يحيونها

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f49.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f49.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f49.claim: Al-Khuli rejects claims that Arabic descended perfect and unchanged from heaven; like other human languages, it developed over humanity's history in sounds, words, syntax, and style.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f49.anchor: فلم تظهر العربية — كما يقول الخولي — خلقًا سويًّا مستقلًّا

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f51.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f51.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f51.claim: Al-Khuli rejects emotional claims that Arabic is uniquely superior, complete, or at the end of its development, since they cut it off from historical change.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f51.anchor: وجد الخولي في رفض ودحض كل الدعاوى الانفعالية العاطفية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f52.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f52.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f52.claim: Islam's universal reach across peoples and generations guarantees changing needs; ijtihād is essential, human solutions are respected, and differences among legal authorities leave room for adaptation.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f52.anchor: امتداد دعوة الإسلام أفقيًّا إلى الناس جميعًا، ورأسيًّا مع توالي الأزمنة والأجيال

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f53.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f53.speaker: الرسول الكريم ﷺ
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f53.claim: Al-Khuli invokes the Prophetic principle that people know best the affairs of their worldly life to support human responsibility for practical solutions.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f53.anchor: قرر الرسول الكريم ﷺ أن الناس أعلم بشئون دنياهم

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f54.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f54.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f54.claim: Islam's concise treatment of unseen matters, creation, human origins, and historical details prevents unnecessary clashes with discoveries about nature and makes adaptation easier.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f54.anchor: اقتصاد دعوته في الغيبيات واكتفاؤه بالإجمال العام فيما يجب الإيمان به

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f55.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f55.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f55.claim: Al-Khuli says Islam can move forward alongside historical, geological, and natural science and keep pace with life's evolution without crisis.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f55.anchor: إذا ما شعر الإسلام أنه يستطيع أن يمضي مع أصحاب التاريخ دون تأزم، كما مضى مع أصحاب طبقات الأرض

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f56.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f56.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f56.claim: Al-Khuli surveys the first four centuries' renewers—including ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, al-Shāfiʿī, Ibn Surayj, al-Ashʿarī, and al-Bāqillānī—to recover their useful contributions.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f56.anchor: عمر بن عبد العزيز، والإمام الشافعي، وابن سريج، وأبو سهل الصعلوكي، وأبو الحسن الأشعري، والباقلاني

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f57.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f57.speaker: النبي ﷺ
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f57.claim: Al-Khuli cites the report that God raises a renewer for the community at each century's start; the source traces it to Abū Hurayra and says hadith authorities agree it is sound.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f57.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f58.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f58.speaker: جلال الدين السيوطي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f58.claim: Al-Khuli uses al-Suyuti's and al-Maraghi's works to show renewal remained an established religious idea even in periods of intellectual closure; al-Suyuti deemed an era without a mujtahid unacceptable.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f58.anchor: كتابا «التنبئة بمن يبعثه الله على رأس كل مائة» للإمام جلال الدين السيوطي

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f59.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f59.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f59.claim: Al-Khuli distinguishes developmental renewal, which discovers something genuinely new, from merely reviving or repeating what had existed before.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f59.anchor: اهتداء إلى جديد كان بعد أن لم يكن، سواء أكان الاهتداء إلى هذا الجديد بطريق الأخذ من قديم

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f60.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f60.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f60.claim: Al-Khuli presents evolution as an open ideal for Islam, not a new sect or imported Western doctrine; Islam can welcome studied innovations and social reform without being labeled capitalist or socialist.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f60.anchor: ديدن الإسلام — بتعبير الخولي — هو «مثالية لا مذهبية»

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f61.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f61.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f61.claim: Against an al-Azhar shaykh who confines evolution to ritual law, al-Khuli says change concerns creed, worship, and transactions; practical law should select what is easier and fitter to endure.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f61.anchor: ويعترض الخولي على قول لشيخ الأزهر

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f62.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f62.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f62.claim: Early Islamic disputes over divine attributes and the created Qur'an show doctrinal difference was possible; al-Khuli concludes doctrinal evolution is possible and now necessary, without endorsing those conflicts as its content.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f62.anchor: تطور العقائد ممكن، وهو اليوم واجب لحاجة الحياة إليه، وحاجة الدين إلى تقريره

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f63.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f63.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f63.claim: The author argues that al-Khuli's most consequential renewal reaches theology itself, while his better-known literary, topic-by-topic Qur'an commentary is grounded in the text's close relation to human life.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f63.anchor: أخطر ما في تراث الخولي، وما يستحق أن نتوقف عنده فعلًا، هو هذا التجديد في الفكر الديني

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f64.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f64.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f64.claim: The author makes renewal urgent because religion is central to Egyptian and Arab civilizational identity, which faces cultural dependency, extremism, and challenges to freedom, justice, and rationality.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f64.anchor: ذلك أن أصالتنا — أو بمصطلح أفضل خصوصيتنا الحضارية — إنما يتمركز

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f65.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f65.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f65.claim: Al-Khuli emphasized religion's strength in Egyptian identity and did not rule out divine revelation having reached ancient Egyptians.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f65.anchor: كثيرًا ما أشار الخولي إلى قوة البعد الديني في الشخصية المصرية، ولا يستبعد وحيًا إلهيًّا هبط على قدماء المصريين

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f66.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f66.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f66.claim: The author connects current cultural confrontation to post-Cold War claims by W. S. Lind and Samuel Huntington that future conflict would follow civilizational lines, with Islam cast as a leading threat.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f66.anchor: في مقال صمويل هنتنجتون — الأستاذ بجامعة هارفارد —

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f67.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f67.speaker: جلال الدين السيوطي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f67.claim: Al-Khuli cites al-Suyuti's account of crises recurring at century turns—including the Qarmatians and Crusader capture of Jerusalem—as occasions demanding renewal to repair accumulated weakness.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f67.anchor: كتاب السيوطي المذكور «التنبئة بمن يبعثه الله على رأس كل مائة»

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f68.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f68.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f68.claim: Al-Khuli distinguishes periodic renewal from a radical, revolutionary renewal required by major crises, describing the latter as a recurring social revolution.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f68.anchor: إن ذلك التجديد الجذري في رءوس القرون هو العمل الثوري الكبير الذي تحتاجه الأمة، كأنما هو ثورة اجتماعية دورية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f69.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f69.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f69.claim: The author calls for a historical, scientific, and developmental rereading of religious foundations to address present crises rather than disowning them in submission to outside dependency.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f69.anchor: إعادة قراءة أصولنا الدينية قراءة تاريخانية علمية تجديدية تطويرية، لا أن ننفصل عنها وننكر لها

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f70.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f70.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f70.claim: The conclusion presents al-Khuli's path as a way to preserve national and civilizational identity amid globalization's pressure toward cultural uniformity.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/f70.anchor: الرائد الشيخ أمين الخولي للتجديد والتطور في الفكر الديني

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p175#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p175#2/r1.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p175#2/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ gives the pronoun hā after silent yā a light, incomplete vowel, without reaching a yā glide; the same pronunciation applies in comparable forms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p175#2/r1.anchor: قال أحمد بن موسى : قرأ نافع: (فيه هدى)، و (عليه إنه)

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p175#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p175#2/r3.speaker: الكسائي عن إسماعيل عن نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p175#2/r3.claim: This transmission gives Nāfiʿ a yā after hā throughout the Qurʾān, with light hā vowels after silent wāw, alif, or other consonants and connected glides after moving letters.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p175#2/r3.anchor: وروى الكسائي عن إسماعيل عن نافع أنه قرأ: عليهي، يثبت الياء في كل القرآن

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p175#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p175#2/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p175#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim generally follow the light-vowel treatment of hā, with a special disagreement over وما أنسانيه described in the next passage.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p175#2/r5.anchor: وكذلك مذهب أبي عمرو وعاصم إلا في قوله: (وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان)

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r3.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn ʿĀmir follow the light-vowel rule for the pronoun hā; only Ḥafṣ's transmissions from ʿĀṣim are said to lengthen the kasra in the listed exceptions.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r3.anchor: وهو مذهب حمزة والكسائي وابن عامر، إلا ما روى حفص عن عاصم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr connects hā with yā after yā, wāw, alif, or any still or moving letter, and with waw after the corresponding vowel contexts.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r4.anchor: فأما ابن كثير فإنه كان [يصل الهاء بياء في كل ذلك

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r5.speaker: أبو بكر محمد بن السري
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r5.claim: Abū Bakr ibn al-Sarrī prefers kasra without yā or assimilation in فيه; Abū Ḥātim calls this the common reading, and the consonant skeleton also lacks yā.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r5.anchor: قال أبو بكر محمد بن السري: الاختيار في (فيه) الكسر بغير ياء ولا إدغام

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r6.speaker: أبو بكر محمد بن السري
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r6.claim: He rejects assimilation after kasra: the kasra implies an intended yā, while an actual yā separates the two hāʾs; their assimilation is also heavy.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r6.anchor: وأكره الإدغام، لأن من كسر، فالياء يريد، ومن أثبت الياء لم يجز له أن يدغم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r7.speaker: أبو حاتم
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r7.claim: Abū Ḥātim reports that Nāfiʿ assimilated the two hāʾs with a trace of ḍamma, and argues that Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr only lightly colored the hā rather than adding a glide.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: يروى عن نافع أنه كان يدغم: ((فيه هدى)) ويشمها شيئا من الضم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r8.speaker: أبو حاتم
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r8.claim: Abū Ḥātim says ḍamma is a recognized dialect without a spoken waw; adding waw or yā would separate the hāʾs and prevent assimilation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r8.anchor: والضم لغة مشهورة، وليس بعد الضم واو في اللفظ

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r9.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r9.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r9.claim: Some colleagues judge assimilation heavy in pronunciation but valid by analogy because the hāʾs share an articulation point; throat letters and a word boundary make it awkward.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p177/r9.anchor: وقال بعض أصحابنا: قراءة من قرأ ((فيه هدى))، بإدغام الهاء في الهاء، هو ثقيل في اللفظ وجائز

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r1.speaker: الأخفش
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash reports assimilation of the two hāʾs in فيه هدى as a reading.

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r2.claim: Abū Bakr says true assimilation cannot coexist with a vowel or separation; Abū ʿAmr instead made a quick, concealed vowel that listeners mistook for assimilation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر- في رواية من روى عن أبي عمرو وغيره أنه كان يشم ويدغم-: هذا محال

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r3.speaker: أبو حاتم
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r3.claim: Abū Ḥātim says Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr intended concealment, not full assimilation, since genuine assimilation would silence the first hā; Abū ʿAmr avoided excessive movement and full vowels.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r3.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: أراد أبو عمرو ونافع الإخفاء، فلذلك أشما الضم والكسر

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r4.speaker: سيبويه
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r4.claim: Sībawayh distinguishes أراب, to become a possessor of doubt, from رابني, to put me into doubt, comparing the first pattern to becoming deserving of blame.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r4.anchor: قال سيبويه: قالوا: أراب كما قالوا : ألام، أي صار صاحب ريبة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r5.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r5.claim: Abū Zayd says رابني describes a witnessed matter that makes doubt certain, whereas أرابني describes suspicion without certainty; a poem illustrates the latter.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r5.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: قد رابني من فلان أمر رأيته منه ريبا إذا كنت مستيقنا

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses لا ريب as no doubt.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: لا ريب: لا شك

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r7.speaker: سيبويه
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r7.claim: Sībawayh notes that a shortened verbal noun of this pattern is rare except with weak roots, and explains هدى as an exceptional source form of هديته.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p179/r7.anchor: قال سيبويه : قلما يكون ما ضم أوله من المصدر منقوصا

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r1.claim: Al-Fārisī allows هدى to be a source form confined to weak roots, like كينونة, though the corresponding source pattern is absent from sound roots.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r1.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يكون فعل مصدرا اختص به المعتل وإن لم يكن في الصحيح

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r2.claim: He notes that words not normally classified as verbal nouns can function like sources, citing Labīd's construction as an object governed like a source.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r2.anchor: ويقويه أيضا أن ناسا من النحويين يزعمون أنه قد يجرى الأسماء التي ليست بمصادر

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r3.claim: On this usage, هدى, سرى, and تقى can stand in for a source, as تقاة does in 3:28; the cited poetic usage likewise treats a noun as a source.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r3.anchor: فكذلك يكون الهدى والسرى والتقى، وفي التنزيل: إلا أن تتقوا منهم تقاة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda explains هدى للمتقين as clarification for the God-fearing.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: (هدى للمتقين): بيانا لهم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r6.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan reports that some Arabs treat هدى as feminine.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r6.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن: زعموا أن من العرب من يؤنث الهدى

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r7.claim: The verb هدى takes two objects; its second object may be introduced by إلى or لام, as the cited Qurʾanic examples show.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r7.anchor: وأما الفعل من الهدى: فيتعدى إلى مفعولين، يتعدى إلى الثاني منهما بأحد حرفي جر

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r8.claim: When the preposition is omitted, اهدنا الصراط means show us the path and lead us on it; the request seeks the guidance promised to followers of God's good pleasure.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p181/r8.anchor: وقد يحذف الحرف من قولهم: هديته لكذا وإلى كذا، فيصل الفعل إلى المفعول الثاني

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r1.claim: دار السلام may be an honorific genitive referring to God's name al-Salām, like بيت الله or عبد الله.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r1.anchor: إما أن يراد به الإضافة إلى السلام الذي هو اسم من أسماء الله

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r2.claim: Alternatively, دار السلام means the abode of safety, where residents suffer neither hardship nor punishment, as 35:35 describes.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r2.anchor: وإما أن يراد بالسلام جمع سلامة، كأنه: دار السلامة التي لا يلقون في حلولها عنتا

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r3.claim: Asking for the straight path can mean asking for firmness in faith and the ways of religion, avoiding those who have strayed; 6:153 and 37:117–118 reinforce this reading.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r3.anchor: وقد يكون قوله: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم سؤالا لأن يلطف لهم بالتثبيت على الإيمان

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r4.claim: The other interpretation asks for direction to Paradise and reward, supported by the promise to guide those slain in God's path and set their affairs right.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p184/r4.anchor: ويقوي الوجه الأول قوله: والذين قتلوا في سبيل الله فلن يضل أعمالهم، سيهديهم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r1.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan distinguishes guiding a bride to her husband from presenting her as a gift; Tamīm uses the former form while Qays uses the latter.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r1.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن: يقال هديت العروس إلى بعلها، وتقول أيضا: أهديتها إليه

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r2.claim: The opposition of guidance and misguidance supports glossing الهدى as direction or guidance.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r2.anchor: ومما يدل على أن الهدى الدلالة- كما فسره أبو الحسن- أنه قد قوبل به الضلال

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r3.speaker: ابن مقبل
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r3.claim: Ibn Muqbil's poem uses أهدي for guiding others, contrasting it with not being guided himself.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r3.anchor: وقال ابن مقبل : قد كنت أهدي ولا أهدى فعلمني ... حسن المقادة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r4.claim: In the cited desert poem, استبنت الهدى means daylight became clear; the mirage makes the distant desert and camels appear to rise and sink.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r4.anchor: وقيل في قوله: حتى استبنت الهدى والبيد هاجمة ... يخشعن في الآل غلفا أو يصلينا

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr glosses غلفا as having nothing that covers the camels and explains يصلينا as their seeming to burn while the mirage lifts and lowers them.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: غلفا: ليس عليها شيء يسترها. وقوله: أو يصلينا، كأنهن

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r6.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r6.claim: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā reports Baghdad usage of هدي بيت الله; Hijaz speakers lighten الهدي while Tamīm gives it a heavier pronunciation, and its singular is هدية.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r6.anchor: وحكى أحمد بن يحيى عن بعض البغداديين يقال: هدي بيت الله، وأهل الحجاز يخففون

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r7.claim: Both vocalic forms are read in the phrase about the sacrificial offering reaching its place in 2:196.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r7.anchor: وقد قرئ بالوجهين، حتى يبلغ الهدي محله [البقرة/ 196] والهدي محله

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r8.claim: Calling someone the هدي of a tribe means its protected neighbor, whose harm is forbidden like that of a sacrificial offering.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r8.anchor: ويقال: فلان هدي بني فلان وهديهم، أي جارهم يحرم عليهم منه ما يحرم من الهدي

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r9.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r9.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r9.claim: The derivatives cover offering a sacrifice or a gift, escorting a bride, the direction of a matter, demeanor, guiding a lost animal or a person to religion, a generous giver, and a gift tray.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r9.anchor: وأهديت الهدي إهداء، وأهديت الهدية إهداء، وهديت العروس إلى زوجها هداء

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r10.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r10.speaker: أحمد
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r10.claim: Aḥmad treats هدى and أهدى as equivalent, citing a poem in which a speaker tells a woman to give him meat.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r10.anchor: وقال أحمد هدى وأهدى واحد، وأنشد: لقد علمت أم الأديبر أنني

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r11.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r11.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r11.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the singular of الهدي is هدية, by analogy with مطي and مطية, and cites a poem about garlanded offerings.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p186/r11.anchor: قال أبو علي: وواحد الهدي هدية، مثل مطي ومطية

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r1.claim: فيه may be the predicate of لا ريب, raised as the predicate of the subject under Sībawayh's analysis or as the predicate of إن under Abū al-Ḥasan's.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r1.anchor: فأما قوله: (لا ريب فيه) فيجوز أن تجعل (فيه) خبرا

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r2.claim: Alternatively, فيه is an adjective with an omitted predicate; it is accusative if the adjective follows the surface form, but raised if it follows the syntactic position.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r2.anchor: فإن جعلته صفة أضمرت الخبر، وإن جعلته خبرا كان موضعه رفعا

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r3.claim: The case belongs to the adverbial phrase itself, not the omitted word it modifies, because the pronoun is contained in the adverb.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r3.anchor: والموضع للظرف نفسه لا لما كان يتعلق به، لأن الحكم له دون ما كان

IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r1.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r1.claim: Nafi gives hā a slight vowel after silent yā without fully realizing a following yā, as in fīhi hudan.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r1.anchor: إذا كان قبل الهاء ياء ساكنة حركها حركة مختلسة من غير أن يبلغ بها الياء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r2.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r2.claim: After silent wāw or alif, Nafi lightly dammas hā without reaching full wāw, as in the cited examples.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r2.anchor: وإذا كان قبلها واو ساكنة مثل ﴿ ندعوه إنه ﴾ الطور 28 أو ألف مثل ﴿ اجتباه وهداه ﴾ النحل 121

IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r3.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r3.claim: After another silent consonant Nafi gives hā a light vowel without full wāw; al-Musayyibi reports a wāw link only in وأشركه في أمري.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r3.anchor: وإذا كان قبل الهاء حرف غير الياء والواو والألف وهو ساكن حرك الهاء أيضا حركة خفيفة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r6.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r6.claim: With a preceding kasra Nafi kasras hā and links it to yā; after ḍamma or fatḥa he links it to wāw, but pauses without wāw.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p130/r6.anchor: فإن كان ما قبل الهاء متحركا وكانت الحركة كسرة كسر الهاء ووصلها بياء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p131/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p131/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p131/r1.claim: Abu ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim generally follow Nafi's hā treatment, with the cited differences in the following verses.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p131/r1.anchor: وكذلك مذهب أبي عمرو وعاصم إلا في قوله ﴿ وما أنسانيه ﴾ الكهف 63

IBNMUJAHID:v1p131/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p131/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p131/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir links hā to a following yā or wāw in every environment, with either a silent or vowelled preceding letter.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p131/r4.anchor: وأما ابن كثير فكان يصل الهاء في ذلك كله كان قبلها ياء أو واو أو ألف أو حرف ساكن أو متحرك

NASHR:v1p227/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p227/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p227/r3.claim: The sufficiency of a stop may depend on parsing or reading: he gives examples where a following phrase is a new subject, predicate, or coordinated clause, changing the stop from sufficient to good or complete.
NASHR:v1p227/r3.anchor: وقد يكون الوقف كافيا على تفسير، أو إعراب ويكون غير كاف على آخر

NASHR:v1p227/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p227/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p227/r5.claim: A stop at hudan lil-muttaqīn is good if alladhīna is an adjective, sufficient if parsed as a raised or accusative explanation, and complete if alladhīna begins a clause predicated by ulāʾika.
NASHR:v1p227/r5.anchor: هدى للمتقين يجوز أن يكون حسنا إذا جعل الذين يؤمنون بالغيب نعتا للمتقين

NASHR:v1p234/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p234/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p234/r4.claim: Although Sajawandi forbids stopping at hudan lil-muttaqīn, the author says most leading authorities call it sufficient and permit both stopping and restarting; it remains acceptable even if alladhīna is an adjective because it ends a verse.
NASHR:v1p234/r4.anchor: واختار كثير من أئمتنا كونه كافيا، وعلى كل تقدير فيجوز الوقف عليه والابتداء بما بعده

NASHR:v1p232/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p232/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p232/r1.claim: He rejects stopping at lā rayb and restarting with fīhi hudan lil-muttaqīn: the phrase should remain together, as reinforced by the parallel lā rayba fīhi min rabb al-ʿālamīn.
NASHR:v1p232/r1.anchor: الوقف على لا ريب والابتداء فيه هدى للمتقين، وهذا يرده قوله تعالى: في سورة السجدة لا ريب فيه

NASHR:v1p232/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p232/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p232/r2.claim: Some pauses are strongly recommended to clarify intended meaning when joining the phrases could suggest a false relation; Sajawandi calls these lāzim and others call them wājib, without legal liability for omission.
NASHR:v1p232/r2.anchor: ما لو وصل طرفاه لأوهم معنى غير المراد وهذا هو الذي اصطلح عليه السجاوندي لازم وعبر عنه بعضهم بالواجب وليس معناه الواجب عند الفقهاء

NASHR:v1p235/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p235/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
NASHR:v1p235/r1.claim: Abu al-Fadl al-Khuza'i reports that Ibn Abbas prayed dawn, reciting al-Fatiha and 2:2 in the first rakʿa, then al-Fatiha and the opening of 2:3 in the second, before salām.
NASHR:v1p235/r1.anchor: أنه صلى الغداة فقرأ في الركعة الأولى بفاتحة الكتاب وب الم ذلك الكتاب لا ريب فيه هدى للمتقين وفي الثانية بفاتحة الكتاب

NASHR:v1p235/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p235/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p235/r5.claim: He disputes the prohibition on stopping at illā al-fāsiqīn on the ground that alladhīna is their adjective; the excerpt begins to reject that grammatical constraint.
NASHR:v1p235/r5.anchor: ومن ذلك إلا الفاسقين منع الوقف عليه

NASHR:v2p23/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p23/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p23/r1.claim: The established performance of most reciters assimilates nūn sākinah or tanwīn into lām and rā without ghunnah.
NASHR:v2p23/r1.anchor: هذا هو مذهب الجمهور من أهل الأداء والجلة من أئمة التجويد

NASHR:v2p23/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p23/r2.speaker: نافع، ابن كثير، أبو عمرو، ابن عامر، عاصم، أبو جعفر، يعقوب
NASHR:v2p23/r2.claim: Many performance authorities preserve ghunnah in lām and rā, reporting it from these readers and others.
NASHR:v2p23/r2.anchor: كنافع، وابن كثير، وأبي عمرو، وابن عامر، وعاصم، وأبي جعفر، ويعقوب، وغيرهم

NASHR:v2p23/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p23/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p23/r3.claim: He authenticates ghunnah with lām and rā by text and performance from Hijaz, Syria, Basra and Hafs, and says he read it from Qalun, Ibn Kathir, Hisham, Isa b. Wardan, Rawh and others.
NASHR:v2p23/r3.anchor: وقد وردت الغنة مع اللام والراء عن كل من القراء وصحت من طريق كتابنا نصا وأداء

NASHR:v2p23/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p23/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p23/r4.claim: The remaining letters nūn, mīm, wāw and yāʾ take nūn sākinah or tanwīn by assimilation with ghunnah.
NASHR:v2p23/r4.anchor: وهي حروف " ينمو " تدغم فيها النون الساكنة والتنوين بغنة

NASHR:v2p23/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p23/r5.speaker: خلف عن حمزة
NASHR:v2p23/r5.claim: Khalaf from Hamzah assimilates nūn and tanwīn into wāw and yāʾ without ghunnah.
NASHR:v2p23/r5.anchor: فأدغم خلف عن حمزة فيهما النون والتنوين بلا غنة

NASHR:v2p23/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p23/r6.speaker: الدوري عن الكسائي، أبو عثمان الضرير
NASHR:v2p23/r6.claim: The yāʾ reading differs in al-Duri from al-Kisa'i; Abu Uthman al-Darir transmits assimilation without ghunnah.
NASHR:v2p23/r6.anchor: واختلف عن الدوري عن الكسائي في الياء فروى أبو عثمان الضرير الإدغام بغير غنة

NASHR:v2p73/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p73/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p73/r1.claim: When a following consonant makes the imāla-bearing alif drop in connected recitation, both imāla forms disappear; pausing separates the consonant and restores imāla.
NASHR:v2p73/r1.anchor: فحينئذ تذهب الإمالة على نوعيها لأنها إنما كانت من أجل وجود الألف لفظا

NASHR:v2p73/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p73/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p73/r2.claim: He distinguishes madd from imāla: madd's cause, sukūn, occurs and counts, while imāla's cause, kasra, disappears and does not count.
NASHR:v2p73/r2.anchor: والفرق بين الحالين أن المد موجبه الإسكان، وقد حصل فاعتبروا الإمالة موجبها الكسر، وقد زال فلم يعتبر

NASHR:v2p73/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p73/r3.speaker: الكسائي
NASHR:v2p73/r3.claim: Al-Kisa'i pauses on huda lil-muttaqin and similar forms with yāʾ; Ibn al-Anbari says Hamzah does so likewise, and mentions readers who retain yāʾ on Ahya al-nas.
NASHR:v2p73/r3.anchor: قال الإمام أبو بكر بن الأنباري: حدثنا إدريس قال: حدثنا خلف قال: سمعت الكسائي يقف على: هدى للمتقين بالياء

NASHR:v1p237/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p237/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p237/r3.claim: Some authorities treat alternative stops as mutually exclusive: choosing one stop bars the other, including the paired stops inside this verse.
NASHR:v1p237/r3.anchor: بين الوقفين مراقبة على التضاد، فإذا وقف على أحدهما امتنع الوقف الآخر

NASHR:v1p237/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p237/r4.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
NASHR:v1p237/r4.claim: Abu al-Fadl al-Razi was the first to point out this mutual monitoring between pause locations, borrowing the idea from prosody.
NASHR:v1p237/r4.anchor: وأول من نبه على المراقبة في الوقف الإمام الأستاذ أبو الفضل الرازي

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p39#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p39#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p39#2/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses “no doubt in it” as “there is no uncertainty in it.”
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p39#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة ﴿ لا ريب فيه هدى ﴾ يقول لا شك فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r3.claim: The demonstrative ذا is two-part in form but three-part in origin; its alif is original from yāʾ, against the Kufans and al-Suhaylī, and its final element is built.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r3.anchor: ذا: اسم إشارة ثنائي الوضع لفظا، ثلاثي الأصل، لا أحادي الوضع، وألفه ليست زائدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r4.claim: Bare ذا denotes nearness, ذاك an intermediate distance, and ذلك remoteness; some grammarians instead treat any form with the address kāf or lām as remote.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r4.anchor: فإذا دخلت الكاف فقلت: ذاك دل على التوسط، فإذا أدخلت اللام فقلت: ذلك دل على البعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r5.claim: The kāf in demonstratives is an address particle that marks the addressee’s person, number, and gender, like a pronoun; demonstrative syntax is treated in grammar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r5.anchor: والكاف حرف خطاب تبين أحوال المخاطب من إفراد وتثنية وجمع وتذكير وتأنيث كما تبينها إذا كان ضميرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r6.claim: Kitāb can mean a manumission contract paid in installments, as in the Quranic reference to enslaved people seeking a contract.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r6.anchor: العقد المعروف بين العبد وسيده على مال مؤجل منجم للعتق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r7.claim: Kitāb can mean an obligation, as in the timed prayer obligation and the commands prescribing retaliation and fasting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r7.anchor: وعلى الفرض إن الصلاة كانت على

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r8.speaker: الجوهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r8.claim: Al-Jawharī gives kitāb the sense of a ruling or judgment, illustrated by deciding between two people by God’s Book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r8.anchor: وعلى الحكم، قاله الجوهري لأقضين بينكما بكتاب الله كتاب الله أحق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p56/r9.claim: Kitāb is also given the meaning of decree.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r1.claim: The poem’s “Book of God” means His decree, which brought the speaker out and away from his cousins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r1.anchor: يا ابنة عمي كتاب الله أخرجني ... عنكم وهل أمنعن الله ما فعلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r2.claim: Kitāb can denote the act of writing itself, the verbal noun of kataba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r2.anchor: وعلى مصدر كتبت تقول: كتبت كتابا وكتبا، ومنه كتاب الله عليكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r3.claim: Kitāb can mean a written object, as ḥisāb can mean what has been calculated; a poem about a letter illustrates this usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r3.anchor: وعلى المكتوب كالحساب بمعنى المحسوب، قال: بشرت عيالي إذ رأيت صحيفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r4.claim: Lā here is the negating particle; negation is one of its established functions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r4.anchor: لا نافية، والنفي أحد أقسامها، وقد تقدمت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r5.claim: Rīb means doubt accompanied by suspicion or accusation; the verb rāba can mean to establish the suspicion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r5.anchor: ريب، الريب: الشك بتهمة راب حقق التهمة قال:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r6.claim: The cited verse distinguishes true rīb from truth by associating rīb with what a liar says.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r6.anchor: ليس في الحق يا أمية ريب ... إنما الريب ما يقول الكذوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r7.claim: Rīb’s underlying sense is inner unease: the saying advises leaving what unsettles one for what does not, since doubt troubles while truth brings calm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r7.anchor: وحقيقة الريب قلق النفس: دع ما يريبك إلى ما لا يريبك، فإن الشك ريبة وإن الصدق طمأنينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r8.claim: He cites an account of someone passing a fluttering gazelle and saying that no one should cause it distress, as an example of rīb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r8.anchor: ومنه: أنه مر بظني خافق فقال لا يربه أحد بشيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r9.claim: The expression rīb al-dahr refers to the vicissitudes and afflictions of time.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r10.claim: The preposition fī can mark literal or figurative containment, accompaniment, cause, comparison, or the sense of ʿalā; the preposition bi can have similar uses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r10.anchor: في للوعاء حقيقة أو مجاز، أو زيد للمصاحبة، وللتعليل، وللمقايسة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r11.claim: He illustrates the range of fī with Quranic examples: life in retaliation, entry among earlier peoples, participation in slander, worldly and next life, palm trunks, and increase through it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r12.claim: The hāʾ in fīhi is a third-person masculine singular pronoun; Ibn Kathīr also reads it with an attached yāʾ, and its vowel variants are covered in grammar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r12.anchor: الهاء المتصلة بفي من فيه ضمير غائب مذكر مفرد، وقد يوصل بياء، وهي قراءة ابن كثير،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r13.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r13.claim: Al-Farrāʾ records huda as masculine, while Banū Asad use it as feminine and say “this is good guidance.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r13.anchor: وبنو أسد يؤنثونه، يقولون: هذه هدى حسنة، قاله الفراء في كتاب المذكر والمؤنث.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r14.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the word huda feminine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: الهدى لفظ مؤنث، وقال اللحياني: هو مذكر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r15.speaker: اللحياني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r15.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: الهدى لفظ مؤنث، وقال اللحياني: هو مذكر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r16.speaker: ابن سيده
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r16.claim: Ibn Sīda says al-hudā is also a name for daylight and cites Ibn Muqbil’s verse as evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r16.anchor: قال ابن سيده: والهدى اسم من أسماء النهار، قال ابن مقبل:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r17.claim: A grammarian’s claim that only surā, bukā, and hudā are verbal nouns on the fuʿlā pattern is incorrect; Arabic also has liqā for meeting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r17.anchor: وزعم بعض أكابر نحاتنا أنه لم يجئ من فعلى مصدر سوى هذه الثلاثة، وليس بصحيح،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r18.speaker: رضي الدين أبو عبد الله محمد بن علي بن يوسف الشاطبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r18.claim: Al-Shāṭibī told the author that Arabs used liqā for meeting, supporting another verbal noun on the fuʿlā pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p57/r18.anchor: رضي الدين أبو عبد الله محمد بن علي بن يوسف الشاطبي أن العرب قالت: لقيته لقى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r1.claim: The pattern faʿal can serve as a regular or irregular plural, a singular, a proper name, or a common name for a person, meaning, or quality; examples include hudā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r1.anchor: وفعل يكون جمعا معدولا وغير معدول، ومفردا وعلما معدولا وغير معدول، واسم جنس لشخص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r2.claim: Muttaqīn is the active participle of ittaqā, from waqā, meaning to protect or guard; iftaʿala here means to adopt a protection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r2.anchor: المتقي اسم فاعل من اتقى، وهو افتعل من وقى بمعنى حفظ وحرس، وافتعل هنا: للاتخاذ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r3.claim: Iftaʿala has twelve listed functions, including adoption, causation, reflexive action, selection, snatching, and several patterns equivalent to other verb forms; examples illustrate them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r3.anchor: وهو أحد المعاني الاثنى عشر التي جاءت لها افتعل، وهو: الاتخاذ، والتسبب، وفعل الفاعل بنفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r4.claim: In ittaqā, wāw changes to tāʾ and is then deleted after the hamzat al-waṣl, leaving taqā; this is a standard morphology topic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p58/r4.anchor: وإبدال الواو في اتقى تاء وحذفها مع همزة الوصل قبلها فيبقى تقى مذكور في علم التصريف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r6.claim: The demonstrative ذلك is a remote demonstrative; the author sees no need to reinterpret it as “this,” as some do.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r6.anchor: وذلك اسم مشار بعيد، ويصح أن يكون في قوله ذلك الكتاب على بابه فيحمل عليه ولا حاجة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r7.speaker: ابن كيسان وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r7.claim: Ibn Kaysān and others identify the demonstrative’s referent as the Quran revealed at Mecca.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r7.anchor: فالمشار إليه ما نزل بمكة من القرآن، قاله ابن كيسان وغيره،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r8.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r8.claim: ʿIkrima says the demonstrative refers to the Torah and Gospel.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r9.speaker: ابن حبيب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r9.claim: Ibn Ḥabīb identifies the referent as what is in the Preserved Tablet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r9.anchor: أو ما في اللوح المحفوظ، قاله ابن حبيب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says it is the promised book that water cannot erase and repeated recitation cannot wear out.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r10.anchor: أو ما وعد به نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم من أنه ينزل إليه كتابا لا يمحوه الماء ولا يخلق على كثرة الرد، قاله ابن عباس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r11.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r11.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib identifies it as the book promised on the day of the covenant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r11.anchor: أو الكتاب الذي وعد به يوم الميثاق، قاله عطاء بن السائب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r12.speaker: ابن رئاب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r12.claim: Ibn Riʾāb says it is the book mentioned in the Torah and Gospel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r12.anchor: أو الكتاب الذي ذكرته في التوراة والإنجيل، قاله ابن رئاب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r13.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r13.claim: Other suggestions are the Quran not yet revealed, the distant goal between sender and recipient, or the alphabet letters used in the composition challenge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r13.anchor: أو الذي لم ينزل من القرآن، أو البعد بالنسبة إلى الغاية التي بين المنزل والمنزل إليه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r14.speaker: أبو جعفر بن إبراهيم بن الزبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r14.claim: Abū Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr interprets ذلك as the path requested in al-Fātiḥa: that path is the Book; the author prefers this as referring to something already mentioned and linking the sūras.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p60#2/r14.anchor: أبا جعفر بن إبراهيم بن الزبير شيخنا يقول: ذلك إشارة إلى الصراط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r1.claim: The author chooses to parse ذلك الكتاب as a complete independent subject-and-predicate sentence, since Arabic allows it without ellipsis or dependence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r1.anchor: والذي نختاره منها أن قوله: ذلك الكتاب جملة مستقلة من مبتدأ وخبر، لأنه متى أمكن حمل الكلام على غير إضمار ولا افتقار،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r2.claim: His general method is to choose the most eloquent, least forced Arabic parsing rather than assign God’s speech every possibility accepted for poetry; alternatives are included for consideration.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r2.anchor: وهكذا تكون عادتنا في إعراب القرآن، لا نسلك فيه إلا الحمل على أحسن الوجوه، وأبعدها من التكلف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r3.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r3.claim: One parse supplies an omitted subject, “it is that Book,” with al-kitāb as adjective, apposition, or clarifying noun; another makes ذلك the subject and what follows its predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يكون ذلك خبر المبتدأ محذوف تقديره هو ذلك الكتاب، والكتاب صفة أو بدل أو عطف بيان،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r4.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r4.claim: The clause lā rayba fīhi can stand independently or serve as the predicate of the demonstrative; al-kitāb can then be an adjective, apposition, clarifier, or further predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r4.anchor: ولا ريب جملة تحتمل الاستئناف، فلا يكون لها موضع من الإعراب، وأن تكون في موضع خبر لذلك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r5.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r5.claim: With lā operating like inna, rīb is built in the accusative; Sibawayh treats the following raised element as the predicate of an underlying subject, so lā marks only its noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r5.anchor: فالمرفوع بعده على طريق الإسناد خبر لذلك المبتدأ فلم تعمل حالة البناء إلا النصب في الاسم فقط، هذا مذهب سيبويه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r6.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash instead makes the raised element the predicate of lā itself and says lā governs both accusative and nominative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r6.anchor: وأما الأخفش فذلك المرفوع خبر للا، فعملت عنده النصب والرفع،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r7.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r7.claim: The majority read rīb with fatḥa; when lā works like inna, this construction expresses comprehensive negation of every doubt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r7.anchor: وإذا عملت عمل إن أفادت الاستغراق فنفت هنا كل ريب، والفتح هو قراءة الجمهور.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r8.speaker: أبو الشعثاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r8.claim: Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ reads rīb with nominative, as does Zayd ibn ʿAlī wherever the phrase occurs; comprehensive negation is inferred from context rather than the case form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p61/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو الشعثاء: لا ريب فيه بالرفع، وكذا قراءة زيد بن علي حيث وقع، والمراد أيضا هنا الاستغراق،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r1.claim: In the nominative reading, the form itself may suggest either comprehensive negation or denial of only one instance; context makes the intended meaning comprehensive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r1.anchor: بالبناء والرفع، لكن البناء يدل بلفظه على قضية العموم، والرفع لا يدل لأنه يحتمل العموم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r2.claim: Raising rīb could make it a subject with fīhi as predicate, or let lā work like laysa; the author considers the latter analysis weak because this use of lā is rare, so he calls the reading weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r2.anchor: ورفعه على أن يكون ريب مبتدأ وفيه الخبر، وهذا ضعيف لعدم تكرار لا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r3.speaker: الزهري وابن محيصن ومسلم بن جندب وعبيد بن عمير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r3.claim: Al-Zuhrī, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Muslim ibn Jundub, and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read the hāʾ in fīhi, ilayhi, ʿalayhi, bihi, and similar forms with ḍamma, following the original vowel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r3.anchor: وقرأ الزهري، وابن محيصن، ومسلم بن جندب، وعبيد بن عمير، فيه: بضم الهاء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r4.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r4.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq reads the hāʾ with ḍamma and links it with a wāw.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق: فهو بضم الهاء ووصلها بواو،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r5.speaker: author
