ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r5.claim: Fīhi might be the predicate of lā, a predicate with its noun under Sibawayh’s analysis, an adjective with an omitted predicate, or attached to rīb by an implied verb; the last makes lā’s noun extended and declinable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r5.anchor: وجوزوا في قوله: أن يكون خبرا للا على مذهب الأخفش، وخبرا لها مع اسمها على مذهب سيبويه، أن يكون صفة والخبر محذوف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r6.claim: He chooses an omitted predicate for lā because the predicate is often suppressed when understood, especially in Hijazi usage; it is clear here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r6.anchor: والذي نختاره أن الخبر محذوف لأن الخبر في باب لا العاملة عمل إن إذا علم لم تلفظ به بنو تميم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r7.claim: Idghām of the bāʾ in lā rayb into the fāʾ of fīhi is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr, though clear articulation is the famous reading; al-Yazīdī transmits that articulation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r7.anchor: وإدغام الباء من لا ريب في فاء فيه مروي عن أبي عمرو، والمشهور عنه الإظهار، وهي رواية اليزيدي عنه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الطباع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r8.claim: The author says he read both assimilation and clear articulation from Abū ʿAmr with Abū Jaʿfar ibn al-Ṭabbāʿ in al-Andalus.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r8.anchor: وقد قرأته بالوجهين على الأستاذ أبي جعفر بن الطباع بالأندلس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r9.claim: Negating rīb denies that doubt belongs to or can characterize the Book; it does not deny that people have in fact doubted it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p62/r9.anchor: ونفي الريب يدل على نفي الماهية، أي ليس مما يحله الريب ولا يكون فيه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r1.claim: There is no contradiction with “if you are in doubt”: the addressed people may be in doubt, while doubt is denied of the Book itself because the context and subject differ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r1.anchor: لاختلاف الحال والمحل، فالحال هناك المخاطبون، والريب هو المحل، والحال هنا منفي، والمحل الكتاب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r2.claim: He rejects unnecessary qualifications that the Book has no doubt only for its speaker or believers, or that an omitted “cause of doubt” is intended; the wording needs no such additions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r2.anchor: وقد قيد بعضهم الريب فقال: لا ريب فيه عند المتكلم به، وقيل هو عموم يراد به الخصوص،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes fīhi as the predicate and asks why the ظرف precedes rīb, comparing it with “no ghawl in them.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r3.anchor: واختيار الزمخشري أن فيه خبر، وبذلك بنى عليه سؤالا وهو أن قال: هلا قدم الظرف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī answers that fronting fīhi suggests other books contain doubt, just as the wine verse contrasts paradise wine with worldly wine that harms the mind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r4.anchor: وأجاب: بأن التقديم يشعر بما يبعد عن المراد، وهو أن كتابا غيره فيه الريب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r5.claim: The author says al-Zamakhsharī shifts from an argument about fronted objects to one about fronted predicates and sees no difference between the two word orders he compares.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r5.anchor: وقد انتقل الزمخشري من دعوى الاختصاص بتقديم المفعول إلى دعواه بتقديم الخبر، ولا نعلم أحدا يفرق بين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r6.claim: Al-ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada’s verse describes worldly wine as easing headache without causing the drinker to reel, illustrating the contrast invoked in the discussion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r6.anchor: تشفي الصداع ولا يؤذيك طالبها ... ولا يخالطها في الرأس تدويم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r7.claim: He considers it far-fetched to construe the declarative “there is no doubt” as a prohibition meaning “do not doubt.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r7.anchor: وأبعد من ذهب إلى أن قوله: لا ريب صيغة خبر ومعناه النهي عن الريب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r8.claim: Huda may be nominative as a subject with fīhi as predicate, an omitted subject’s predicate, a predicate with an omitted fī, or an additional predicate in the clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r8.anchor: وجوزوا في قوله تعالى: هدى للمتقين أن يكون هدى في موضع رفع على أنه مبتدأ،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r9.claim: Huda may also be accusative as a circumstantial accusative, with the demonstrative or al-kitāb as its referent; he notes a difficulty because a state normally qualifies the absence of doubt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r9.anchor: أو في موضع نصب على الحال، وبولغ بجعل المصدر حالا وصاحب الحال اسم الإشارة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r10.claim: The difficulty with a circumstantial reading is eased if the state is understood as a constant, inseparable quality.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p63/r10.anchor: لكن يزيل الإشكال أنها حال لازمة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r1.claim: He prefers three independent but closely connected clauses: the referent is the complete Book, no doubt is in it, and it contains guidance for the God-fearing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r1.anchor: والأولى: جعل كل جملة مستقلة، فذلك الكتاب جملة، ولا ريب جملة، وفيه هدى للمتقين جملة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r2.claim: The first clause identifies the referent as the complete Book, as in calling someone “the man” to mean the one complete in his qualities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r2.anchor: فالأولى أخبرت بأن المشار إليه هو الكتاب الكامل، كما تقول: زيد الرجل، أي الكامل في الأوصاف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r3.claim: The second clause characterizes the Book as having no kind of doubt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r3.anchor: والثانية نعت لا يكون شيء ما من ريب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r4.claim: The third clause says the Book contains guidance for the God-fearing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r4.anchor: والثالثة أخبرت أن فيه الهدى للمتقين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r5.claim: One figurative reading makes “in it is guidance” mean continuing guidance, since the God-fearing are already guided; he compares it with the prayer “guide us to the path.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r5.anchor: والمجاز إما في فيه هدى، أي استمرار هدى لأن المتقين مهتدون فصار نظير اهدنا الصراط،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r6.claim: Alternatively, al-muttaqīn means those on the verge of acquiring piety, as in the cited poetic phrase about a dead man from Tamīm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r6.anchor: وإما في المتقين أي المشارفين لاكتساب التقوى، كقوله: إذا ما مات ميت من تميم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r7.claim: In religious law, a muttaqī guards himself against acts or omissions threatened with punishment; scholars disagree whether piety also requires avoiding minor sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r7.anchor: والمتقي في الشريعة هو الذي يقي نفسه أن يتعاطى ما توعد عليه بعقوبة من فعل أو ترك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r8.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r8.claim: Some supply “and disbelievers” after “for the God-fearing,” with the latter named alone to honor them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r8.anchor: وجوز بعضهم أن يكون التقدير هدى للمتقين والكافرين، فحذف لدلالة أحد الفريقين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r9.claim: The passage calls the revealed Book the fullest of books and the way leading to God; because it contains all things, no book is more complete, and it has neither doubt nor lack of guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r9.anchor: الإخبار عن المشار إليه الذي هو الطريق الموصل إلى الله تعالى، هو الكتاب أي الكامل في الكتب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r10.claim: He links the Book’s completeness to “We have neglected nothing in the Book,” reasoning that a book containing all things cannot be surpassed in completeness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r10.anchor: الذي قال فيه ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r11.claim: The first clause is complete and literal; the second uses ellipsis by omitting lā’s predicate, while the third pictures meaning as a physical container with guidance inside.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r11.anchor: ففي الآية الأولى الإتيان بالجملة كاملة الأجزاء حقيقة لا مجاز فيها، وفي الثانية مجازا لحذف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r12.claim: The preposition fī makes the Book a container and guidance its contents, treating an abstract meaning like a physical object inside a house.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p64/r12.anchor: إذ جعل القرآن ظرفا والهدى مظروفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p73/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p73/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p73/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and a group say the opening verses, from alif-lām-mīm through al-mufliḥūn, concern believing People of the Book specifically.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p73/r4.anchor: أحدها: أنها نزلت في مؤمني أهل الكتاب دون غيرهم، وهو قول ابن عباس وجماعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p73/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p73/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p73/r5.claim: Mujāhid says the opening verses concern all believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p73/r5.anchor: الثاني: نزلت في جميع المؤمنين، قاله مجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p74/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p74/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p74/r1.claim: The lām in dhālika signals the distant, elevated rank of the Book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p74/r1.anchor: الإشارة في قوله ذلك أدخل اللام إشارة إلى بعد المنازل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p74/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p74/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p74/r2.claim: The declarative form lā rayba fīhi functions as a command in meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p74/r2.anchor: معدول الخطاب في قوله تعالى: لا ريب فيه صيغته خبر ومعناه أمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p74/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p74/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p74/r3.claim: Hudan lil-muttaqīn expresses exclusivity of guidance for the God-fearing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p74/r3.anchor: الاختصاص هو في قوله هدى للمتقين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r1.claim: The opening may be a new independent sentence or connected to what precedes; al-Ālūsī favors the soundest Arabic reading with least strain.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r1.anchor: جملة مستأنفة وابتداء كلام أو متعلقة بما قبلها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r2.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r2.claim: Al-Wāḥidī takes “that” as the Book promised to Muḥammad in 73:5.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r2.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى الكتاب الموعود به صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بقوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r3.claim: Another proposed referent is the Book promised through Moses and Jesus, with the earlier community’s expectation in 2:89 offered as support.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r3.anchor: أو على لسان موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام لقوله تعالى : ( وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r4.speaker: كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r4.claim: Kaʿb urges adherence to the Qur’an as intellect’s understanding, wisdom’s light, and knowledge’s springs.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r4.anchor: ما روي عن كعب عليكم بالقرآن فإنه فهم العقل ونور الحكمة وينابيع العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r5.speaker: كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r5.claim: The same report calls the Qur’an the newest book in covenant with God and quotes the Torah’s promise of a new revelation to Muḥammad that opens blind eyes, deaf ears, and closed hearts.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r5.anchor: وقال في التوراة يامحمد إني منزل عليك توراة حديثة تفتح بها أعينا عميا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r6.claim: The demonstrative may point to the Qur’an before its audience, with distance expressing exalted rank; al-Sakkākī’s explanation is preferred.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r6.anchor: والإشارة بذلك للتعظيم وتنزيل البعد الرتبي منزلة البعد الحقيقي كما في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r7.claim: A possible explanation is that revelation became “that” once it descended from the divine presence and was conveyed to people, as something separated from its source.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r7.anchor: أو لأنه لما نزل عن حضرة الربوبية وصار بحضرتنا بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r8.claim: A poet’s maxim that whatever is not in one’s hand is distant supports the separation-based explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r8.anchor: كل ما ليس في يديك بعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r9.speaker: السهيلي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r9.claim: Al-Suhaylī explains the contrast with 6:92’s “this Book” by the different settings, including the opening disjointed letters in this sūra.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r9.anchor: حروف التهجي في الأول وهي تقطع بها الحروف وهو لا يكون إلا في حقنا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r10.claim: A far-fetched explanation treats the Qur’an as a transient utterance: each part vanishes as it is produced and so is distant from the senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r10.anchor: القرآن لفظ وهو من قبيل الأعراض السيالة الغير القارة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r11.speaker: الجرجاني
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r11.claim: Al-Jurjānī transmits a group’s view that near and far demonstratives can alternate, citing Qur’anic examples from the story of Jesus.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r12.claim: The cited verse may use “that” for someone famous or previously spoken of, so the poem does not prove that a far form simply means “this.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r12.anchor: أقول له والرمح يأطر متنه تأمل خفافا إنني أنا ذلكا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r13.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r13.claim: Al-Rāzī’s claim that “that” is distant by convention but not by linguistic form conflicts with what Arabic grammar authorities teach.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r13.anchor: وقول الإمام الرازي إن ذلك للبعيد عرفا لا وضعا فحمله هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r14.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r14.claim: Al-ʿIkrima’s identification with the Torah and Gospel is acceptable only if supported by an authentic report; otherwise al-Ālūsī rejects it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r14.anchor: والقول بأن الإشارة إلى التوراة والإنجيل كما نقل عن عكرمة إن كان قد ورد فيه حديث صحيح قبلناه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r15.claim: A highly unusual view makes “that” the straight path requested in al-Fātiḥa and thereby links al-Baqara to it; al-Ālūsī calls this far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r15.anchor: وأغرب ما رأيناه في توجيه الإشارة أنها إلى الصراط المستقيم في الفاتحة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r16.claim: Al-Ālūsī’s preferred referent is the Qur’an, with rank-distance as in al-Sakkākī’s account and the radiance of nearness still apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r16.anchor: والذي تنفتح له الآذان أنه إشارة إلى القرآن ووجه البعد ما ذكره صاحب المفتاح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r17.claim: Demonstratives normally indicate sensory objects; for the imperceptible or an unseen perceptible thing, they make it present as though witnessed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r17.anchor: والمعتبر في أسماء الإشارة هو الإشارة الحسية التي لا يتصور تعلقها إلا بمحسوس مشاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r18.speaker: الرضي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r18.claim: Al-Raḍī describes this treatment of unseen referents as making rational indication stand in place of sensory indication.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r18.anchor: وتنزيل الإشارة العقلية منزلة الحسية كما في الرضى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r19.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r19.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that a demonstrative need not refer to something perceptible whenever it has an adjectival modifier.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p105/r19.anchor: وقول بعضهم أن اسم الإشارة إذا كان معه صفة له لم يلزم أن يكون محسوسا وهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r1.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib traces “book” to joining one piece of leather to another by sewing; ordinary writing joins letters.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r1.anchor: قال الراغب ضم أديم إلى أديم بالخياطة وفي المتعارف ضم الحروف بعضها إلى بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r2.claim: Writing originally orders letters in script; “book” can also name anything conjoined in speech, and the terms are metaphorically exchanged.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r2.anchor: والأصل في الكتابة النظم بالخط وقد يقال ذلك للمضموم وبعضه إلى بعض باللفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r3.claim: The Qur’an is called God’s Book even though it is not a physical written book, since “book” extends to composed revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r3.anchor: ولذا سمى كتاب الله وإن لم يكن كتابا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r4.claim: “Book” can remain a verbal noun used for its object emphatically, or mean the object itself; it names the Qur’an’s composed utterance before script records it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r4.anchor: والكتاب هنا إما باق على المصدرية وسمى به المفعول للمبالغة أو هو بمعنى المفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r5.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r5.claim: The proposed derivations from collecting things, gathering troops, repelling doubts, containing all knowledge, or assembling duties are a fabricated explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r5.anchor: وقول الإمامإن اشتقاق الكتاب من كتبت الشيء إذا جمعته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r6.claim: The article in “the Book” is generic and marks the Qur’an as the perfect book deserving the name above other heavenly books.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r6.anchor: واللام في الكتاب للحقيقة مثلها في أنت الرجل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r7.speaker: ابن عصفور
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṣfūr says the article after a demonstrative, in a vocative with ayy, and after sudden idhā is presentational and referential.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r7.anchor: كل لام وقعت بعد اسم الإشارة وأي في النداء وإذا الفجائية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r8.claim: A variant reading is reported as “tanẓīl al-kitāb.”

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r9.claim: Rayb originally names the unease a thing causes, then extends to troubling events and inner stirrings such as anger.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r9.anchor: والريب الشك وأصله مصدر رابني الشيء إذا حصل فيك الريبة وهي قلق النفس

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r10.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r10.claim: Al-Rāzī explains temporal calamities and inner agitation as forms of doubt because they are uncertain; al-Ālūsī rejects this derivation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r10.anchor: وقول الإمام الرازي : إن هذين قد يرجعان إلى معنى الشك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r11.speaker: أبو زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r11.claim: Abū Zayd distinguishes rābanī, when one is certain of a troubling matter, from arābanī, when one suspects it without certainty.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r11.anchor: وفرق أبو زيد بين رابني وأرابني فيقال رابني من فلان أمر إذا كنت مستيقنا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r12.speaker: بشار
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r12.claim: Bashshār’s verse witnesses the distinction: a friend says “I only suspected” when the matter is doubted, but speaks directly when certain.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r12.anchor: أخوك الذي إن ربته قال إنما أراب وإن عاتبته لان جانبه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r13.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r13.claim: Some lexicographers distinguish rayb from ordinary doubt by adding an element of accusation or suspicion.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r13.anchor: وبعض فرق بين الريب والشك بأن الريب شك مع تهمة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r14.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r14.claim: Al-Rāghib defines doubt as equal hesitation between two alternatives without a preponderating sign.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r14.anchor: وقال الراغب : الشك وقوف النفس بين شيئين متقابلين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r15.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r15.claim: Al-Rāghib derives mirya from rubbing an udder to draw milk and uses it for hesitation that seeks an indication.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r15.anchor: والمرية التردد في المتقابلين وطلب الأمارة من مري الضرع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r16.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r16.claim: For al-Rāghib, rayb is imagining something about an object, then finding that the suspicion was mistaken.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106/r16.anchor: والريب أن يتوهم في الشيء ثم ينكشف عما توهم فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r1.speaker: الجولي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r1.claim: Al-Jūlī distinguishes doubt, which may fall short of decisive clarity, from rayb, which has some appearance but not certainty.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r1.anchor: وقال الجولي : يقال الشك لما استوى فيه الاعتقاد أن أو لم يستويا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r2.claim: The phrasing is apt because rayb falls short of certainty while showing itself somewhat; negating rayb therefore rules out even lesser uncertainty.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r2.anchor: حسن هنا ( لا ريب فيه ) للإشارة إلى أنه لا يحصل فيه ريب فضلا عن شك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r3.claim: Despite many who doubt it, the Qur’an’s elevated rank and manifest proof leave no rational person in doubt after reflection that it is revelation from God.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r3.anchor: ونفى سبحانه الريب فيه مع كثرة المرتابين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r4.claim: One explanation supplies an omitted “cause”: the Qur’an contains none of the obscurity, complexity, contradiction, or unsupported claims that cause doubt.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r4.anchor: وقيل إنه على الحذف كأنه قال لا سبب ريب فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r5.claim: Another reading takes the declarative form as a prohibition: “Do not doubt it,” by analogy with the prohibition in 2:197.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r5.anchor: وقيل معناه النهي وإن كان لفظه خبرا أي لا ترتابوا فيه على حد ( لا رفث ولا فسوق )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r6.claim: A syntactic option makes “in it” an adjective of “doubt” and “for the godfearing” the predicate: no doubt in it for them.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r7.claim: On another parse, “guidance” is a circumstantial accusative from the pronoun in “in it,” describing the Book as guiding while free of doubt.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r7.anchor: حال من الضمير المجرور أي لا ريب كائنا فيه للمتقين حال كونه هاديا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r8.claim: On the author’s parse, lā negates the noun’s predicate quality, not a restricted subset of the noun, preserving comprehensive negation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r8.anchor: لنفي اتصاف الاسم بالخبر لا لنفي قيد الاسم فلا تتوجه إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says fronting “in it” avoids suggesting that this Book lacks a defect found in other books, unlike 37:47’s contrast with worldly wine.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r9.anchor: وإنما لم يقل سبحانه لا فيه ريب على حد ( لا فيها غول )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r10.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān denies that fronting the predicate here conveys exclusivity; al-Ālūsī dismisses that objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r10.anchor: حتى أنكر أبو حيان إفادة تقديم الخبر هنا الحصر وهو مما لا يلتفت إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r11.speaker: سليم أبو الشعثاء
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r11.claim: Sulaym Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ reads raybun in the nominative; negating one instance differs from the common reading’s comprehensive negation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ سليم أبو الشعثاء لا ريب فيه بالرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r12.claim: In the common reading, lā negates all instances of doubt rather than merely denying that doubt is universal.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r12.anchor: فلا لعموم النفي لا لنفي العموم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r13.claim: Most readers pause after “in it,” making the Book itself the guidance, a usage repeated elsewhere in the Qur’an.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r13.anchor: والوقف على ( فيه ) هو المشهور وعليه يكون الكتاب نفسه هدى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r14.speaker: نافع وعاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r14.claim: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim pause after “no doubt,” treating the predicate as omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r14.anchor: وعن نافع وعاصم الوقف على ( لا ريب ) ولا ريب في حذف الخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r15.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r15.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets lā rayb as “truly” and treats the pause after it as complete, though al-Ālūsī ranks this below the common pause.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r15.anchor: وذهب الزجاج إلى جعل ( لا ريب ) بمعنى حقا فالوقف عليه تام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r16.speaker: ابن كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r16.claim: Ibn Kathīr links the pronominal hāʾ to a preceding silent yāʾ; when preceded by another silent consonant it is linked with wāw.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r16.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير فيهي بوصل الهاء ياء في اللفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r17.speaker: حفص
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r17.claim: Ḥafṣ agrees with the linked hāʾ in “fīhi muhānan,” “mulāqīhi,” and “sa-uṣlīhi.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r17.anchor: ووافقه حفص في ( فيه مهانا ) وملاقيه وسأصليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r18.speaker: الزهري وابن جندب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r18.claim: Al-Zuhrī and Ibn Jundub read pronominal hāʾs with ḍamma throughout the Qur’an, following the original form.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r18.anchor: وقرأ الزهري وابن جندب بضم الهاء من الكنايات في جميع القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r19.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r19.claim: Hudā is originally a verbal noun or a substitute for one; Sibawayh counts fuʿal as a rare verbal-noun pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p106#2/r19.anchor: والهدى ( في الأصل مصدر هدى أو عوض عن المصدر وكل في كلام سيبويه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r1.speaker: الشاطبي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r1.claim: Al-Shāṭibī cites poetry to illustrate the rare verbal-noun pattern with the word liqā.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r1.anchor: الشاطبي وأنشد : وقد زعموا حلما لقاك فلم أزد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r2.claim: Here hudā functions as an active participle through a familiar nominal usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r2.anchor: والمراد منه هنا اسم الفاعل بأحد الوجوه المعروفة في أمثاله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats hudā as feminine in gender.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r3.anchor: وهو لفظ مؤنث عند ابن عطية ومذكر عند اللحياني

ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r4.speaker: اللحياني والفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r4.claim: Al-Liḥyānī treats hudā as masculine, while Banū Asad use it as feminine according to al-Farrāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r4.anchor: ومذكر عند اللحياني وبنو أسد يؤنثون كما قال الفراء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī defines guidance as direction that actually brings its recipient to the desired goal.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r5.anchor: وفي الكشاف هي الدلالة الموصلة إلى البغية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that guidance reaches the goal because it is opposed to misguidance, which is failure to reach it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r6.anchor: واستدل عليه بثلاثة وجوه الأول وقوع الضلال في مقابله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r7.claim: He also argues that “guided” is praise like “rightly guided”; mere instruction without attaining the path does not earn that description.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r7.anchor: والثاني أنه يقال مهدي في موضع المدح كمهتد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r8.claim: His third argument is that ihtadā is the mutāwaʿ form of hadā, supposedly carrying the base verb’s meaning as “broke” carries into “became broken.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r8.anchor: والثالث أن اهتدى مطاوع هدى ولن يكون المطاوع في خلاف معنى أصله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that the first contrast concerns intransitive guidance or being guided; transitive guidance is opposed by leading astray, so the contrast proves no lexical arrival.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r9.anchor: أما أولا فلأن المذكور في مقابلة الضلالة هو الهدى اللازم بمعنى الاهتداء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r10.claim: Even if misguidance means failure to reach, that is only a possible consequence; it does not establish arrival as part of the meaning of guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r10.anchor: بل هو العدول عن الطريق الموصل إلى البغية فيكون الهدى عبارة عن الدلالة على الطريق الموصل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r11.claim: The fact that “guided” is usually said only of one who has attained the goal can reflect common usage, not the lexical meaning of guidance itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r11.anchor: وأما ثانيا فلأنا لا نسلم أن الضلالة عبارة عن الخيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r12.claim: The verb ihtadā need not be a true mutāwaʿ of hadā; it can describe the recipient’s separate action of following the path after being shown it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r12.anchor: وأما رابعا فلأنا لا نسلم أن اهتدى مطاوع هدى بل هو من قبيل أمره فأتمر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r13.claim: The phrase hadāhu fa-ihtadā means that he showed him the road and the recipient then travelled it; “He guided him but he did not follow” is possible.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p107/r13.anchor: بدليل أنه يقال هداه فلم يهتد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r1.claim: The existence of an action does not always entail its mutāwaʿ; in the Mukhtār agreement is unnecessary, while other verb classes require it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r1.anchor: قالوا : لا يلزم من وجود الفعل وجود مطاوعه مطلقا ففي المختار لا يجب أن يوافق المطاوع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r2.claim: The Qur’an says God sends signs for warning but that warning may increase people’s defiance rather than produce fear, showing that an action’s effect may fail.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r2.anchor: مع قوله سبحانه ( ونخوفهم فما يزيدهم إلا طغيانا )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r3.claim: The difference between mutāwaʿ verbs that must or need not match their base verb is treated at length in ʿUrūs al-afrāḥ.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r3.anchor: والفرق بينهما مفصل في عروس الأفراح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r4.claim: Qur’anic uses of guidance without arrival at the goal challenge al-Zamakhsharī’s definition of guidance as necessarily reaching the goal.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r4.anchor: ليس فيه وصول إلى البغية وقد مر بعضه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r5.claim: Scholars variously hold that guidance literally means general direction and figuratively means successful direction, the reverse, both by homonymy, or a shared common sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r5.anchor: ولهذا اختلفوا هل هي حقيقة في الدلالة المطلقة مجاز في غيرها أو بالعكس

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r6.claim: The passage records competing attributions of the two definitions to Ashʿarites and Muʿtazilites, while noting that the popular attribution reverses them.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r6.anchor: والمذكور في كلام الأشاعرة أن المختار عندهم ما ذكر في الكشاف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r7.claim: The proposed reconciliation assigns the Ashʿarite definition to technical religious usage and the popular definition to ordinary language, but al-Ālūsī argues it should be reversed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r7.anchor: والتوفيق بأن كلام الأشاعرة في المعنى الشرعي والمشهور مبني على المعنى اللغوي أو العرفي يخدشه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī’s final position is that guidance covers both meanings and preventing destruction, resolving much of the dispute.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r8.anchor: والحق عند أهل الحق أن الهداية مشتركة بين المعنيين المذكورين وعدم الإهلاك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r9.claim: Muttaqīn is the plural active participle of ittaqā; its root begins with wāw, and the tāʾ belongs to the derived form.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r9.anchor: والمتقين ( جمع متق اسم فاعل من وقاه فأتقى فقاؤه واو لا تاء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r10.claim: Wiqāya means protection generally; in religious usage taqwā is protecting oneself from what harms in the afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r10.anchor: والوقاية لغة الصيانة مطلقا وشرعا صيانة المرء نفسه عما يضر في الآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r11.claim: The first level of taqwā is avoiding association with God.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r11.anchor: فأولاها التوقي عن الشرك والثانية عن الكبائر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r12.claim: The second level is avoiding major sins, including persistence in minor sins.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r13.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r13.claim: A report transmitted by al-Tirmidhī from the Prophet says a servant does not reach taqwā until leaving harmless things out of caution against harmful ones; al-Ālūsī gives no grading.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r13.anchor: ما رواه الترمذي عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يبلغ العبد أن يكون من المتقين حتى يدع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r14.claim: The third level therefore includes avoiding minor sins as well as the doubtful, out of caution.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r14.anchor: وفي هذه المرتبة يعتبر ترك الصغائر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r15.claim: A poem defines the wary person as one who leaves both major and minor sins, careful even of small dangers.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r15.anchor: خل الذنوب كبيرها وصغيرها فهو التقي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r16.claim: One definition of taqwā is that God does not find a person where He forbade him and does not miss him where He commanded him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r16.anchor: التقوى أن لا يراك الله حيث نهاك ولا يفقدك حيث أمرك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r17.claim: Other definitions are disavowing one’s own power and avoiding anything that distracts the heart’s innermost self from God.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r17.anchor: التبري عن الحول والقوة وقيل : التنزه عن كل ما يشغل السر عن الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r18.claim: A Sufi poet says that even a momentary thought of desiring anything besides God would make him judge himself an apostate.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r18.anchor: ولو خطرت لي في سواك إرادة على خاطري سهوا حكمت بردتي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r19.claim: The Book’s guidance encompasses people at all levels of taqwā.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r19.anchor: وهداية الكتاب المبين شاملة لأرباب هذه المراتب أجمعين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r20.claim: If guidance means bringing people to the first level, “the godfearing” can mean those approaching it, a prospective metaphor used concisely to honor God’s allies.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r20.anchor: فإن أريد بكونه ( هدى للمتقين ) إرشاده إياهم إلى تحصيل المرتبة الأولى فالمراد بهم المشارفون مجازا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r21.claim: The prospective reading suits the sūra’s opening praise of God’s allies; the following description of believers can refer to the time the guidance relation is established.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r21.anchor: وإيثاره على العبارة المعربة عن ذلك للإيجاز وتصدير السورة الكريمة بذكر أوليائه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r22.claim: Reading the whole phrase as a direct answer to “who are the godfearing?” and making all its referents prospective is rejected as contrary to the flow.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r22.anchor: وحمل الكل على المشارفة يأباه السوق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r23.claim: If the Book guides one rank upward, the expression is literal when the godfearing are at the lower rank and figurative when they already occupy the target rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r23.anchor: فإن عني بالمتقين أصحاب المرتبة الأولى تعينت الحقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r24.claim: Likewise, if guidance is toward the third level, calling people at the second level godfearing is literal; calling those already at the third level so makes guidance figurative.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p108/r24.anchor: فإن أريد بالهدى الإرشاد إلى تحصيل المرتبة الثالثة فإن عني بالمتقين أصحاب المرتبة الثانية تعينت الحقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r1.speaker: مولانا مفتي الديار الرومية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r1.claim: When guidance would advance people already at the highest rank, the guidance is figurative while “godfearing” remains literal, according to the Ottoman mufti.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r1.anchor: كذا حققه مولانا مفتي الديار الرومية ومنه يعلم اندفاع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r2.speaker: مولانا مفتي الديار الرومية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r2.claim: The mufti answers the objection that guidance for the already guided is tautological, whether guidance is defined as arrival or direction.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r2.anchor: ومنه يعلم اندفاع ما قيل أن الهداية إن فسرت بالدلالة الموصلة يقتضي أن يكون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r3.claim: Another investigator says no metaphor is needed: as a weapon is protection for the protected and wealth is richness for the rich, the Book truly guides those already guided.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r3.anchor: إذا قيل السلاح عصمة للمعتصم والمال غنى للغني

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r4.claim: For derived predicates, the relevant time is when the relation is asserted, according to the established view of the precise scholars.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r4.anchor: والذي عليه المحققون أنه زمان النسبة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r5.speaker: السبكي والكرماني
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r5.claim: Al-Subkī and al-Kirmānī hold that “whoever kills a man gets his spoils” is literal, rejecting the claim that the derived predicate is figurative.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r5.anchor: وقد ذهب السبكي والكرماني إلى أن من قتل قتيلا فله سلبه حقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r6.claim: The killer example is meaningful because a contextual cue makes the claim exclusive: the killing was done by this person rather than another.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r6.anchor: فكأنه قيل لم يشاركه فيه غيره فسلبه له دون غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r7.claim: With a demonstrative such as “I squeezed this wine,” the relevant time for whether the description is literal is the time of pointing, not the earlier judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r7.anchor: والمعتبر زمان الإشارة لا زمان الحكم السابق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r8.claim: The Qur’an remains guidance despite containing ambiguous and difficult passages, since guidance need not be supplied by every individual part.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r8.anchor: ثم لا يقدح في كونه هدى ما فيه من المجمل والمتشابه لأنه لا يستلزم كونه هدى هدايته باعتبار كل جزء منه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r9.claim: Alternatively, the ambiguous material does not lack an explanation of its intent; on the Shāfiʿī view it guides once clarified.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r9.anchor: أو لأن ذلك لا ينفك عن بيان المراد منه كما ذهب إليه الشافعية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r10.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r10.claim: Al-Rāzī argues that the Qur’an cannot guide to truths on which its own authority depends, such as God’s existence and attributes and proof of prophecy, lest circularity follow.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r10.anchor: فقد نص الإمام على أنه كل ما يتوقف صحة كون القرآن حجة على صحته لا يكون القرآن هدى فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r11.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r11.claim: Some scholars hold that reflection on the Qur’an’s rational proofs can guide even to knowledge of God; 2:185 is cited in support.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r11.anchor: وبعض صحح أن القرآن في نفسه هدى في كل شيء حتى معرفة الله تعالى لمن تأمل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r12.claim: Mentioning only the godfearing praises those who benefit from the Qur’an’s guidance, just as 79:45 singles out those who fear the Hour though the Prophet warns everyone.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r12.anchor: ويكون الاقتصار على المتقين هنا بناء على تفسيرنا الهداية مدحا لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r13.claim: Those who do not believe remain outside its benefit: 17:45 describes a veiled barrier and 17:82 says it increases wrongdoers only in loss.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r13.anchor: وإذا قرأت القرآن جعلنا بينك وبين الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة حجابا مستورا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r14.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects supplying an omitted “and disbelievers” after “godfearing,” by analogy with the verse about garments protecting from heat.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r14.anchor: هدى للمتقين والكافرين فحذف لدلالة المتقين على حد ( سرابيل تقيكم الحر )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r15.claim: The opening’s clauses cohere: the disjointed letters gesture, “that Book” confirms its uniqueness, “no doubt” confirms one pillar, and guidance confirms the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r15.anchor: ( الم ) أشارت إلى ما أشارت و ( ذلك الكتاب ) قررت بعض إشارتها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r16.claim: One rhetorical reconstruction answers why the Qur’an is miraculous: it is fully excellent in wording and meaning, which makes it the complete Book.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r16.anchor: وقيل : بالحمل على الاستئناف كأنه سئل ما باله صار معجزا فأجيب بأنه كامل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r17.claim: In that reconstruction, “no doubt” answers why this alone deserves the title of complete Book, and “guidance” supplies proof through its religious and worldly benefits.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r17.anchor: ثم سئل عن مقتضى الاختصاص بكونه هو الكتاب الكامل فأجيب بأنه لا يحوم حوله ريب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r18.claim: The Qur’an’s inimitability entails its perfection; eloquent perfection removes doubt about its truth, which in turn makes it guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r18.anchor: وقد يقال الإعجاز مستلزم غاية الكمال وغاية كمال الكلام البليغ ببعده من الريب والشبه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r19.claim: If the clauses’ meanings converge, the second confirms the first; if the first entails the next, it functions like a badal of inclusion, and omission of conjunction signals their tight bond.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p109/r19.anchor: فإن نظر إلى اتحاد المعاني بحسب المآل كان الثاني مقررا للأول فلذا ترك العطف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r1.claim: “That Book” means this Book, the Quran.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {ذلك الكتاب} أي هذا الكتاب وهو القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r2.claim: An alternative supplies an omitted phrase: “this is that Book.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r2.anchor: وقيل: هذا فيه مضمر أي هذا ذلك الكتاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r3.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says God had promised the Prophet in the Torah, Gospel, and through earlier prophets a Book that water could not erase and repeated recitation could not wear out; the Quran is that promised Book.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: كان الله قد وعد نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن ينزل عليه كتابا لا يمحوه الماء، ولا يخلق عن كثرة الرد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r4.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains “this” as indicating nearness and “that” as indicating distance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r4.anchor: أنزله عليك في التوراة والإنجيل وعلى لسان النبيين من قبلك "وهذا" للتقريب "وذلك" للتبعيد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r5.speaker: ابن كيسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r5.claim: Ibn Kaysān takes “that Book” to mean the surahs preceding al-Baqara, which the polytheists had rejected and which contain no doubt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r5.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: إن الله تعالى أنزل قبل سورة البقرة سورا كذب بها المشركون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r6.claim: Kitāb is a verbal noun used to mean something written, as khalq can mean something created and ḍarb a thing struck by someone.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r6.anchor: والكتاب مصدر وهو بمعنى المكتوب كما يقال للمخلوق خلق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r7.claim: The root sense of kitāb is joining and gathering; a troop is called a katība because its members gather, and a book joins letter to letter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#3/r7.anchor: وأصل الكتب: الضم والجمع، ويقال للجند: كتيبة لاجتماعها، وسمي الكتاب كتابا لأنه جمع حرف إلى حرف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r1.claim: There is no doubt that the Quran is from God and is the truth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {لا ريب فيه} أي لا شك فيه أنه من عند الله عز وجل وأنه الحق والصدق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r2.claim: An alternative reads the statement as a prohibition: “Do not doubt it,” like the prohibition in 2:197 against indecent conduct and disobedience.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r2.anchor: وقيل هو خبر بمعنى النهي أي لا ترتابوا فيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir lengthens the pronominal hāʾ in connected recitation when preceded by a consonant and not followed by another consonant; after yāʾ he lengthens with kasra, otherwise with ḍamma, and Ḥafṣ agrees at 25:69.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير: فيه بالإشباع في الوصل وكذلك كل هاء كناية قبلها ساكن يشبعها وصلا ما لم يلقها ساكن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r4.claim: These readers assimilate ghunna before lām and rā; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī add yāʾ, and Ḥamza adds wāw, while the others do not assimilate it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r4.anchor: يدغم الغنة عند اللام والراء أبو جعفر وابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r5.claim: Abū Jaʿfar conceals nūn and tanwīn before khāʾ and ghayn.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r5.anchor: ويخفي أبو جعفر النون والتنوين عند الخاء والغين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r6.claim: The Quran is guidance: right direction and clarification for people of piety; here “the pious” means believers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r6.anchor: أي هو هدى أي رشد وبيان لأهل التقوى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r7.claim: One analysis makes hudan an accusative circumstantial expression meaning “guiding,” with the sense that there is no doubt in its guidance to the pious.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r7.anchor: وقيل هو نصب على الحال أي هاديا تقديره لا ريب في هدايته للمتقين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas defines the pious as those who guard themselves against idolatry, major sins, and indecencies.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: المتقي من يتقي الشرك والكبائر والفواحش

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r9.claim: Taqwā derives from guarding or placing a barrier between two things; the pious make obedience and avoiding prohibitions a barrier against punishment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r9.anchor: وأصله الحجز بين الشيئين ومنه يقال اتقى بترسه أي جعله حاجزا بين نفسه وبين ما يقصده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r10.claim: A hadith says that in intense battle the Companions sheltered behind the Messenger, illustrating taqwā as a protective barrier.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r10.anchor: كنا إذا احمر البأس اتقينا برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r11.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r11.claim: When ʿUmar asked Kaʿb about taqwā, Kaʿb compared it to carefully gathering oneself while crossing a thorny path.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r11.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه لكعب الأحبار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r12.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r12.claim: Shahr ibn Ḥawshab says the pious leave what is harmless for fear of what is harmful.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r12.anchor: وقال شهر بن حوشب: المتقي الذي يترك ما لا بأس به حذرا لما به بأس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r13.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r13.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz defines taqwā as avoiding what God forbids and performing what He obligates; whatever God grants afterward is added good.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r13.anchor: وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز: التقوى ترك ما حرم الله وأداء ما افترض الله فما رزق الله بعد ذلك فهو خير إلى خير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r14.claim: Another definition is following the Prophet; a hadith gathers the essence of taqwā in God's command to justice and excellence at 16:90.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r15.speaker: ابن عمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r15.claim: Ibn ʿUmar defines taqwā as not seeing oneself as better than anyone else.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r15.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: التقوى أن لا ترى نفسك خيرا من أحد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r16.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r16.claim: The pious are singled out either to honor them or because they are the ones who benefit from guidance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p59#4/r16.anchor: وتخصيص المتقين بالذكر تشريف لهم أو لأنهم هم المتقون بالهدى

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r1.claim: The demonstrative may point to alif-lām-mīm as the letters composing the Qurʾān, to the sūra or Qurʾān after its utterance, or to the promised Book revealed now or in earlier scriptures.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r1.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى { الم } إن أول بالمؤلف من هذه الحروف أو فسر بالسورة أو القرآن فإنه لما تكلم به وتقضى

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r2.claim: Kitāb is a verbal noun applied to its object for emphasis; alternatively it is a pattern meaning written object, applied to a composed discourse before writing because it is meant to be written. Its root means gathering.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r2.anchor: وهو مصدر سمي به المفعول للمبالغة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r3.claim: The Qurʾān is so clear and its proof so evident that sound reflection leaves no rational doubt that it is revelation at the level of inimitability; this does not mean nobody doubts it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r3.anchor: لا أن أحدا لا يرتاب فيه، ألا ترى إلى قوله تعالى:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r4.claim: Verse 2:23 confirms that the challenge does not remove their initial doubt; it gives them a way to settle it by trying to compose one sūra and exhausting their effort, whose failure proves the Book beyond suspicion.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r4.anchor: فإنه ما أبعد عنهم الريب بل عرفهم الطريق المريح له، وهو أن يجتهدوا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r5.claim: An alternative construal takes the negation as meaning that there is no doubt in the Book for the Godfearing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r5.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا ريب فيه للمتقين.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r6.claim: Rayb originally denotes the anxiety and disturbance caused by something; doubt is called rayb because it unsettles the soul and removes tranquility, as in the cited saying and the phrase for time's calamities.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2/r6.anchor: والريب في الأصل مصدر رابني الشيء إذا حصل فيك الريبة، وهي قلق النفس واضطرابها،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r1.claim: Hudā means guidance, originally indication that leads people to the truth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r1.anchor: يهديهم إلى الحق، والهدى في الأصل كالسرى والتقى ومعناه الدلالة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r2.claim: Another definition is indication that reaches the sought goal, since guidance is contrasted with misguidance in 34:24 and one is called guided only on reaching the aim.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: الدلالة الموصلة إلى البغية لأنه جعل مقابل الضلالة في قوله تعالى:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r3.claim: The Book is singled out as guidance for the Godfearing because they follow and benefit from it, although its indication is available to every observer, Muslim or unbeliever; hence it is also called guidance for people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r3.anchor: واختصاصه بالمتقين لأنهم المهتدون به والمنتفعون بنصه، وإن كانت دلالته عامة لكل ناظر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, only people who refine their intellect, contemplate signs and miracles, and recognize prophecy benefit, just as good food benefits only someone already healthy; the Qurʾān heals believers but increases wrongdoers' loss.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r4.anchor: أو لأنه لا ينتفع بالتأمل فيه إلا من صقل العقل واستعمله في تدبر الآيات والنظر في المعجزات،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r5.claim: The presence of concise or ambiguous passages does not prevent the Qurʾān from being guidance, since it is accompanied by clarification that identifies their intended meaning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r5.anchor: ولا يقدح ما فيه من المجمل والمتشابه في كونه هدى لما لم ينفك عن بيان يعين المراد منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r6.claim: Muttaqī is the active participle of guarding oneself; in religious usage it is one who protects oneself from harm in the afterlife.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r6.anchor: والمتقي اسم فاعل من قولهم وقاه فاتقى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r7.claim: Taqwā has three ranks: avoiding eternal punishment by renouncing shirk (48:26); avoiding every sin of commission or omission, even minor sins according to some (7:96); and detaching from all that distracts from God and devoting oneself wholly to Him (3:102).
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r7.anchor: وله ثلاث مراتب: الأولى: التوقي من العذاب المخلد بالتبري من الشرك

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r8.claim: Bayḍāwī says the phrase is interpreted here according to all three ranks of taqwā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r8.anchor: وقد فسر قوله: { هدى للمتقين } ههنا على الأوجه الثلاثة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r9.claim: One parsing makes alif-lām-mīm the subject as a name for the Qurʾān, the sūra, or what is composed from these letters; dhālika is its predicate and al-kitāb describes the fully perfected composition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#2/r9.anchor: أن يكون { الم } مبتدأ على أنه اسم للقرآن.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r1.claim: Other parses make alif-lām-mīm the predicate of an omitted subject and dhālika a second predicate or apposition, with al-kitāb as its adjective; alternatively dhālika is the subject and al-kitāb its predicate or adjective.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r1.anchor: وأن يكون { الم } خبر مبتدأ محذوف وذلك خبرا ثانيا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r2.claim: In the common reading, rayb is accusative in construction with the categorical negative lā, which governs like inna and implies min.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r2.anchor: و { لا ريب } في المشهورة مبني لتضمنه معنى من منصوب المحل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r3.speaker: أبو الشعثاء
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r3.claim: Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ reads rayb in the nominative, taking lā as lā of negation like laysa and fīhi as its predicate; this avoids restricting the negation to this book, unlike 37:47. The phrase may instead be an adjective with lil-muttaqīn as predicate.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r3.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي الشعثاء مرفوع بلا التي بمعنى ليس وفيه خبره ولم يقدم كما قدم في قوله تعالى:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r4.claim: Hudā may be an accusative circumstantial phrase or have an omitted predicate as lā does; on the latter analysis, fīhi is the fronted predicate of the indefinite hudā, and the reciter pauses after lā rayba.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r4.anchor: وهدى نصب على الحال، أو الخبر محذوف كما في

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r5.claim: Another analysis makes dhālika the subject and al-kitāb its predicate, meaning the complete book worthy of the name; or al-kitāb is an adjective and the following clause is the predicate of alif-lām-mīm.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r5.anchor: وأن يكون ذلك مبتدأ و { الكتب } خبره على معنى

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r6.claim: Bayḍāwī prefers treating the four clauses as a sequence without conjunctions, each confirming what precedes: the letters signal the challenge, the Book confirms its excellence, its freedom from doubt confirms perfection, and its guidance confirms truth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r6.anchor: والأولى أن يقال إنها جمل متناسقة تقرر اللاحقة منها السابقة ولذلك لم يدخل العاطف بينهما.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r7.claim: He identifies a distinct rhetorical grace in each clause: ellipsis and allusion with explanation, the grandeur of definiteness, delayed adverbial wording avoiding a false implication, then ellipsis and an indefinite verbal noun for emphasis and magnificence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r7.anchor: وفي كل واحدة منها نكتة ذات جزالة ففي الأولى الحذف والرمز إلى المقصود مع التعليل، وفي الثانية فخامة التعريف،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r8.claim: The restriction of guidance to the pious is by outcome: those approaching taqwā are called pious, a concise wording that magnifies their standing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:2#3/r8.anchor: وتخصيص الهدى بالمتقين باعتبار الغاية تسمية المشارف للتقوى متقيا إيجازا وتفخيما لشأنه.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r1.claim: The opening letters are shared human speech; failure to produce a comparable sura proves the Qur’an is God’s speech, while the demonstrative and lām mark its perfection and exalted rank.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r2.claim: The distant demonstrative and lām of perfection exalt the Book’s effects and rank, beyond the reach of those driven away from it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r2.anchor: فأشير إليه بأداة البعد ولام الكمال في قوله { ذلك الكتب }

BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r3.claim: For anyone who reflects correctly, neither the Book’s meanings nor its arrangement gives grounds for doubt; the negation denies that it is liable to suspicion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r3.anchor: أي في شيء من معناه ولانظمه في نفس الأمر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r4.claim: Harali derives kitāb from joining separated things with a subtle bond of their own kind; lā universally negates, and rayb is hesitation between accusations that prevents assurance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r4.anchor: قال الحرالي : ( ذا ) اسم مدلوله المشار إليه والام مدلوله معها بعدما { الكتاب }

BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r5.claim: Rayb originates in agitation and disturbance of the soul; the term also describes the unsettling calamities of time.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r5.anchor: وأصله قلق النفس واضراربه , ومنه ريب الزمان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r6.claim: The Qur’an guides those receptive to it; the obstinate gain no guidance and instead doubt it, although it is not actually a ground for doubt.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r6.anchor: وخص المنتفعين لن الألد لادواء له والتعنت

BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r7.claim: Harali defines the God-fearing as those who restrain themselves because they recognize their deficiency and dependence; taqwa is the root of guidance and worship and a divine charge to the People of Scripture.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p33/r7.anchor: قال الحرالي : جمع المتقى وهو المتوقف عن الإقدام على كل أمر لشعوره بتقصير

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r1.claim: Biqai connects the Qur’an’s guidance here to the opening of the sūra, where it is declared free of doubt.

DURR-FULL:v1p59/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the final passage Jibrīl rehearsed with the Prophet was Alif-Lām-Mīm, that Book without doubt, guidance for the God-fearing.
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: آخر حرف عارض به جبريل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم {الم ذلك الكتاب لا ريب فيه هدى للمتقين}

DURR-FULL:v1p59/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r3.claim: Mujāhid divides the opening into four verses describing believers, two describing disbelievers, thirteen describing hypocrites, and verses 40–120 concerning the Children of Israel.
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: من أول البقرة أربع آيات في نعت المؤمنين وآيتان في نعت الكافرين وثلاث عشرة آية في نعت المنافقين

DURR-FULL:v1p59/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r4.claim: Mujāhid says the first four verses through al-mufliḥūn describe believers, the next two through ʿaẓīm describe disbelievers, and up to verse ten describes hypocrites.
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: هؤلاء الآيات الأربع في أول سورة البقرة إلى {المفلحون} نزلت في نعت المؤمنين

DURR-FULL:v1p59/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r5.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r5.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas says four verses at the start of al-Baqara concern believers and two concern the leaders of the confederate groups.
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r5.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس قال: أربع آيات من فاتحة سورة البقرة في الذين آمنوا وآيتان في قادة الأحزاب

DURR-FULL:v1p59/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd glosses Alif-Lām-Mīm as a letter of God's name, al-kitāb as the Quran, and lā rayba as no doubt.
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود {الم} حرف اسم الله و {الكتاب} القرآن {لا ريب} لا شك فيه

DURR-FULL:v1p59/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, with ʿIkrima transmitting the same gloss, explains dhālika al-kitāb as this book.
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ذلك الكتاب} قال: هذا الكتاب

DURR-FULL:v1p59/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains lā rayba fīhi as meaning there is no doubt in it.
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {لا ريب فيه} قال: لا شك فيه

DURR-FULL:v1p59/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r9.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r9.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ says doubt belongs to unbelief.
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r9.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال ال {ريب} الشك من الكفر

DURR-FULL:v1p59/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains rayb as doubt and cites Ibn al-Zibaʿrī's verse distinguishing doubt from truth to show Arab usage.
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r10.anchor: ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله عز وجل {لا ريب فيه} قال: لا شك فيه

DURR-FULL:v1p59/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r11.claim: Qatāda glosses lā rayba fīhi as meaning there is no doubt in it.
DURR-FULL:v1p59/r11.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {لا ريب فيه} قال: لا شك فيه

DURR-FULL:v1p60/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r1.claim: Mujāhid likewise glosses lā rayba fīhi as meaning there is no doubt in it.

DURR-FULL:v1p60/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r2.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī explains guidance as leading out of misguidance.
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r2.anchor: عن الشعبي في قوله {هدى} قال: من الضلالة

DURR-FULL:v1p60/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd glosses guidance as light.
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله {هدى} قال: نور

DURR-FULL:v1p60/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd identifies the God-fearing as believers.
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله {هدى} قال: نور {للمتقين} قال: هم المؤمنون

DURR-FULL:v1p60/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the God-fearing as those who fear God's punishment for abandoning known guidance and hope for His mercy by affirming what comes from Him.
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {هدى للمتقين} أي الذين يحذرون من أمر الله عقوبته في ترك ما يعرفون

DURR-FULL:v1p60/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also defines them as believers who avoid associating partners with God and obey Him.
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {هدى للمتقين} قال: للمؤمنين الذين يتقون الشرك ويعملون بطاعتي

DURR-FULL:v1p60/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r7.claim: Qatāda says God made the Quran guidance and radiance for whoever affirms it, and light for the God-fearing.
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {هدى للمتقين} قال: جعله الله هدى وضياء لمن صدق به ونور للمتقين

DURR-FULL:v1p60/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r8.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r8.claim: Muʿādh ibn Jabal reports that on Judgment Day the God-fearing will stand under divine mercy without a veil; they are those who shunned idolatry and worshipped God sincerely, and they enter Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r8.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل قال: يحبس الناس يوم القيامة بقيع واحد فينادي مناد: أين المتقون

DURR-FULL:v1p60/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r9.claim: The Prophet said a believer does not attain true God-fearingness until leaving harmless things out of caution against harmful things; al-Tirmidhī graded the report ḥasan and al-Ḥākim authenticated it.
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r9.anchor: عن عطية السعدي وكان من الصحابة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يبلغ العبد المؤمن أن يكون من المتقين حتى يدع

DURR-FULL:v1p60/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r10.claim: Abū Hurayra compares piety to avoiding thorns on a thorny path: one passes around them or keeps away, and that is taqwā.
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r10.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رجلا قال له: ما التقوى قال: هل أخذت طريقا ذا شوك

DURR-FULL:v1p60/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r11.speaker: طلق بن حبيب
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r11.claim: Ṭalq ibn Ḥabīb defines taqwā as obeying God in His light while hoping for mercy and avoiding disobedience in His light while fearing punishment.
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r11.anchor: عن طلق بن حبيب أنه قيل له: ألا تجمع لنا التقوى في كلام يسير

DURR-FULL:v1p60/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r12.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r12.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ says complete taqwā means fearing God down to an atom's weight and leaving some things thought lawful for fear they may be unlawful.
DURR-FULL:v1p60/r12.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: تمام التقوى أن يتقي الله العبد حتى يتقيه من مثقال ذرة

DURR-FULL:v1p63/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p63/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v1p63/r1.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ's poem says people seek their desires but God wills otherwise, and taqwā is a better gain than wealth or provision.
DURR-FULL:v1p63/r1.anchor: لأبي الدرداء: إنه ليس أحد له بيت في الأنصار إلا قال شعرا فما لك لا تقول قال: وأنا قلت فاستمعوه: يريد المرء أن يعطي مناه

DURR-FULL:v1p63/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p63/r2.speaker: أبو العفيف
DURR-FULL:v1p63/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿAfīf says Paradise entrants fall into four groups: the God-fearing, the thankful, the fearful, and the companions of the right.
DURR-FULL:v1p63/r2.anchor: عن أبي العفيف وكان من أصحاب معاذ بن جبل قال: يدخل أهل الجنة على أربعة أصناف

DURR-FULL:v1p63/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p63/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p63/r3.claim: Qatāda says the following description of those who believe in the unseen characterizes the God-fearing mentioned in the preceding verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p63/r3.anchor: عن قتادة {هدى للمتقين} قال: نعتهم ووصفهم بقوله {الذين يؤمنون بالغيب} الآية

IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة وسعيد بن جبير والسدي ومقاتل بن حيان وزيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r1.claim: They explain “that Book” as this Book.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة : ذلك الكتاب قال : هذا الكتاب . قال : وهكذا فسره سعيد ابن جبير والسدى ومقاتل بن حيان وزيد بن اسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r2.speaker: الحسن وابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan, with Ibn Abbas also reported to agree, identifies the Book as the Qur’an.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r2.anchor: عن الحسن في قول الله : الكتاب قال : القران . قال : أبو محمد : وروى عن ابن عباس مثل ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Darda says rayb means doubt and that doubt is a form of disbelief.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال : الريب - يعني الشك - من الكفر

IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim says he knows no disagreement among the named commentators that rayb means doubt.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو محمد : ولا اعلم في هذا الحرف اختلافا بين المفسرين منهم ابن عباس ، وسعيد بن جبير ، وابو مالك ونافع مولى ابن عمر

IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r5.speaker: الشعبي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbi explains guidance as guidance away from misguidance.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r5.anchor: عن الشعبي في قوله : هدى قال : من الضلالة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says the Book is light for the God-conscious.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r6.anchor: عن السدى : واما هدى للمتقين نور للمتقين

IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr explains it as clarification for the God-conscious.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير : هدى للمتقين تبيان للمتقين

IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r8.speaker: عطية السعدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r8.claim: The Prophet says a person is not among the God-conscious until he leaves harmless things for fear of falling into harm.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p33#2/r8.anchor: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم : لا يكون الرجل من المتقين حتى يدع مالا باس به

IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r1.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r1.claim: Muʿadh reports that the God-conscious avoid associating partners and idol worship, worship God sincerely, and enter Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r1.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل ؟ قال : بلى ، سمعته يقول : يجلس الناس يوم القيامة في تقيع واحد

IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r2.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r2.claim: At the resurrection, the God-conscious stand in God’s protection, with no veil separating them from Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r2.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل ؟ قال : بلى ، سمعته يقول : يجلس الناس يوم القيامة في تقيع واحد

IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r3.claim: The God-conscious fear God’s punishment for abandoning known guidance and hope for His mercy by affirming what He sent.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : يقول الله سبحانه وبحمده : هدى للمتقين اي الذين يحذرون من الله عقوبته

IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r4.claim: Al-Suddi calls the guidance a light and identifies the God-conscious as believers.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r4.anchor: عن السدى : هدى للمتقين نور للمتقين ، وهم المؤمنون .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r5.claim: Qatada says God describes the God-conscious here as those who believe in the unseen, as the next verse continues.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p35/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : هدى للمتقين من هم ؟ نعتهم الله ، فاثبت نعتهم ووصفهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r1.claim: The verse begins a new utterance, syntactically independent of the disjoint letters alif-lam-mim, on the most apparent analysis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r1.anchor: مبدأ كلام لا اتصال له في الإعراب بحروف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r2.claim: On the view that alif-lam-mim is a challenge, the demonstrative may point to those letters: the book is composed from the Arabs' own letters, yet they cannot rival it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r2.anchor: صاحب ( الكشاف ) على احتمال أن تكون حروف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r3.claim: On the apparent reading, the demonstrative is the subject, al-kitab is an appositive explaining the unseen referent, and what follows supplies the predicate; the reference is the Quran already revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r3.anchor: وعلى الأظهر تكون الإشارة إلى القرآن المعروف لديهم يومئذ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r4.speaker: author
