IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r4.claim: The demonstrative can refer to the revealed Quran known then, meaning the surahs preceding al-Baqara, since every portion already revealed is called Quran and later revelation joins it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r4.anchor: النازل بالفعل وهي السور المتقدمة على سورة البقرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r5.claim: Alternatively it refers to the whole Quran, including future revelation, which is mentally anticipated; al-kitab then explains the demonstrative and لا ريب فيه is the predicate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الإشارة إلى جميع القرآن ما نزل منه وما سينزل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r6.speaker: الرضي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r6.claim: Al-Radi says demonstratives are for present, near objects, while distant forms can point to absent things; near forms are less common for absent referents, with the pattern reversed for speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219/r6.anchor: وضع اسم الإشارة للحضور والقربب لأنه للمشار إليه حسا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r1.speaker: ابن مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r1.claim: Ibn Malik allows near and distant demonstratives alike for preceding discourse; Ibn Ashur says his account better matches actual usage and rejects al-Radi's broad claim of rarity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r1.anchor: وابن مالك في ( التسهيل ) سوى بين الإتيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r2.claim: The alternation between distant and near demonstratives for one referent appears across the Jesus passage, where 3:58 and 3:62 point to the same account.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r3.claim: Both demonstrative distances also occur for a non-speech referent, as in the two men whom Moses found fighting: one is of his party and one his enemy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r3.anchor: فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان هذا من شيعته وهذا من عدوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r4.claim: Because both forms are linguistically available, eloquent speakers select between them for contextual purposes; here the distant form elevates the Quran's rank and makes it seem remote in dignity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r4.anchor: فلا جرم أن كانت الإشارة في الآية باستعمال اسم الإشارة للبعيد لإظهار رفعة شأن هذا القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r5.claim: A noble thing is figuratively placed high and out of reach to protect it from wear and casual handling; the Quran is likewise beyond the polytheists' ability to rival it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r5.anchor: وقد شاع في الكلام البليغ تمثيل الأمر الشريف بالشيء المرفوع في عزة المنال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r6.claim: The Quran may be distant because its truthful meanings and beneficial guidance are beyond those who dismiss it as fabricated or tales of the ancients.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r6.anchor: أو لأنه لصدق معانيه ونفع إرشاده بعيد عمن يتناوله بهجر القول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r7.claim: The nearby demonstrative in 6:92 is no objection: it points to a book physically before its audience to encourage study and heedfulness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r7.anchor: فذلك للإشارة إلى كتاب بين يدي أهله لترغيبهم في العكوف عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari apparently did not treat the distant demonstrative as an honorific; Ibn Ashur praises the author of al-Miftah for listing distance as a means of glorification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r8.anchor: ولعل صاحب ( الكشاف ) بنى على مثل ما بنى عليه الرضي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r9.speaker: خفاف بن ندبة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r9.claim: Khuffaf's line uses ذلك to present himself as a figure of elevated standing, illustrating the honorific force of a distant demonstrative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r9.anchor: كما قال خفاف بن ندبة : أقول له والرمح يأطر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r10.speaker: قيس بن الخطيم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r10.claim: Qays ibn al-Khatim uses the near demonstrative هذا for death to convey disregard, illustrating a contextual use of proximity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p219#2/r10.anchor: كقول قيس بن الخطيم في ( الحماسة ) : متى يأتت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r1.claim: Al-kitab may be an appositive to the demonstrative, identifying its unseen referent by definite reference; the clause لا ريب فيه then serves as predicate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون بدلا من اسم الإشارة لقصد بيان المشار إليه لعدم مشاهدته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r2.claim: Alternatively al-kitab is the predicate, and its definite article marks the genus; defining both terms rhetorically restricts complete bookhood to the Quran, not by literal exclusion of other books.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ( الكتاب ) خبرا عن اسم الإشارة ويكون التعريف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r3.claim: The genus reading means the Quran gathers the perfect qualities of books, while other scriptures lack some such perfection; grammarians call this definite article a marker of perfection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r3.anchor: ذلك هو الكتاب الجامع لصفات الكمال في جنس الكتب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r4.claim: Kitab means something written: it can be an intensive verbal noun or a fa'al form with passive sense, like libas for something worn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r4.anchor: و ( الكتاب ) فعال بمعنى المكتوب إما مصدر كاتب المصوغ للمبالغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r5.claim: The root كتب means to gather and join, since a book gathers its pages and letters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r5.anchor: واشتقاقه من كتب بمعنى جمع وضم لأن الكتاب تجمع أوراقه وحروفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r6.claim: The Prophet ordered all revelation to be written and appointed scribes; calling the Quran a book signals writing as its preservation, and Quranic writing is a communal obligation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p221/r6.anchor: فإن النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر بكتابة كل ما ينزل من الوحي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r1.claim: لا ريب فيه may be a circumstantial phrase modifying al-kitab or one of its first or second predicates, as already discussed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r1.anchor: حال من الكتاب أو خبر أول أو ثان على ما مر قريبا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r2.claim: Rayb means doubt, but originally denotes inner anxiety and disturbance; calamities of time are also called rayb because they unsettle the soul.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r2.anchor: والريب الشك وأصل الريب القلق واضطراب النفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r3.claim: The verbs رابه and أرابه both mean to make someone doubt; the hamza does not add causative force, like the pairs لحق وألحق and زلقه وأزلقه.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r3.anchor: ويقال أرابه كذلك إذ الهمزة لم تكسبه تعدية زائدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r4.claim: Abu Zayd distinguishes the verbs: أراب is weaker than راب and means bringing someone close to doubt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r4.anchor: وقد قيل إن أراب أضعف من راب أراب بمعنى قربه من أن يشك قاله أبو زيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r5.speaker: بشار
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r5.claim: Bashshar's verse witnesses the distinction, using أرِبتُ for being brought near to doubt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r5.anchor: قال بشار : أخوك الذي إن ربته قال إنما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r6.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r6.claim: The hadith advises leaving an action that makes one uncertain about its prohibition for another whose permissibility is clear; Ibn Ashur gives no grading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( دع ما يريبك إلى ما لا يريبك )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r7.speaker: القراء المتواترون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r7.claim: The transmitted readers all pronounce لا ريب with fatḥ, negating the genus emphatically; nominative رفع could deny only an individual doubt rather than all doubt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r7.anchor: في فتح { لا ريب } نفيا للجنس على سبيل التنصيص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r8.claim: If the demonstrative points to the challenge in alif-lam-mim and al-kitab predicates it, no doubt specifically denies uncertainty that a book made from familiar letters could defeat them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r8.anchor: نفيا لريب خاص وهو الريب الذي يعرض في كون هذا الكتاب مؤلفا من حروف كلامهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r9.claim: Majority attach فيه to rayb as an adverbial complement and pause there, as in the cited verses; alternatively it is a stable predicate for هدى.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r10.claim: On the second parse, figurative containment means the Quran's wording indicates guidance; the indefinite هدى suggests some guidance and coaxes avoidant hearers to listen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r10.anchor: هو الظرفية المجازية العرفية تشبيها لدلالة اللفظ باحتواء الظرف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r11.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r11.claim: The Prophet told Abu Dharr, إنك امرؤ فيك جاهلية, an example of figurative containment; no grading is stated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r11.anchor: قول النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي ذر : ( إنك امرؤ فيك جاهلية )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r12.claim: The predicate of لا is omitted because it is obvious—there is no doubt present; this omission is common, as in قالوا لا ضير and ordinary لا بأس.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p222/r12.anchor: محذوفا لظهوره أي لا ريب موجود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.claim: A third possible sense is guidance for future people who will become God-fearing; the verbal noun هدى itself carries no fixed tense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.anchor: الثالث : أنه هدى في المستقبل للذين سيتقون في المستقبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.claim: Calling the Quran هدى, rather than هاد, conveys richer praise and leads into praise of believers who benefit from its guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.anchor: حصل من وصف الكتاب بالمصدر من وفرة المعاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.claim: The Quran guides the pious in religion, public affairs, ethics, legislation, and jurisprudence across ranks and times, according to their effort, learning, and needs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.anchor: ومن منتفع في السياسة وتدبير أمور الأمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.speaker: أئمة الأصول
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.claim: Legal theorists count jurisprudential ijtihad as taqwa and infer its obligation from the command to fear God as much as one can.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.anchor: وقد جعل أئمة الأصول الاجتهاد في الفقه من التقوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r5.claim: Any failure to benefit fully reflects a shortcoming in the recipient, not a defect in Quranic guidance; scholars and the pious keep striving to follow it more completely.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r5.anchor: فإنما ذلك لنقص فيه لا في الهداية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r6.claim: The four opening clauses cohere: alif-lam-mim announces inimitability; ذلك الكتاب praises the Quran's perfection, urging rational Arabs to follow and take pride in it, and reminding the People of the Book it surpasses their scripture.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p226#2/r6.anchor: تسجيل لإعجاز القرآن وإنحاء على عامة المشركين عجزهم عن معارضته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r1.claim: Where Qur’anic wording, syntax, semantics, or pause permits several readings without violating context, the passage should bear all of them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r1.anchor: يجب حمل الكلام على جميعها كالوصل والوقف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r2.claim: One valid reading pauses after لا ريب or فيه; Ibn Ashur develops both effects in the next discussion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r2.anchor: كالوصل والوقف في قوله تعالى ) لا ريب فيه هدى للمتقين (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r3.claim: The same principle allows distinct pauses in 3:146 and 3:7, and either attachment of Ibrahim’s vocative to the reproach or threat in 19:46.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r3.anchor: باختلاف ارتباط النداء من قوله ( يا إبراهيم ) بالتوبيخ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r4.claim: Because the Quran addresses every nation and age, God made it Arabic, which Ibn Ashur considers rich, concise, eloquent, flexible, and abundant in expression.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r4.anchor: وقد أراد الله تعالى أن يكون القرآن كتابا مخاطبا به كل الأمم في جميع العصور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r5.claim: The Quran packs many meanings Arabic syntax can bear into minimal wording, favoring concise expression and using forms rarer than in Arab eloquence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r5.anchor: في أقل ما يسمح به نظم تلك اللغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r6.claim: Among the Quran’s subtle styles are simultaneous senses of a polysemous word, literal and figurative senses, explicit and allusive meanings, and implications carried by constructions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r6.anchor: استعمال اللفظ المشترك في معنييه أو معانيه دفعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r7.claim: Rhetoricians recognized meanings implied by constructions, but simultaneous polysemy and literal-plus-figurative use remain disputed because prior Arabic usage rarely attested them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r7.anchor: وبقي المبحثان الأولان وهما استعمال المشترك في معنييه أو معانيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r8.speaker: الغزالي وأبو الحسين البصري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r8.claim: Al-Ghazali and Abu al-Husayn al-Basri allow a speaker to intend several senses of a shared word, but say this comes from intention rather than linguistic denotation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r8.anchor: إذ قال الغزالي وأبو الحسين البصري يصح أن يراد بالمشترك عدة معان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r9.claim: Ibn Ashur takes their point to mean that intended senses can be rational implications of a construction, requiring no metaphorical relation or cue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r9.anchor: وظني بهما أنهما يريدان تصيير تلك الإرادة إلى أنها دلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r10.claim: Ibn Ashur holds that a shared word can linguistically denote all or some of its several senses at once.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r10.anchor: والحق أن المشترك يصح إطلاقه على عدة من معانيه جميعا أو بعضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r11.speaker: قوم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r11.claim: One group treats a shared word intended in multiple senses as literal; this is attributed to al-Shafi‘i, al-Baqillani, and most Mu‘tazilites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r11.anchor: نسب إلى الشافعي وأبي بكر الباقلاني وجمهور المعتزلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r12.speaker: قوم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r12.claim: Another group considers multiple intended senses figurative.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r13.speaker: ابن الحاجب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r13.claim: Ibn al-Hajib reads al-Baqillani as allowing a shared word to carry multiple senses only with an indicator, which he takes to mark figurative usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r13.anchor: وجزم ابن الحاجب بأنه مراد الباقلاني من قوله في كتاب التقريب والإرشاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r14.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects Ibn al-Hajib’s reading: a metaphor cue blocks the literal sense, whereas every sense of a genuinely shared word is literal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r14.anchor: وهذا لا يستقيم لأن القرينة التي هي من علامات المجاز هي القرينة المانعة من إرادة المعنى الحقيقي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r15.claim: The cue for a shared word selects which literal senses, all or some, the speaker intends; treating these senses as nonliteral would erase the category.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p97/r15.anchor: إذ معاني المشترك كلها من قبيل الحقيقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r1.claim: A brief pause can build anticipation like an explanatory ellipsis; the following clause then functions like a resumption, even if not formally one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r1.anchor: السكوت عند كلمة وتعقيبها بما بعدها يجعل ما بعدها بمنزلة الاستئناف البياني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r3.claim: Stopping after لا ريب elides a completion such as no doubt that it is the Book; فيه هدى للمتقين begins a new sentence, conceding that it contains guidance even if opponents deny the whole is guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r3.anchor: كان من قبيل إيجاز الحذف أي لا ريب في أنه الكتاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r4.claim: Connecting فيه to the preceding clause is an elaborated reading in which what follows shows that the whole Book is guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r4.anchor: وكان ما بعده مفيدا أن هذا الكتاب كله هدى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r5.claim: The Quran generally varies wording and form instead of repeating them, except where repetition serves emphasis or another purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r5.anchor: ومن أساليب القرآن العدول عن تكرير اللفظ والصيغة فيما عدا المقامات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r11.claim: The Quran broadened Arabic literary expression; before it, poetry was the dominant surviving and circulating form of Arab literature.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r11.anchor: ومنها اتساع أدب اللغة في القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r12.claim: Other Arab forms included sermons, proverbs, and dialogue: sermons were poorly retained and briefly influential, proverbs were concise lessons, and dialogue ranged from everyday talk to public assemblies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r12.anchor: فأما الخطب فكانت تنسى بانتهاء المقامات المقولة فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r13.speaker: لبيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r13.claim: Labid’s verse depicts public assemblies with unknown visitors, expected benefits, and feared blame, illustrating the forum-dialogue genre Ibn Ashur describes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r13.anchor: أشار إليها لبيد بقوله : وكثيرة غرباؤها مجهولة ترجى نوافلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r1.claim: The demonstrative is analyzed as dhāl plus alif, or dhāl alone with alif as reinforcement; the lām marks distance and emphasis, and the kāf marks address.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r1.anchor: الاسم من ذلك الذال والألف، وقيل الذال وحدها، والألف تقوية، واللام لبعد المشار إليه وللتأكيد، والكاف للخطاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r2.claim: ذلك is nominative, either as the predicate of an understood subject or as a subject whose predicate follows.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r2.anchor: وموضع ذلك رفع كأنه خبر ابتداء، أو ابتداء وخبره بعده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r3.claim: One view takes ذلك as meaning this and pointing to the Qur’anic letters just recited.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r3.anchor: فقيل: هو بمعنى «هذا» ، وتكون الإشارة إلى هذه الحروف من القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r4.claim: Arabic may use ذلك for something present that has an aspect of remoteness, and هذا for something absent that is firmly established and near in status.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r4.anchor: قد يشار ب «ذلك» إلى حاضر تعلق به بعض الغيبة وب «هذا» إلى غائب هو من الثبوت والحضور بمنزلة وقرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r5.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r5.claim: On the ordinary distant demonstrative, one proposed referent is the portion of the Qur’an already revealed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو على بابه إشارة إلى غائب، واختلف في ذلك الغائب، فقيل: ما قد كان نزل من القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r6.claim: Another proposed referent is the Torah and Gospel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r6.anchor: واختلف في ذلك الغائب، فقيل: ما قد كان نزل من القرآن، وقيل: التوراة والإنجيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r7.claim: Another view identifies the absent book with the Preserved Tablet, the book of decree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r7.anchor: وقيل: اللوح المحفوظ أي الكتاب الذي هو القدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r8.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r8.claim: God had promised the Prophet a book that water could not erase, and the demonstrative points to that promise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r8.anchor: وقيل: إن الله قد كان وعد نبيه أن ينزل عليه كتابا لا يمحوه الماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r9.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r9.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says the demonstrative points to the Qur’an in heaven that had not yet been sent down.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r9.anchor: وقال الكسائي: «ذلك إشارة إلى القرآن الذي في السماء لم ينزل بعد»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r10.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r10.claim: Another view points to God’s promise to the People of the Book that He would send a scripture to Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r10.anchor: وقيل: إن الله قد كان وعد أهل الكتاب أن ينزل على محمد كتابا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r11.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r11.claim: For those who take alif-lām-mīm as the alphabet letters with which people were challenged to compose, ذلك points to those letters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r11.anchor: وقيل: إن الإشارة إلى حروف المعجم في قول من قال الم حروف المعجم التي تحديتكم بالنظم منها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r12.claim: Kitāb derives from katabtu al-shayʾ, “I assembled it,” as when beads are strung or a she-camel is marked.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r12.anchor: ولفظ الكتاب مأخوذ من «كتبت الشيء» إذا جمعته وضممت بعضه إلى بعض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r13.claim: الكتاب can be parsed as an appositive, predicate of an initial subject, or explanatory apposition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r13.anchor: ورفع الكتاب يتوجه على البدل أو على خبر الابتداء أو على عطف البيان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r14.claim: There is no doubt or uncertainty in the Book itself, even though unbelievers do in fact doubt it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r14.anchor: لا شك فيه ولا ارتياب به والمعنى أنه في ذاته لا ريب فيه وإن وقع ريب للكفار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r15.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r15.claim: Some take the declarative wording لا ريب فيه as intended to function as a prohibition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r15.anchor: وقال قوم: لفظ قوله لا ريب فيه لفظ الخبر ومعناه النهي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r16.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r16.claim: Some understand the general wording as restricted to believers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r16.anchor: وقال قوم: هو عموم يراد به الخصوص أي عند المؤمنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya judges the restriction of the general wording to believers weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r17.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا ضعيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r18.speaker: الزهري وابن محيصن ومسلم بن جندب وعبيد بن عمير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r18.claim: These readers pronounce the hāʾ in فيه with ḍamma, as they do in إليه، عليه، به، نصله and similar forms, following the original form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r18.anchor: وقرأ الزهري، وابن محيصن، ومسلم بن جندب، وعبيد بن عمير: «فيه» بضم الهاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r19.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r19.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reads فيهو, with a ḍamma on hāʾ and a connecting wāw.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r19.anchor: وقرأ ابن إسحاق: «فيهو» ضم الهاء ووصلها بواو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r20.claim: Hudā means right guidance and clarification.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r21.claim: هدى may be nominative as the predicate of ذلك, the predicate of an implicit subject, or a subject whose predicate is the preceding prepositional phrase.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r21.anchor: وموضعه، من الإعراب رفع على أنه خبر ذلك، أو خبر ابتداء مضمر، أو ابتداء وخبره في المجرور قبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r22.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r22.claim: هدى may also be accusative as a circumstantial expression from ذلك, الكتاب, or the pronoun in فيه; the last analysis is weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p83/r22.anchor: ويصح أن يكون موضعه نصبا على الحال من ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p84/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p84/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p84/r1.claim: Al-muttaqīn derives from waqā via ittaqā on the iftaʿala pattern; its underlying form is للموتقيين, reduced through vowel shift, deletion, replacement of wāw by tāʾ, and assimilation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p84/r1.anchor: اللفظ مأخوذ من وقى، وفعله اتقى، على وزن افتعل، وأصله «للموتقيين»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p84/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p84/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p84/r2.claim: The God-fearing are those who obey God’s commands and avoid His disobedience, making that conduct a protection from His punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p84/r2.anchor: الذين يتقون الله تعالى بامتثال أوامره واجتناب معاصيه، كان ذلك وقاية بينهم وبين عذاب الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والكسائي وأبو عبيدة والأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r1.claim: They take dhalika to mean “this”; Khuffaf’s poetic use of dhalika is cited as evidence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنه بمعنى هذا وهو قول ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والكسائي وأبي عبيدة والأخفش واحتج بعضهم بقول خفاف بن ندبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says Khuffaf means, “I am the one you know,” rather than using dhalika simply for “this.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري إنما أراد أنا ذلك الذي تعرفه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r3.claim: On the view that dhalika points to something absent, it refers to the Quran already revealed to Muhammad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r3.anchor: والثاني أنه إشارة إلى غائب ثم فيه ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنه أراد به ما تقدم إنزاله عليه من القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r4.claim: A second reported referent is the Quran promised to Muhammad in the words “We shall cast upon you a weighty word.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r4.anchor: والثانى أنه أراد به ما وعده أن يوحيه إليه في قبوله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r5.claim: A third referent is the Prophet and Book promised to the communities of earlier scriptures.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r5.anchor: والثالث أنه أراد بذلك ما وعد به أهل الكتب السالفة لأنهم وعدوا بنبي وكتاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r6.claim: The Book means the Quran; it is called a book because its parts are gathered together, like a battalion and a camel described with the same root.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r6.anchor: والكتاب القرآن وسمي كتابا لأنه جمع بعضه إلى بعض ومنه الكتيبة سميت بذلك لاجتماع بعضها إلى بعض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r7.anchor: الريب الشك والهدى الإرشاد والمتقون المحترزون مما اتقوه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r8.anchor: الريب الشك والهدى الإرشاد والمتقون المحترزون مما اتقوه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r9.claim: The mindful are those who guard themselves against what they avoid.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r9.anchor: والهدى الإرشاد والمتقون المحترزون مما اتقوه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r10.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r10.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah distinguishes taqwa as taking precaution from waraʿ as warding off a doubtful matter; taqwa has a certain cause, while waraʿ has a conjectural outcome.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r10.anchor: وفرق شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله بين التقوى والورع فقال التقوى أخذ عدة والورع دفع شبهة فالتقوى متحقق السبب والورع مظنون المسبب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r11.speaker: الخليل وابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r11.claim: Though phrased as a denial, the verse functions as a prohibition: no one ought to doubt this perfected, firmly ordered Book; the cited parallels use the same construction.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r12.speaker: المبرد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r12.claim: Al-Mubarrad reads the phrase as saying there is no doubt that the Book is guidance for the mindful.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r12.anchor: والثاني أن معناها لا ريب فيه أنه هدى للمتقين قاله المبرد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r13.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r13.claim: Muqatil and others understand the phrase to mean there is no doubt that the Book is from God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r13.anchor: والثالث أن معناها لا ريب فيه أنه من عند الله قاله مقاتل في آخرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r14.claim: Although some people have doubted it, the Book is true in itself and sound investigation reveals that truth, as the cited poem says.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r14.anchor: فالجواب انه حق في نفسه فمن حقق النظر فيه علم قال الشاعر ليس في الحق يا أمامة ريب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r15.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r15.claim: One answer to why guidance is attributed specifically to the mindful is that the verse names one group while leaving its opposite implicit, as in saying garments protect from heat while also meaning cold.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p23/r15.anchor: أراد المتقين والكافرين فاكتفى بذكر كر أحد الفريقين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p24/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p24/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p24/r1.claim: Guidance is attributed to the mindful because they are the ones who benefit from it, while the Prophet's warning also reaches those who do not fear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p24/r1.anchor: وكان منذرا لمن يخشى ولمن لا يخشى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and the named early authorities understand dhālika here as ‘this’; Ibn Kathir endorses them and says Arabic uses these two demonstratives interchangeably.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن جريج: قال ابن عباس: "ذلك الكتاب": هذا الكتاب. وكذا قال مجاهد، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r2.claim: Arabic speakers interchange the two demonstratives, using either in place of the other.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r2.anchor: والعرب تقارض بين هذين الاسمين من أسماء الإشارة فيستعملون كلا منهما مكان الآخر، وهذا معروف في كلامهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r3.anchor: و {الكتاب} القرآن. ومن قال: إن المراد بذلك الكتاب الإشارة إلى التوراة والإنجيل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r4.speaker: ابن جرير وغيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir and others are reported to take ‘the Book’ as the Torah and Gospel; Ibn Kathir rejects this as far-fetched and unsupported.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r4.anchor: ومن قال: إن المراد بذلك الكتاب الإشارة إلى التوراة والإنجيل، كما حكاه ابن جرير وغيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r5.claim: Al-rayb means doubt; Ibn Kathir cites al-Suddi, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud, many others, and says Ibn Abi Hatim knows no disagreement.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r5.anchor: والريب: الشك، قال السدي عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة الهمداني عن ابن مسعود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r6.claim: Rayb can also mean suspicion, as Jamil’s verse shows, or a need, as another poet’s verse shows.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r6.anchor: قال جميل: بثينة قالت يا جميل أربتني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r7.claim: The Qur’an is without doubt revealed from God, as the parallel opening of Surat al-Sajda says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r7.anchor: كما قال تعالى في السجدة: {الم * تنزيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين} [السجدة: 1، 2]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r8.claim: Some say the statement is formally declarative but means a prohibition: do not doubt the Qur’an.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هذا خبر ومعناه النهي، أي: لا ترتابوا فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r9.speaker: بعض القراء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r9.claim: Some reciters pause after ‘no doubt’ and begin again with ‘in it is guidance for the God-fearing.’
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r9.anchor: ومن القراء من يقف على قوله: {لا ريب} ويبتدئ بقوله: {فيه هدى للمتقين}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r10.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers pausing after ‘no doubt in it’; then ‘guidance’ directly describes the Qur’an, which is more emphatic than saying guidance is in it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r10.anchor: والوقف على قوله تعالى: {لا ريب فيه} أولى للآية التي ذكرنا، ولأنه يصير قوله: {هدى} صفة للقرآن، وذلك أبلغ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r11.claim: From the perspective of Arabic grammar, huda may be nominative as an adjective or accusative as a circumstantial expression.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r11.anchor: و {هدى} يحتمل من حيث العربية أن يكون مرفوعا على النعت، ومنصوبا على الحال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r12.claim: The Qur’an is guidance in itself, but only the righteous benefit from it; other verses likewise describe its benefit as specific to believers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p162#2/r12.anchor: وخصت الهداية للمتقين. كما قال: {قل هو للذين آمنوا هدى وشفاء والذين لا يؤمنون في آذانهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r1.claim: Taqwa is guarding oneself against what one dislikes; its root comes from wiqaya, protection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r1.anchor: وأصل التقوى: التوقي مما يكره لأن أصلها وقوى من الوقاية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r2.claim: Al-Nabigha and another poet use forms of the root for shielding oneself, illustrating taqwa as protection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r2.anchor: قال النابغة: سقط النصيف ولم ترد إسقاطه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r3.claim: Ubayy explains taqwa to Umar through a thorny path: the traveler gathers his clothes and walks carefully; Ubayy says that is taqwa.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r3.anchor: وقد قيل: إن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه، سأل أبي بن كعب عن التقوى، فقال له: أما سلكت طريقا ذا شوك؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r4.speaker: ابن المعتز
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r4.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz urges avoiding small and great sins, walking warily as over thorns, and not belittling small sins, since mountains consist of pebbles.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r4.anchor: ابن المعتز فقال: خل الذنوب صغيرها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r5.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r5.claim: Abu al-Darda recites that people seek their desires, but God wills otherwise, and taqwa is the best thing a person gains.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r5.anchor: وأنشد أبو الدرداء يوما: يريد المرء أن يؤتى مناه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r6.claim: Abu Umama reports the Prophet saying that after taqwa the best gain is a righteous spouse, who pleases, obeys, fulfills an oath, and protects herself and property when absent.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p164/r6.anchor: وفي سنن ابن ماجه عن أبي أمامة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما استفاد المرء بعد تقوى الله خيرا من زوجة صالحة

JISHUMI:v1p222/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p222/r1.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p222/r1.claim: An unnamed view treats the initials as a secret whose intended meaning is unknowable; Jishumi rejects it because revelation aims to be understood and early scholars interpreted them, so it conflicts with their consensus.
JISHUMI:v1p222/r1.anchor: وقيل: هو شيء يسر لا يعلم المراد به، وهذا لا يصح؛ لأن الغرض من الخطاب الإفهام

JISHUMI:v1p222/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p222/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
JISHUMI:v1p222/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir lengthens the pronoun ending in fīhi, ladayhi, ʿalayhi and similar forms; Ḥafṣ agrees in fīhi mahānan, while the others omit the yāʾ.
JISHUMI:v1p222/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير فيه بياء، وكذلك لديه وعليه، ونحوهما مما فيه هاء الكناية، ووافقه حفص

JISHUMI:v1p222/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p222/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p222/r3.claim: Arabic permits four forms here: with wāw, with yāʾ, or either short form; the underlying form is fīhū, and the faint hāʾ makes the sequence behave like yāʾ plus wāw, where wāw regularly turns to yāʾ, as in sayyid and mayyit.
JISHUMI:v1p222/r3.anchor: وتجوز العربية فيه أربعة أوجه، فيهو، وفيهي، وفيه، وفيه، والأصل فيهو

JISHUMI:v1p222/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p222/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p222/r4.claim: Jishumi prefers the common short reading because it is lighter without omitting a sound.
JISHUMI:v1p222/r4.anchor: والاختيار قراءة العامة؛ لأنه أخف من غير إخلاء

JISHUMI:v1p222/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p222/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير
JISHUMI:v1p222/r5.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Ibn Kathir assimilate the nūn of tanwīn into lām and rāʾ without nasalization; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī also assimilate before yāʾ, while the remaining readers retain nasalization.
JISHUMI:v1p222/r5.anchor: فأما هدى للمتقين بإدغام الغنة في اللام، فأبو جعفر وابن كثير يدغمانهما باللام والراء من غير إظهار الغنة

JISHUMI:v1p222/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p222/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p222/r6.claim: Hādhā points to what is near and dhāka to what is far; dhā is the noun, the lām is connective support, and the kāf marks address.
JISHUMI:v1p222/r6.anchor: إلا أن (هذا) لما قرب، وذاك لما بعد، و(ذا): اسم، واللام عماد، والكاف خطاب.

JISHUMI:v1p222/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p222/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p222/r7.claim: Kitāb derives from gathering, like a troop whose members assemble; literally it joins meaningful letters, and though a verbal noun it means the written thing, like ḥisāb or a dirham struck by the ruler.
JISHUMI:v1p222/r7.anchor: والكتاب: أصله الجمع، ومنه الكتيبة؛ لانضمام بعضهم إلى بعض، وحقيقة الكتاب: ضم بعض الحروف

JISHUMI:v1p222/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p222/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p222/r8.claim: Rayb means doubt; another definition adds suspicion along with doubt.
JISHUMI:v1p222/r8.anchor: والريب: الشك، وقيل: الريب تهمة مع الشك

JISHUMI:v1p222/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p222/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p222/r9.claim: Guidance means direction or indication in its basic sense.

JISHUMI:v1p222/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p222/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p222/r10.claim: Muttaqī derives from taqwā and protection; taqwā is a barrier between things, as when someone shields himself with armor, and the root wāw changes to tāʾ.
JISHUMI:v1p222/r10.anchor: والمتقي: أصله من التقوى، وهو من الوقاية

JISHUMI:v2p1053/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1053/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1053/r10.claim: The accusative in lā rayba fīhi is explained as an answer to the question “Is there any doubt in it?”
JISHUMI:v2p1053/r10.anchor: ونصب لا ريب لأنه جواب هل من ريب فيه

JISHUMI:v2p1053/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1053/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1053/r11.claim: Alternatively, lā rayba fīhi negates doubt comprehensively, while the other construction negates two things that might each have been assumed present.
JISHUMI:v2p1053/r11.anchor: وقيل: لا ريب فيه، على عموم النفي، فهو في أحدهما على عموم النفي، وفي الآخر على اشتمال النفي شيئين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r1.claim: The demonstrative can point back to the recited alif-lam-mim: once spoken and completed, that discourse is treated as distant.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r1.anchor: وقعت الإشارة إلى الم بعد ما سبق التكلم به وتقضى والمقضى في حكم المتباعد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r2.claim: An unnamed interpretation identifies the book as the one previously promised.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r2.anchor: وقيل معناه ذلك الكتاب الذي وعدوا به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r3.claim: If al-kitāb is the predicate, the masculine demonstrative follows its masculine meaning or name although the referent is a feminine sura.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r3.anchor: فإن جعلته خبره كان ذلك في معناه ومسماه مسماه فجاز إجراء حكمه عليه في التذكير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r4.claim: If al-kitāb is an adjective, the demonstrative explicitly points to the masculine generic noun kitāb, not to the feminine sura.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r4.anchor: وإن جعلته صفته فإنما أشير به إلى الكتاب صريحا لأن اسم الإشارة مشار به إلى الجنس الواقع صفة له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r5.speaker: الذبياني
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r5.claim: Al-Dhubyānī uses masculine ذاك with feminine نعمى, illustrating masculine agreement by the noun's sense or class.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p73#2/r5.anchor: وقال الذبياني ( نبئت نعمى على الهجران عاتبة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r1.claim: If alif-lam-mim names the sura, it may be the first subject, with dhalika a second subject and al-kitāb its predicate; the whole second clause predicates the first.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r2.claim: On that parse, the Qur'an is the complete book, uniquely deserving the name, as a person may be called the man for full manly virtues.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r2.anchor: ومعناه ان ذلك الكتاب هو الكتاب الكامل كأن ما عداه من الكتب في مقابلته ناقص

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r3.claim: Other parses take al-kitāb as an adjective for the promised book, make alif-lam-mim a predicate of an omitted demonstrative, or treat each phrase as an independent sentence.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r3.anchor: وأن يكون الكتاب صفة ومعناه هو ذلك الكتاب الموعود

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r4.claim: If alif-lam-mim is a sound rather than a sura name, dhalika may be subject and al-kitāb predicate, or al-kitāb an adjective with an omitted subject.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r4.anchor: وإن جعلت الم بمنزلة الصوت كان ذلك مبتدأ خبره الكتاب أي ذلك الكتاب المنزل هو الكتاب الكامل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r5.speaker: عبد الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r5.claim: Abd Allah reads the passage as “alif-lam-mim, the sending down of the Book; no doubt in it,” making its construction straightforward.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r5.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ( الم تنزيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r6.claim: Rayb is the verbal noun of rābanī and means unsettled psychological doubt, agitation, and distress.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r6.anchor: والريب مصدر رابني اذا حصل فيك الريبة وحقيقة الريبة قلق النفس واضطرابها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r7.claim: The Prophet teaches leaving what causes doubt for what does not, since doubt unsettles the heart while truth brings tranquility.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r7.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول 10 ( دع ما يريبك إلى ما لا يريبك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r8.claim: “The afflictions of time” are called rayb because they disturb minds and strike hearts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r8.anchor: ومنه ريب الزمان وهو ما يقلق النفوس ويشخص بالقلوب من نوائبه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r9.speaker: غير مسمى
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r9.claim: A report about a crouching gazelle says no one should trouble it, illustrating rayb as disturbance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p74/r9.anchor: 11 أنه مر بظبي حاقف فقال ( لا يربه أحد بشيء )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r1.claim: The verse does not deny that anyone doubts; it says the Book is no proper object or ground for doubt because its proof is manifest.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r1.anchor: فما أبعد وجود الريب منهم وإنما عرفهم الطريق إلى مزيل الريب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r2.claim: The challenge to produce a comparable sura directs doubters to test their eloquence; their inability shows there is no basis for suspicion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r2.anchor: فما أبعد وجود الريب منهم وإنما عرفهم الطريق إلى مزيل الريب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r3.claim: Putting the negation before “in it” focuses on denying suspicion and affirming truth, rather than implying some other book is doubtful.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r3.anchor: لأن القصد في إيلاء الريب حرف النفي نفي الريب عنه وإثبات انه حق وصدق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r4.claim: The order contrasts with “no harm in it,” which foregrounds that Paradise wine lacks the mind-clouding defect of worldly wine.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p75/r4.anchor: تفضيل خمر الجنة على خمور الدنيا بأنها لا تغتال العقول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r1.speaker: أبو الشعثاء
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r1.claim: Abu al-Shaʿthāʾ reads لا ريب فيه with nominative rafʿ; unlike the common reading, it permits rather than requires comprehensive negation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r1.anchor: بالرفع والفرق بينها وبين المشهورة ان المشهورة توجب الاستغراق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r2.speaker: نافع وعاصم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r2.claim: The usual pause is after فيه; Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim also pause after لا ريب, requiring an understood predicate, as in لا ضير.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r2.anchor: وعن نافع وعاصم انهما وقفا على ( لا ريب )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r3.claim: Hudā is a verbal noun on the fuʿal pattern for guidance that leads to the goal, as shown by its contrast with misguidance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r3.anchor: الهدى مصدر على فعل كالسرى والبكى وهو الدلالة الموصلة إلى البغية بدليل وقوع الضلالة في مقابلته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r4.claim: Mahdī may serve as praise like muhtadī: ihtadā is the responsive form of hadā and retains its root sense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76/r4.anchor: ويقال مهدي في موضع المدح كمهتد ولأن اهتدى مطاوع هدى ولن يكون المطاوع في خلاف معنى أصله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r1.claim: Calling already guided believers people of taqwa asks for increase and constancy, like asking to be kept on the straight path.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r1.anchor: هو كقولك للعزيز المكرم أعزك الله واكرمك تريد طلب الزيادة إلى ما هو ثابت فيه واستدامته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r2.claim: The Prophet calls a person slain in battle a “killer” when promising the slain enemy's spoils, illustrating naming by an imminent outcome.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r2.anchor: كقول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم 12 ( من قتل قتيلا فله سلبه )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās urges an intending pilgrim to hurry because illness, lost property, or another need may intervene, naming the person by an impending state.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r3.anchor: وعن إبن عباس 13 ( اذا أراد أحدكم الحج فليعجل فإنه يمرض المريض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r4.claim: The guided are called muttaqūn as they approach acquiring taqwa, just as the verse says people will bear the outcome of future conduct.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r4.anchor: فسمى المشارف للقتل والمرض والضلال قتيلا ومريضا وضالا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r5.claim: It says guidance for muttaqūn rather than the misguided because some are destined to persist in error while others will turn to guidance; the phrase concisely selects the latter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r5.anchor: لأن الضالين فريقان فريق علم بقاؤهم على الضلالة وهم المطبوع على قلوبهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r6.claim: The phrase opens the sura by naming God's allies and approved servants, befitting al-Baqara's place among the two luminous suras, the Qur'an's pinnacle, and the first of the repeated seven.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r6.anchor: وأيضا فقد جعل ذلك سلما إلى تصدير السورة التي هي أولى الزهراوين وسنام القرآن وأول المثاني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r7.claim: Muttaqī derives from waqā-ittaqā; wiqāya is thorough protection, like a horse or animal protecting its hoof from hurt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r7.anchor: والمتقي في اللغة اسم فاعل من قولهم وقاه فاتقى والوقاية فرط الصيانة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r8.claim: In religious usage, the muttaqī protects himself from acts or omissions that merit punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r8.anchor: وهو في الشريعة الذي يقي نفسه تعاطي ما يستحق به العقوبة من فعل أو ترك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r9.claim: Scholars differ on minor sins; the sounder view excludes them from this definition because avoiding major sins expiates them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r9.anchor: واختلف في الصغائر وقيل الصحيح أنه لا يتناولها لأنها تقع مكفرة عن مجتنب الكبائر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r10.claim: A person may be called a believer from outward appearance, but is called muttaqī or just only after tested knowledge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p76#2/r10.anchor: وقيل يطلق على الرجل اسم المؤمن لظاهر الحال والمتقي لا يطلق الا عن خبرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r1.claim: Hudā may be a predicate of an omitted subject, a predicate with لا ريب فيه, a subject after a fronted predicate, or an accusative circumstantial.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r1.anchor: الرفع لأنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو خبر مع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r2.claim: He prefers four independent, uncoordinated clauses: alif-lam-mim; the Book; its freedom from doubt; and its guidance, each embracing and continuing the previous one.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r2.anchor: والذي هو أرسخ عرقا في البلاغة أن يضرب عن هذه المحال صفحا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r3.claim: The sequence first marks the challenged discourse, then calls it the perfect Book, affirming the challenge; denying doubt certifies its truth, and calling it guidance confirms its certainty.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r3.anchor: فالثانية متحدة بالأولى معتنقة لها وهلم جرا إلى الثالثة والرابعة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r4.claim: Each clause has its own rhetorical force: delicate ellipsis in the first, grandeur in definiteness in the second, foregrounding rayb in the third, and ellipsis in the fourth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78/r4.anchor: ففي الأولى الحذف والرمز إلى الغرض بألطف وجه وأرشقه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78#2/r1.claim: Using the verbal noun hudā instead of the adjective hād, leaving it indefinite, and briefly naming the muttaqūn are further rhetorical refinements.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p78#2/r1.anchor: موضع الوصف الذي هو هاد وايراده منكرا والايجاز في ذكر المتقين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r1.claim: One view identifies the Book as the Torah and Gospel, making the statement a report about the past.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r1.anchor: أحدها : يعني التوراة والإنجيل , ليكون إخبارا عن ماض .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r2.speaker: الأصم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r2.claim: Al-Asamm takes it as the Qur'an revealed before this passage in Mecca and Medina.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r2.anchor: والثاني : يعني به ما نزل من القرآن قبل هذا بمكة والمدينة , وهذا قول الأصم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r3.claim: A third view means this Book; although dhalika normally indicates something absent, it can point to something present, as Khafaf ibn Nudba's verse shows.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r3.anchor: والثالث : يعني هذا الكتاب , وقد يستعمل ذلك في الإشارة إلى حاضر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r4.claim: If the Book means Torah and Gospel, one view addresses the Prophet: the promised book mentioned there is what was sent to Muhammad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r4.anchor: أحدهما : أن المخاطب به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , أي ذلك الكتاب الذي ذكرته في التوراة والإنجيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r5.claim: The other view addresses the Jews and Christians: the book promised to them is the one sent to Muhammad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r5.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن المخاطب به اليهود والنصارى , وتقديره : أن ذلك الذي وعدتكم به هو هذا الكتاب

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains rayb as doubt; a verse by Abd Allah ibn al-Zibara is cited as evidence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r6.anchor: أحدهما : أن الريب هو الشك , وهو قول ابن عباس , ومنه قول عبد الله بن الزبعرى

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r7.claim: A second lexical sense is accusation or suspicion, illustrated by Jamil's address to Buthayna.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67/r7.anchor: والتأويل الثاني : أن الريب التهمة ومنه قول جميل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r1.claim: The Book guides people away from error.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r2.speaker: الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r2.claim: Hasan al-Basri defines the God-conscious as those who avoid God's prohibitions and fulfill His obligations.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r2.anchor: أنهم الذين اتقوا ما حرم الله عليهم وأدوا ما افترض عليهم , وهذا قول الحسن البصري

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas defines them as those who fear God's punishment and hope for His mercy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r3.anchor: والثاني : أنهم الذين يحذرون من الله تعالى عقوبته ويرجون رحمته وهذا قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r4.claim: A third definition is those who avoid shirk and hypocrisy; al-Mawardi rejects it because such a person could still be sinful.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r4.anchor: والثالث : أنهم الذين اتقوا الشرك وبرئوا من النفاق وهذا فاسد , لأنه قد يكون كذلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r5.claim: Although it guides everyone, the Qur'an is specially called guidance for the God-conscious because they believe and affirm its contents.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p67#2/r5.anchor: وإن كان هدى لجميع الناس , لأنهم آمنوا وصدقوا بما فيه

BURSEVI:v1p19/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p19/r1.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
BURSEVI:v1p19/r1.claim: Ibn ʿArabi says the unfamiliar opening letters arrested Arab idle talk, drew listeners to the revelation after them, invited reflection on their relation to nearby words, and restrained obstinacy through their obscurity.
BURSEVI:v1p19/r1.anchor: وقال الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره في أول تفسير : {الاما * ذالك الكتاب}

BURSEVI:v1p19/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p19/r2.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v1p19/r2.claim: Some knowers hold that rational explanations of the disconnected letters are conjectural; only divine unveiling discloses God's intended meaning.
BURSEVI:v1p19/r2.anchor: قال بعض العارفين : كل ما قيل في شرحها بطريق النظر والاعتبار فتخمين النظر من قائله

BURSEVI:v1p19/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p19/r3.speaker: شيخي الأكمل
BURSEVI:v1p19/r3.claim: Bursevi cites his shaykh: people who deviate from knowledge stumble over such ambiguous passages, while rooted scholars are perplexed; some refrain from interpretation out of reverence.
BURSEVI:v1p19/r3.anchor: قال شيخي الأكمل في هامش كتاب "اللائحات البرقيات" له بعدما ذكر بعض خواص

MUQATIL:2:1-2/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:1-2/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:1-2/r1.claim: When Muhammad invited Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and Kaʿb ibn Asad to Islam, they denied him, claiming God sent no book after Moses; Muqatil says their denial prompted the verse.
MUQATIL:2:1-2/r1.anchor: وذلك أن كعب بن الأشرف، وكعب بن أسيد، لما دعاهما النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الإسلام

MUQATIL:2:1-2/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:1-2/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:1-2/r2.claim: “That Book” means this Qurʾān, the book the Jews rejected.
MUQATIL:2:1-2/r2.anchor: بمعنى هذا الكتاب الذى كفرت به اليهود

MUQATIL:2:1-2/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:1-2/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:1-2/r3.claim: There is no doubt that the Qurʾān came from God and that He revealed it to Muhammad.
MUQATIL:2:1-2/r3.anchor: لا شك فيه أنه من الله جاء، وهو أنزله على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:2:1-2/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:1-2/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:1-2/r4.claim: The Qurʾān guides people away from error, and the God-fearing are those who avoid associating partners with God.
MUQATIL:2:1-2/r4.anchor: هذا القرآن { هدى } من الضلالة { للمتقين } من الشرك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r1.claim: ‘That Book’ may be the Scripture promised through Moses and Jesus, or the book signaled by the opening letters alif lām mīm.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r1.anchor: ذلك الكتاب الذى وعد به على لسان موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام أو ذلك إشارة إلى الم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.claim: The masculine demonstrative can refer to the feminine sūra because its predicate is ‘the Book’; as an adjective it points directly to the masculine noun book.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.anchor: وإن كان صفته فالاشارة به إلى الكتاب صريحا لأن اسم الاشارة مشار به إلى الجنس الواقع صفة له

NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.claim: If alif lām mīm names the sūra, it may be a subject followed by a second subject and predicate, or a report with an omitted subject; if it is a sound, ‘that Book’ is subject and predicate.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.anchor: أن يكون الم مبتدأ وذلك مبتدأ ثانيا والكتاب خبره والجملة خبر للمبتدأ الأول

NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.claim: Calling it the Book means it is complete, with other books comparatively deficient, like calling someone ‘the man’ for full manliness.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.anchor: ومعناه أن ذلك هو الكتاب الكامل كأن ما عداه من الكتب فى مقابلته ناقص

NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.claim: Rayb is doubt that makes a person inwardly uneasy and unsettled; the verb rābanī means it caused such unease.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.anchor: وحقيقة الريبة قلق النفس واضطرابها ومنه قوله عليه السلام دع ما يريبك إلى مالا يريبك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r6.speaker: النبي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r6.claim: The Prophet counsels leaving what causes doubt for what does not; doubt unsettles the soul, while truth and soundness bring reassurance. No grading is stated.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r6.anchor: قوله عليه السلام دع ما يريبك إلى مالا يريبك فان الشك ريبة وان الصدق طمأنينة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r7.claim: The exhaustive negation means the Qur’an gives no proper ground for doubt because its proof is clear, not that nobody has ever doubted it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r7.anchor: من وضوح الدلالة له وسطوع البرهان بحيث لا ينبغى لمرتاب أن يقع فيه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r8.claim: Putting ‘doubt’ before ‘in it’ denies doubt of this book and affirms its truth; reversing the order could imply another book has no doubt. He contrasts this with 37:47.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r8.anchor: ولو أولى الظرف لقصد إلى ما يعد عن المراد وهو أن كتابا آخر فيه ريب لافيه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r9.speaker: نافع
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r9.claim: The common pause is after ‘in it’; Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim pause after ‘doubt,’ requiring the predicate ‘in it’ to be supplied.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r9.anchor: والوقف على فيه هو المشهور وعن نافع وعاصم أنهما وقفا على ريب ولا بد للواقف من أن ينوى خبرا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r10.speaker: مكي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r10.claim: The Meccan reader lengthens the hāʾ in fīhi throughout; Ḥafṣ agrees in fīhi mahānan. Sibawayh objects that this combines three still letters, treating the weak hāʾ like a still letter.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r10.anchor: فيه باشباع كل هاء مكى ووافقه حفص فى فيه مهانا وهو الأصل كقولك مررت به

NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r11.claim: Hudā is a verbal noun meaning guidance that leads to the goal; its contrast with misguidance is illustrated by 2:16.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r11.anchor: والهدى مصدر على فعل كالبكا وهو الدلالة الموصلة إلى البغية بدليل وقوع الضلالة فى مقابلة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r12.claim: It is guidance for the God-fearing though they are already guided, as a request for continued or increased guidance, like ‘Guide us to the straight path’ (1:6).
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r12.anchor: تريد طلب الزيادة على ما هو ثابت فيه واستدامته كقوله اهدنا الصراط المستقيم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r13.claim: They are called God-fearing as they approach taking up the garment of piety, just as one may name someone for a state he is nearing.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p11#2/r13.anchor: ولأنه سماهم عند مشارفتهم لا كتساء لباس التقوى متقين كقوله عليه السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r1.speaker: النبي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r1.claim: The Prophet’s statement that whoever kills an enemy receives the slain man’s gear illustrates naming someone by a state he approaches; no grading is stated.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās advises anyone intending pilgrimage to hasten, since illness may befall; this likewise names someone by an impending state. No grading is stated.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r2.anchor: وقول ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما إذا أراد احدكم الحج فليعجل فإنه يمرض المريض

NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r3.claim: It is not called guidance for the astray because some are known to persist in error while others are known to reach guidance; the book guides the latter, compressed in this wording.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r3.anchor: ولم يقل هدى للضالين لأنهم فريقان فريق علم بقاءهم على الضلالة وفريق علم أن مصيرهم إلى الهدى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r4.claim: Taqwā derives from waqā, ‘to protect’: the root’s wāw changes to tāʾ and assimilates in iftaʿala, yielding ittaqā; the noun denotes intense protection.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r4.anchor: والمتقى فى اللغة اسم فاعل من قولهم وقاه فاتقى ففاؤها واو ولامها ياء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r5.claim: In religious usage, the God-fearing person guards against doing or omitting what merits punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r5.anchor: وفى الشريعة من يقى نفسه تعاطى ما يستحق به العقوبة من فعل أو ترك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r6.claim: Hudā may be nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject or of lā rayba fīhi, or accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of the pronoun in fīhi.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r6.anchor: ومحل هدى الرفع لأنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو خبر مع لا ريب فيه لذلك أو النصب على الحال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r7.claim: He reads four unjoined clauses as tightly linked: the challenge, the complete Book, its certainty, then its guidance; each develops the preceding one.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r7.anchor: وقد أصيب بترتيبها مفصل البلاغة حيث جئ بها متناسقة هكذا من غير حرف عطف

NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r8.claim: The sequence uses ellipsis, the grandeur of the definite article, and the placing of doubt before ‘in it’; hudā is an indefinite verbal noun, as if the Book itself were guidance beyond full comprehension.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p12/r8.anchor: وفى الرابعة الحذف ووضع المصدر الذى هو هدى موضع الوصف الذى هو هاد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2/r14.claim: Al-Qurtubi answers that “no doubt in it” can be the oath’s answer; the oath interpretation is therefore sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2/r14.anchor: والجواب أن يقال: موضع القسم قوله تعالى: { لا ريب فيه } فلو أن إنسانا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda, Ikrima, and others take “that” to mean “this”: the demonstrative refers to the present Qur’an, yielding “ALM, this Book, no doubt in it.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r6.anchor: وهذا قول أبي عبيدة وعكرمة وغيرهما ومنه قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r7.speaker: معمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r7.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits Maʿmar’s gloss that “that Book” means “this Qur’an.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r7.anchor: وفي البخاري «وقال معمر ذلك الكتاب: هذا القرآن»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi notes that Arabic and prophetic usage can also use “this” for something distant, citing the report about sailing the bosom of this sea.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r8.anchor: قلت: وقد جاء «هذا» بمعنى «ذلك» ومنه قوله عليه السلام في حديث أم حرام:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r9.claim: Another view keeps the demonstrative in its normal distal sense; the following interpretations identify what it points to.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو على بابه إشارة إلى غائب. واختلف في ذلك الغائب على أقوال عشرة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r10.claim: “Guidance” means clarification and indication, as in the expression “that is God’s judgment.”

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r11.speaker: خفاف بن ندبة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r11.claim: Khafaf ibn Nudba’s poem uses “that” to mean “this,” supporting the demonstrative’s use for a present referent.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r11.anchor:
ومنه قول خفاف بن ندبة:
أقول له والرمح يأطر متنه
تأمل خفافا إنني أنا ذلكا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r12.claim: One distal reading identifies the Book as the decree written for creatures concerning felicity, misery, lifespans, and provision; nothing can alter it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r12.anchor: فقيل: { ذلك الكتاب } أي الكتاب الذي كتبت على الخلائق بالسعادة والشقاوة والأجل والرزق لا ريب فيه أي لا مبدل له

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r13.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r13.claim: Another distal reading identifies the Book as God's primordial self-written decree.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#2/r13.anchor: وقال: ذلك الكتاب أي الذي كتبت على نفسي في الأزل:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet’s statement in Sahih Muslim that God wrote mercy for Himself before creation; a version says mercy “preceded” His anger.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r1.anchor:
" أن رحمتي سبقت غضبي "
وفي صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r2.claim: A view takes “that” as God’s promise to send the Prophet a Book that water cannot erase.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r2.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى قد كان وعد نبيه عليه السلام أن ينزل عليه كتابا لا يمحوه الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r3.speaker: عياض بن حمار
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r3.claim: In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet reports God’s promise of a Book that water cannot wash away and that he recites asleep or awake.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r3.anchor: كما في صحيح مسلم من حديث عياض بن حمار المجاشعي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r4.claim: Another interpretation points to Qur’an already revealed in Mecca.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r4.anchor: وقيل: الإشارة إلى ما قد نزل من القرآن بمكة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r5.claim: After the Meccan promise of a weighty message, this Medinan revelation fulfills the promised Book; “that” points back to the awaited revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r5.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تبارك وتعالى لما أنزل على نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r6.claim: One view says the Qur’an is called ALM and “that Book” because the Torah and Gospel attest it; it encompasses their contents and adds more.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r6.anchor: وقيل: إن { ذلك } إشارة إلى ما في التوراة والإنجيل.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r7.claim: Another reading points to both Torah and Gospel: this Qur’an gathers what is in those two books, using a singular demonstrative for a dual referent.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن { ذلك الكتاب } إشارة إلى التوراة والإنجيل كليهما والمعنى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r8.claim: Some take “that” to point to the Preserved Tablet.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r8.anchor: وقيل: إن { ذلك } إشارة إلى اللوح المحفوظ.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r9.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r9.claim: Al-Kisa’i says it points to the Qur’an in heaven, which had not yet descended.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r9.anchor: وقال الكسائي: { ذلك } إشارة إلى القرآن الذي في السماء لم ينزل بعد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r10.claim: Another view takes the demonstrative to refer to God’s promise to the People of the Book to send Muhammad a Book.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r10.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى قد كان وعد أهل الكتاب أن ينزل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم كتابا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r11.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r11.claim: Al-Mubarrad identifies it as the Qur’an by which the People of the Book sought victory over the unbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r11.anchor: قال المبرد: المعنى هذا القرآن ذلك الكتاب الذي كنتم تستفتحون به على الذين كفروا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r13.claim: Kitab derives from kataba, to gather; related forms name a military troop, horses assembled into units, and binding a she-mule.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#3/r13.anchor: والكتاب مصدر من كتب يكتب إذا جمع ومنه قيل: كتيبة لاجتماعها. وتكتبت الخيل صارت كتائب. وكتبت البغلة: إذا جمعت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r1.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r1.claim: A poet uses the verb for binding a camel with straps, illustrating the related sense of kataba as tying.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r1.anchor:
لا تأمنن فزاريا حللت به
على قلوصك واكتبها بأسيار

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r2.claim: Al-Jawhari says al-katba, with a damma, is a bead; kutub are beads and katb means stringing them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r2.anchor: والكتبة بضم الكاف: الخرزة، والجمع كتب. والكتب: الخرز.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r3.claim: Kitab can mean writing made of alphabet letters, whether assembled or separate; it is called a book even when already written.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r3.anchor: والكتاب: هو خط الكاتب حروف المعجم مجموعة أو متفرقة وسمي كتابا وإن كان مكتوبا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r4.speaker: الجعدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r4.claim: Al-Jaʿdi’s verse uses kitab for God’s decree, which drove the speaker from his kin.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r4.anchor: والكتاب: الفرض والحكم والقدر قال الجعدي:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r5.claim: The negation is universal, so rayb is accusative as the noun governed by “no.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى: { لا ريب } نفي عام، ولذلك نصب الريب به.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبعرى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r6.claim: Ibn al-Zibʿari uses rayb to mean doubt, distinguishing truth from what an ignorant person says.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r6.anchor: أحدها: الشك قال عبد الله بن الزبعرى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r7.speaker: جميل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r7.claim: Jamil uses rayb for suspicion or accusation in the exchange with Buthayna.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r7.anchor:
وثانيها: التهمة قال جميل:
بثينة قالت يا جميل أربتني

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r8.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r8.claim: A poet uses rayb for a need or purpose, as in settling every need in Tihama and Khaybar.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r8.anchor:
وثالثها: الحاجة قال:
قضينا من تهامة كل ريب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r9.claim: The Book is true in itself and revealed by God, an attribute of His that is neither created nor originated, even though unbelievers may doubt it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r9.anchor: فكتاب الله تعالى لا شك فيه ولا ارتياب والمعنى: أنه في ذاته حق وأنه منزل من عند الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r10.speaker: قيل
