QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r10.claim: A reported interpretation reads the statement as a prohibition: “Do not doubt”; the clause then completes the sense that the Book is truly so.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r10.anchor: وقيل: هو خبر ومعناه النهي أي لا ترتابوا، وتم الكلام كأنه قال ذلك الكتاب حقا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r11.claim: The related verbs mean causing doubt and becoming suspect; rayb of time means its changing turns.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r11.anchor: وتقول: رابني هذا الأمر إذا أدخل عليك شكا وخوفا. وأراب: صار ذا ريبة فهو مريب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r12.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r12.claim: The passage gives five forms around fihi; the preferred form is standard, followed by the reading of al-Zuhri and Salam Abu al-Mundhir without a waw.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r12.anchor: وفيه خمسة أوجه أجودها: فيه هدى. ويليه فيه هدى بضم الهاء بغير واو

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r13.speaker: ابن كثير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r13.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the preposition with an added ya; the passage also permits waw and assimilation variants.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r13.anchor: ويليه فيهي هدى بإثبات الياء وهي قراءة ابن كثير. ويجوز فيهو هدى بالواو.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r14.claim: Huda is nominative as the subject, with fihi as its predicate.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r14.anchor: وارتفع { هدى } على الابتداء والخبر { فيه }.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r15.claim: In Arabic, huda means right direction and clarification: disclosure for people of knowledge, sound guidance, and added explanation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r15.anchor: والهدى في كلام العرب معناه الرشد والبيان أي فيه كشف لأهل المعرفة ورشد وزيادة بيان وهدى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r16.speaker: ذو الرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r16.claim: Dhu al-Rummah uses kutub for stitching, illustrating kitab’s underlying sense of joining or binding.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r16.anchor:
قال ذو الرمة:
وفراء غرفية أثأى خوارزها مشلشل ضيعته بينها الكتب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r17.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r17.claim: An anonymous poet uses kitab for a written note, comparing it to something stuck with glue.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r17.anchor: وسمي كتابا وإن كان مكتوبا كما قال الشاعر:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r18.claim: Guidance has two kinds; guidance by indication is within the ability of messengers and their followers.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#4/r18.anchor: الثانية: الهدى هديان: هدى دلالة، وهو الذي تقدر عليه الرسل وأتباعهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r1.claim: The passage describes the Godfearing as restrained and above the merely believing or obedient person.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r1.anchor: التقي ملجم والمتقي فوق المؤمن والطائع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r2.claim: The Godfearing person wards off punishment through righteous deeds and sincere prayer; taqwa is a barrier placed between oneself and harm.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r2.anchor: وهو الذي يتقي بصالح عمله وخالص دعائه عذاب الله تعالى، مأخوذ من اتقاء المكروه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r3.speaker: النابغة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r3.claim: Al-Nabigha’s verse illustrates ittaqa as using the hand to shield someone from what is harmful.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r3.anchor:
كما قال النابغة:
سقط النصيف ولم ترد إسقاطه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r4.speaker: آخر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r4.claim: Another poet uses ittaqa for shielding oneself with joined hand and forearm.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r4.anchor:
وقال آخر:
فألقت قناعا دونه الشمس واتقت
بأحسن موصولين كف ومعصم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r5.claim: Ibn Masud tells his nephew that among the many people, goodness lies in the repentant or Godfearing, and in the scholar or learner.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r5.anchor: وخرج أبو محمد عبد الغني الحافظ من حديث سعيد بن زربي أبي عبيدة عن عاصم بن بهدلة عن زر بن حبيش عن ابن مسعود

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r6.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r6.claim: Al-Bistami describes the Godfearing as one who speaks by God’s word and acts for God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r6.anchor: وقال أبو يزيد البسطامي: المتقي من إذا قال: قال الله، ومن إذا عمل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r7.speaker: أبو سليمان الداراني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r7.claim: Al-Darani defines the Godfearing as those whose hearts God has freed from love of desires.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r7.anchor: وقال أبو سليمان الداراني: المتقون الذين نزع الله عن قلوبهم حب الشهوات

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects defining taqwa only as avoiding shirk and hypocrisy, because someone may do so while still being sinful.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r8.anchor: وقيل: المتقي الذي اتقى الشرك وبرىء من النفاق. قال ابن عطية: وهذا فاسد لأنه قد يكون كذلك وهو فاسق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r9.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r9.claim: Umar explains taqwa to Ubayy with the image of crossing a thorny path while gathering himself and staying wary.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r9.anchor: وسأل عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أبيا عن التقوى فقال: هل أخذت طريقا ذا شوك؟ قال: نعم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r10.speaker: ابن المعتز
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r10.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz’s poem urges avoiding both small and grave sins, watching each step, and never dismissing a small sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r10.anchor:
وأخذ هذا المعنى ابن المعتز فنظمه:
خل الذنوب صغيرها
وكبيرها ذاك التقى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r11.claim: Taqwa gathers all good, is God’s charge to earlier and later peoples, and is the best benefit a person can acquire.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r11.anchor: التقوى فيها جماع الخير كله، وهي وصية الله في الأولين والآخرين، وهي خير ما يستفيده الإنسان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r12.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r12.claim: Abu al-Darda’s verses contrast worldly wealth with taqwa, which is the best thing a person gains.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r12.anchor: كما قال أبو الدرداء وقد قيل له: إن أصحابك يقولون الشعر وأنت ما حفظ عنك شيء فقال: يريد المرء أن يؤتى مناه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r13.speaker: أبو أمامة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r13.claim: Ibn Majah transmits from Abu Umama that the Prophet called a righteous, loyal, pleasing, trustworthy wife the believer’s best gain after taqwa.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r13.anchor:
ابن ماجه في سننه عن أبي أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يقول:
" ما استفاد المؤمن بعد تقوى الله خيرا له

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r14.claim: Ibn Masud’s second answer to his nephew is that among the many people, goodness lies in being a scholar or learner.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#5/r14.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: قال يوما لابن أخيه: يابن أخي ترى الناس ما أكثرهم؟

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#6/r1.claim: Taqwa derives from waqā, “to protect”: the initial waw changed to ta; taqi originally meant one who fears, and taqah derives from waqah, like tijah and turath from wijah and wirath.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#6/r1.anchor: والأصل في التقوى: وقوى على وزن فعلى فقلبت الواو تاء من وقيته أقيه أي منعته ورجل تقي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#6/r2.claim: Taqah originally derives from waqah; the forms tijah and turath similarly derive from wijah and wirath.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:1-2#6/r2.anchor: وكذلك تقاة كانت في الأصل وقاة كما قالوا: تجاه وتراث، والأصل وجاه ووراث.

RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r1.claim: A questioner objects that the referent is present, while ذٰلك ordinarily points to something distant.
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r1.anchor: المشار إليه ههنا حاضر ، و ( ذلك ) اسم مبهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r2.speaker: الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r2.claim: Al-Aṣamm takes ذٰلك as the earlier Meccan revelations: several suras had already descended, and a portion of the Quran may be called Quran or Book.
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r2.anchor: ما قاله الأصم : وهو أن الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r3.claim: The demonstrative can point to the promised Book God would send at Muhammad's mission, a promise the Prophet conveyed to his community; 73:5 supports the early timing.
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r3.anchor: أنه تعالى وعد رسوله عند مبعثه أن ينزل عليه كتابا لا يمحوه الماحي

RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r4.claim: Because al-Baqara is Medinan and largely addresses Israelites, ذٰلك can designate the Book Moses and Jesus foretold would come to a prophet descended from Ishmael.
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r4.anchor: وقد كانت بنو إسرائيل أخبرهم موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام أن الله يرسل محمدا

RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r5.claim: The revealed Quran may be called that Book because it is the same Book established in the Preserved Tablet, mentioned at 43:4.
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r5.anchor: ليعلم أن هذا المنزل هو ذلك الكتاب المثبت في اللوح المحفوظ

RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r6.claim: It may point back to Alif Lam Mim after those letters have been uttered; what has passed is treated as distant.
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r6.anchor: أنه وقعت الإشارة بذلك إلى ( آلم ) بعد ما سبق التكلم به

RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r7.claim: The thing sent crosses distance from sender to recipient, like handing someone an object and telling them to preserve that.
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r7.anchor: لما وصل من المرسل إلى المرسل إليه وقع في حد البعد

RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r8.claim: Although the Quran is present in form, its great rulings and many sciences exceed full human access, so it is absent in its secrets and realities and can be indicated as distant.
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#2/r8.anchor: القرآن وإن كان حاضرا نظرا إلى صورته لكنه غائب نظرا إلى أسراره وحقائقه

RAZI-FULL:v2p12#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#3/r1.claim: Razi argues that ذٰلك is not inherently restricted to distant objects: ذا is the demonstrative, ها alerts the hearer, and the attached kaf and lam add address and emphasis; convention favors distant reference, but context can let it refer nearby. The cited examples show هذا and ذلك interchanged.
RAZI-FULL:v2p12#3/r1.anchor: ذلك ، وهذا حرفا إشارة ، وأصلهما ( ذا )

RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r1.claim: Though the questioner treats the referent as the feminine sura, Razi says the reference is to the masculine named item Alif Lam Mim, not to the feminine word sura.
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r1.anchor: لأن المسمى هو ذلك البعض من القرآن وهو ليس بمؤنث

RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r2.claim: Kitāb is either a verbal noun like standing and fasting, or a faʿāl form meaning the object written, like libās for something worn; here it means the Quran.
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r2.anchor: أحدها : الكتاب وهو مصدر كالقيام والصيام وقيل : فعال

RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r3.claim: Across the Quran, kitāb can mean an obligation, a proof, a fixed term, or a master's contract with an enslaved person seeking manumission.
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r3.anchor: والكتاب جاء في القرآن على وجوه : أحدها : الفرض

RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r4.claim: Kitāb derives from katabtu al-shayʾ when I gathered it, as in katība for an assembled troop; the Quran is named thus as a bulwark against doubts, a gathering of sciences, or a repository of duties.
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r4.anchor: واشتقاق الكتاب من كتبت الشيء إذا جمعته

RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r5.claim: The Quran is another name of revelation, attested in verses describing it as Arabic, revealed in Ramadan, and guiding to the most upright way.
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r5.anchor: وثانيها : القرآن { قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن

RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās equates Quran with qirāʾa, like the synonymous forms khusrān and khasāra; 75:18 glosses Qurʾānahu as its recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r6.anchor: وللمفسرين فيه قولان : أحدهما : قول ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r7.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r7.claim: Qatāda derives Quran as a verbal noun from the expression for gathering water in a basin.
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r7.anchor: الثاني : وهو قول قتادة أنه مصدر من قول القائل

RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r8.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r8.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna says the Quran is so named because letters gather into words, words into verses, verses into suras, and suras into a Quran; it also gathers the sciences of earlier and later peoples.
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r8.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة : سمي القرآن قرآنا

RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r9.claim: The name Quran thus derives either from recitation or from gathering.
RAZI-FULL:v2p13/r9.anchor: فالحاصل أن اشتقاق لفظ القرآن إما من التلاوة أو من الجمعية

RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r1.claim: Furqān is explained either by the Quran's gradual revelation over more than twenty years, in contrast to other scriptures sent down all at once, or by its separating truth from falsehood and legal or interpretive categories.

RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r2.speaker: عكرمة والسدي
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r2.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Suddī explain Furqān as salvation: people escape the darkness of error through the Quran, as in the interpretation of 2:53.
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r2.anchor: وهو قول عكرمة والسدي ، وذلك لأن الخلق في ظلمات

RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r3.claim: The Quran is called dhikr because God reminds servants of its duties and commands; alternatively it is honor and renown for believers, Muhammad, and his community.
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r3.anchor: أنه ذكر من الله تعالى ذكر به عباده فعرفهم تكاليفه وأوامره

RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r4.claim: The Quran is also named tadhkira and dhikrā, as the reminder for the God-fearing and the reminder that benefits believers.
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r4.anchor: وأما التذكرة فقوله : { وإنه لتذكرة للمتقين }

RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r5.claim: The Quran is named Tanzīl, as revelation sent down by the Lord of the worlds through the Trustworthy Spirit.
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r5.anchor: وخامسها : التنزيل { وإنه لتنزيل رب العالمين

RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r6.claim: It is named ḥadīth because its arrival to the recipient is recent and because God addresses accountable people through it in a form like speech.
RAZI-FULL:v2p14/r6.anchor: سماه حديثا ؛ لأن وصوله إليك حديث

RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r1.claim: The Quran is a mawʿiẓa because God is the speaker, Gabriel receives it, and Muhammad is the one to whom it is recited.
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r1.anchor: وهو في الحقيقة موعظة لأن القائل هو الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r2.claim: The Quran is called ḥukm, ḥikma, ḥakīm, and muḥkam, with cited verses for each designation.

RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r3.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r3.claim: Al-Khalīl derives ḥikma from aḥkām and ilzām: making firm and binding.
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r3.anchor: فقال الخليل : هو مأخوذ من الأحكام والإلزام

RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r4.speaker: المؤرخ
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r4.claim: Al-Muʾarrikh derives ḥikma from the bit of a bridle, which restrains an animal, because wisdom restrains foolishness.
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r4.anchor: وقال المؤرخ : هو مأخوذ من حكمة اللجام

RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r5.claim: The Quran is called healing either from illnesses generally or from disbelief and doubt, which God calls a disease and which revelation removes from the heart.
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r5.anchor: وفيه وجهان : أحدهما : أنه شفاء من الأمراض

RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r6.claim: The Quran is called guidance and guide: it guides people and the God-fearing, and guides toward the most upright way and toward right guidance.

RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the straight path in 6:153 as the Quran.
RAZI-FULL:v2p14#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس في تفسيره : إنه القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r1.claim: The Quran is the rope of God; clinging to it in religion saves one from punishment in the afterlife and calamities in this world, like holding a rope saves someone from drowning and peril.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r1.anchor: في التفسير : إنه القرآن ، وإنما سمي به لأن المعتصم

RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r2.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r2.claim: The Prophet calls the Quran a protection for whoever holds fast to it, since it protects people from sins.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك سماه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عصمة

RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r3.claim: The Quran is mercy because nothing is greater than release from ignorance and misguidance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r3.anchor: وأي رحمة فوق التخليص من الجهالات والضلالات

RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r4.claim: It is called spirit because it gives life to souls; scripture also calls Gabriel and Jesus spirit.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r4.anchor: وإنما سمي به لأنه سبب لحياة الأرواح

RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r5.claim: The Quran is called stories either because it should be followed, as qaṣṣī means follow his tracks, or because it recounts earlier peoples' stories.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r5.anchor: سمي به لأنه يجب اتباعه { وقالت لاخته قصيه }

RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r6.claim: The Quran is named bayān, tibyān, and mubīn, supported by verses describing its clarity and explanatory reach.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r6.anchor: أما البيان فقوله : { هاذا بيان للناس }

RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r7.claim: Its basāʾir are proofs by which people see truth, like eyesight that reveals the way to escape.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r7.anchor: أي هي أدلة يبصر بها الحق تشبيها بالبصر الذي يرى طريق الخلاص

RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r8.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r8.claim: One explanation of faṣl is judgment, since God judges among people through the Quran with truth.

RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r9.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r9.claim: Another explanation is that the Quran separates people at resurrection, guiding some to Paradise and driving others to Hell; one who follows it as imam reaches Paradise, while one who leaves it behind is driven to the Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15/r9.anchor: قيل لأنه يفصل بين الناس يوم القيامة فيهدي قوما إلى الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r1.claim: The Quran is named the stars because it descended star by star.

RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r2.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r2.claim: It is called mathānī because its stories and accounts are repeated within it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r2.anchor: قيل لأنه ثنى فيه القصص والأخبار

RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets God's blessing in 93:11 as the Quran.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس يعني به القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r4.claim: The Quran is a proof from God because eloquent speakers have been unable to produce anything like it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r4.anchor: وكيف لا يكون برهانا وقد عجزت الفصحاء عن أن يأتوا بمثله

RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r5.claim: The Quran is both bearer of good news and warner, like the messengers and Muhammad: it promises Paradise to the obedient and warns the disobedient of Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r5.anchor: يعني مبشرا بالجنة لمن أطاع وبالنار منذرا لمن عصى

RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r6.claim: The Quran is called qayyim because it stands on its own in explanation and instruction; the passage also notes this title for religion and God as al-Qayyūm.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r6.anchor: وإنما سمي قيما لأنه قائم بذاته في البيان والإفادة

RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r7.claim: The Quran is muhaymin, derived from amin, because those who cling to it are safe from harm in this world and the next; God sent it through the trustworthy Prophet to a community entrusted over creation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p15#2/r7.anchor: وهو مأخوذ من الأمين ، وإنما وصف به لأنه من تمسك بالقرآن

RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r1.claim: The Quran is guide, and God is also called the Guide; a report uses the designation 'the Light, the Guide.'
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r1.anchor: والله تعالى هو الهادي لأنه جاء في الخبر ( النور الهادي )

RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r2.claim: The Quran is a light; the term is also used for God, Muhammad, his religion, its exposition, the Torah, the Gospel, and faith.
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r2.anchor: وفي القرآن { واتبعوا النور الذى أنزل معه }

RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r3.claim: The Quran is true and named al-Ḥaqq because it opposes and removes falsehood, as in the image of truth striking falsehood until it vanishes.
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r3.anchor: فسماه الله حقا ؛ لأنه ضد الباطل فيزيل الباطل

RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r4.claim: The Quran is ʿazīz, like God, the Prophet, and the community; the adjective means either overpowering, since the Quran defeats opponents and resists imitation, or unmatched.
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r4.anchor: وللعزيز معنيان : أحدهما : القاهر ، والقرآن كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r5.claim: The Quran is called karīm because no other book yields such wisdom and knowledge; God, Moses, reward, the Throne, Gabriel, and Solomon's letter are also called noble, and clinging to this noble book earns noble reward.
RAZI-FULL:v2p16/r5.anchor: لأنه لا يستفاد من كتاب من الحكم والعلوم ما يستفاد منه

RAZI-FULL:v2p17/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p17/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p17/r1.claim: The Quran is called great; the text also applies the epithet to God, the Throne, the Resurrection Day, the Hour's earthquake, the Prophet's character, knowledge, women's plotting, Pharaoh's magicians' sorcery, believers' reward, and hypocrites' punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v2p17/r1.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى سمى نفسه عظيما فقال : { وهو العلي العظيم }

RAZI-FULL:v2p17/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p17/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p17/r2.claim: The Quran is a blessed reminder; Razi calls its chain blessed too: it was sent by a blessed angel, on a blessed Prophet, to a blessed community, like the other blessed things listed.
RAZI-FULL:v2p17/r2.anchor: فالقرآن ذكر مبارك أنزله ملك مبارك في ليلة مباركة على نبي مبارك

RAZI-FULL:v2p17/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p17/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p17/r3.claim: Razi begins explaining how Alif Lam Mim connects to 'that Book'; citing al-Kashshāf, he says that if the letters name the sura, there are several possible compositional relations.
RAZI-FULL:v2p17/r3.anchor: في بيان اتصال قوله : { الم } بقوله : { ذالك الكتاب }

RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r1.claim: One parsing makes alif-lām-mīm the first subject, “that” a second subject, and “the Book” its predicate; this presents the Qur’an as the complete Book, with other books deficient by comparison.
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r1.anchor: أن يكون { الم } مبتدأ و { ذالك } مبتدأ ثانيا و { الكتاب } خبره والجملة خبر المبتدأ الأول

RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, “the Book” is an adjective, and “that Book” means the promised Book.
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r2.anchor: وأن يكون الكتاب صفة ، ومعناه هو ذلك الكتاب الموعود

RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r3.claim: Alif-lām-mīm may predicate an omitted subject (“these letters”), followed by “that Book” as a second predicate or apposition, with “the Book” adjectival.
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r3.anchor: وأن يكون { الم } خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هذه { الم * ويكون * ذالك الكتاب } خبرا ثانيا أو بدلا على أن الكتاب صفة

RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r4.claim: Another analysis treats alif-lām-mīm and “that Book” as two separate sentences.
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r4.anchor: وأن تكون هذه { الم } جملة و { ذالك الكتاب } جملة أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r5.claim: If alif-lām-mīm is treated as a sound, “that” may be subject with “the Book” its predicate, or “the Book” an adjective, or an omitted subject may mean “composed of these letters.”
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r5.anchor: وإن جعلت { الم } بمنزلة الصوت كان { ذالك } مبتدأ وخبره { الكتاب } أي ذلك الكتاب المنزل هو الكتاب الكامل

RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r6.claim: Abdullah’s reading connects these letters directly to “the sending down of the Book”; al-Rāzī says this composition is evident.
RAZI-FULL:v2p17#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله { الم * تنزيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه } ( السجدة : 2 ) وتأليف هذا ظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r1.claim: Rayb is close to doubt but adds suspicion of something bad; “rābanī” means that I suspected something bad of someone.
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r1.anchor: الريب قريب من الشك ، . وفيه زيادة ، كأنه ظن سوء

RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r2.claim: Rayb can also mean the events of time or what stirs anger in the heart; both usages return to doubt, since feared events are possible and inward agitation is uncertain. The verse and poem illustrate these usages.
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r2.anchor: هذان قد يرجعان إلى معنى الشك ، لأن ما يخاف من ريب المنون محتمل

RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r3.claim: The verse denies that the Book gives any ground for doubt: its truth, divine origin, and miraculous character are beyond reasonable suspicion.
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r3.anchor: والمقصود أنه لا شبهة في صحته ، ولا في كونه من عند الله

RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r4.claim: Reading the denial specifically as denying doubt in the Qur’an’s miraculousness is especially apt because 2:23 challenges doubters to match what was sent down.
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r4.anchor: على الخصوص كان أقرب لتأكيد هذا التأويل بقوله : { وإن كنتم فى ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا }

RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r5.claim: Against the objection that people do in fact doubt the Qur’an, or that God’s own lack of doubt would be pointless, al-Rāzī says its clarity is such that no reasonable person ought to doubt it; Arab eloquence could not match even its shortest sūra.
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r5.anchor: بلغ في الوضوح إلى حيث لا ينبغي لمرتاب أن يرتاب فيه ، والأمر كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r6.claim: The order puts the most important denial first: “no doubt in it” avoids suggesting that some other book is doubtful while this one is not.
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r6.anchor: يقدمون الأهم فالأهم ، وههنا الأهم نفي الريب بالكلية عن الكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r7.claim: The contrast with “no harm in it” in 37:47 serves a different purpose: it distinguishes the wine of Paradise, which does not impair reason, from worldly wine.
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r7.anchor: كما قصد في قوله : { لا فيها غول } تفضيل خمر الجنة على خمور الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r8.speaker: أبو الشعثاء
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r8.claim: Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ reads “lā rayba fīhi” with rayb in the nominative.
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r8.anchor: قرأ أبو الشعثاء { لا ريب فيه } بالرفع

RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r9.claim: In the familiar reading, lā negates the genus, denying the very reality of doubt and therefore every individual instance; the nominative reading likewise contradicts the affirmation of even one doubt.
RAZI-FULL:v2p18/r9.anchor: إن قوله : { لا ريب } نفي لماهية الريب ونفي الماهية يقتضي نفي كل فرد

RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r1.speaker: نافع
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim pause after “lā rayb”; that pause requires an understood predicate, as in the idioms “no harm” and “no problem,” common in the Hijaz, yielding “there is no doubt; in it is guidance.”
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r1.anchor: وعن نافع وعاصم أنهما وقفا على { لا ريب } ولا بد للواقف من أن ينوي خبرا

RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r2.claim: The well-known pause after “fīhi” is preferable: it makes the Book itself guidance, whereas the other pause says only that guidance is contained in it; the Qur’an is repeatedly called light and guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r2.anchor: القراءة الأولى أولى ؛ لأن على القراءة الأولى يكون الكتاب نفسه هدى

RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī defines guidance as indication (dalāla), rejecting definitions that make it guidance received or knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r3.anchor: الهدى عبارة عن الدلالة ، وقال صاحب الكشاف : الهدى هو الدلالة الموصلة إلى البغية

RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī defines guidance as an indication that conveys its recipient to the goal.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r4.anchor: وقال صاحب الكشاف : الهدى هو الدلالة الموصلة إلى البغية

RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r5.claim: Guidance need not result in being guided: God says He guided Thamūd, yet they chose blindness, and Arabic permits “I guided him, but he was not guided.”
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r5.anchor: أثبت الهدى مع عدم الاهتداء ، ولأنه يصح في لغة العرب أن يقال : هديته فلم يهتد

RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues from the contrast between guidance and error, the praise implied by “guided,” and the fact that iḥtada is the responsive form of hadā, like breaking and being broken, that guidance reaches its goal.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r6.anchor: واحتج صاحب الكشاف بأمور ثلاثة : أولها : وقوع الضلالة في مقابلة الهدى

RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r7.claim: Al-Rāzī replies that misguidance opposes guidance, while error opposes being guided; only those who benefit are called guided, and an unused means counts as if nonexistent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r7.anchor: الفرق بين الهدى وبين الاهتداء معلوم بالضرورة ، فمقابل الهدى هو الإضلال ومقابل الاهتداء هو الضلال

RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r8.claim: The analogy with “commanded and obeyed” does not establish that guidance entails its recipient’s response; “I guided him, but he was not guided” directly counters that inference.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r8.anchor: أن الائتمار مطاوع الأمر يقال : أمرته فائتمر ، ولم يلزم منه

RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r9.claim: Guidance cannot mean knowledge alone, because God calls the Qur’an guidance although the Qur’an itself is not knowledge; guidance therefore means indication.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19/r9.anchor: وصف القرآن بأنه هدى ولا شك أنه في نفسه ليس بعلم ، فدل على أن الهدى هو الدلالة

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r1.claim: Taqwā is the active participle of waqā, to protect; protection is intense guarding. Since the verse praises the God-fearing, it especially means observing worship and avoiding prohibitions in religious matters.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r1.anchor: المتقي في اللغة اسم فاعل من قولهم وقاه فاتقى ، والوقاية فرط الصيانة

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r2.claim: Some say taqwā includes avoiding minor sins, just as minor sins are included in threats of punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r2.anchor: فقال بعضهم : يدخل كما يدخل الصغائر في الوعيد

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r3.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r3.claim: Others say minor sins are not included in taqwā; all agree that repentance for every sin is obligatory, and dispute only whether a person who fails to avoid minor sins still merits the name muttaqī.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون : لا يدخل ، ولا نزاع في وجوب التوبة عن الكل

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r4.speaker: النبي ﷺ
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet says a servant does not reach the rank of the God-fearing until he leaves harmless matters out of caution against harmful ones.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r4.anchor: فروي عنه عليه السلام أنه قال : ( لا يبلغ العبد درجة المتقين حتى يدع ما لا بأس به

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the God-fearing as those who fear punishment for abandoning what desire inclines them toward and hope for mercy by affirming what God sent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أنهم الذين يحذرون من الله العقوبة

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r6.claim: Taqwā can mean fear of God, as in commands to fear the Lord, fear Him, and fear the Day of Judgment.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r6.anchor: واعلم أن التقوى هي الخشية ، قال في أول النساء : { تفلحون يأيها الناس اتقوا ربكم }

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r7.claim: Depending on context, taqwā in the Qur’an denotes faith or tawḥīd, repentance, obedience, refraining from sin, or sincerity; the cited verses illustrate each usage.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r7.anchor: والغرض الأصلي منها الإيمان تارة ، والتوبة أخرى ، والطاعة ثالثة ، وترك المعصية رابعا

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r8.claim: Taqwā is an exalted station: God is with those who fear Him and do good, and the most honored before God are the most God-fearing.

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r9.speaker: النبي ﷺ
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r9.claim: In a report attributed to the Prophet through Ibn ʿAbbās, the most honored person is the one who fears God, the strongest is the one who trusts God, and the richest is the one more confident in God’s provision than in his own possessions.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r9.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال عليه السلام : ( من أحب أن يكون أكرم الناس فليتق الله ، ومن أحب أن يكون أقوى الناس فليتوكل على الله

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r10.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r10.claim: ʿAlī defines taqwā as not persisting in sin and not being deluded by one’s acts of obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r10.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب : التقوى ترك الإصرار عل المعصية

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan says taqwā is choosing no one over God and knowing that all affairs are in God’s hands.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r11.anchor: قال الحسن : التقوى أن لا تختار عل الله سوى الله ، وتعلم أن الأمور كلها بيد الله

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r12.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r12.claim: Ibrāhīm ibn Adham defines taqwā as having no fault found by people in one’s speech, by angels in one’s deeds, or by the Lord of the Throne in one’s inward self.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r12.anchor: وقال إبراهيم بن أدهم : التقوى أن لا يجد الخلق في لسانك عيبا . ولا الملائكة في أفعالك

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r13.speaker: الواقدي
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r13.claim: Al-Wāqidī says taqwā is adorning one’s inward self for the Truth as one adorns one’s outward self for people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r13.anchor: وقال الواقدي : التقوى أن تزين سرك للحق كما زينت ظاهرك للخلق

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r14.claim: Other definitions say the God-fearing do not appear where their Lord has forbidden them, or follow the Prophet, leave worldly life behind, seek sincerity and fidelity, and avoid the unlawful.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r14.anchor: ويقال : التقوى أن لا يراك مولاك حيث نهاك ، ويقال : المتقي من سلك سبيل المصطفى

RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r15.claim: Since the Qur’an is called guidance for all people in 2:185 and here for the God-fearing, al-Rāzī infers that the God-fearing are all people; one who is not God-fearing is, as it were, not human.
RAZI-FULL:v2p19#2/r15.anchor: أنه تعالى بين أن القرآن هدى للناس في قوله : { شهر رمضان الذى أنزل فيه القرآن هدى للناس } ( البقرة : 185 ) ثم قال ههنا في القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r1.claim: Although the Qur’an is evidence for believers and unbelievers alike about the Creator, religion, and the Messenger’s truth, al-Rāzī names the God-fearing because they are the ones who benefited from it; if guidance means conveying to the goal, it applies only to them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r1.anchor: القرآن كما أنه هدى للمتقين ودلالة لهم على وجود الصانع ، وعلى دينه وصدق رسوله ، فهو أيضا دلالة للكافرين

RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r2.claim: An objection says the Qur’an cannot be guidance when it contains ambiguous passages, depends on reason to distinguish clear from ambiguous, and appears to contain opposing claims about compulsion and free choice.
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r2.anchor: كيف وصف القرآن كله بأنه هدى وفيه مجمل ومتشابه كثير ؛ ولولا دلالة العقل لما تميز المحكم عن المتشابه

RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī cites ʿAlī’s warning to Ibn ʿAbbās, sent to debate the Khārijites, not to argue from the Qur’an because it admits two interpretations.
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r3.anchor: نقل عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه أنه قال لابن عباس حين بعثه رسولا إلى الخوارج

RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī replies that ambiguous and concise passages remain guidance because their intended meaning can be identified through reason or transmitted evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r4.anchor: ذلك المتشابه والمجمل لما لم ينفك عما هو المراد على التعيين وهو إما دلالة العقل أو دلالة السمع صار كله هدى

RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r5.claim: A further objection says the Qur’an cannot guide to knowledge of God, His attributes, or prophecy if its own authority must already be established for it to prove them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p21/r5.anchor: كل ما يتوقف صحة كون القرآن حجة على صحته لم يكن القرآن هدى فيه

RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r1.claim: Guidance need only concern some matters, such as defining religious laws or confirming rational knowledge; it need not cover everything. Al-Rāzī says this proves an unqualified expression does not imply universal scope.
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r1.anchor: ليس من شرط كونه هدى أن يكون هدى في كل شيء ، بل يكفي فيه أن يكون هدى في بعض الأشياء

RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r2.claim: Against the claim that a text with many conflicting interpretations cannot be clear guidance, al-Rāzī answers that the criticism applies to exegetes who merely list conflicting views; he has preferred one by evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r2.anchor: من تكلم في التفسير بحيث يورد الأقوال المتعارضة ، ولا يرجح واحدا منها على الباقي يتوجه عليه هو هذا السؤال

RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows “guidance for the God-fearing” to be nominative as a predicate of an omitted subject, conjoined with “no doubt,” or a subject predicated by the preceding adverb; it may also be an accusative circumstantial phrase.

RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī sees four independent, unjoined statements—alif-lām-mīm, “that Book,” “no doubt in it,” and “guidance for the God-fearing”—as a tightly interlinked sequence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r4.anchor: إن قوله : { الضالين الم } جملة برأسها ، أو طائفة من حروف المعجم مستقلة بنفسها

RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī favors the sequence’s rhetorical force: the opening signals the challenge, the Book is declared supremely perfect, doubt is denied as testimony to that perfection, and guidance confirms its certainty.
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r5.anchor: نبه أولا على أنه الكلام المتحدي به ، ثم أشير إليه بأنه الكتاب المنعوت بغاية الكمال

RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r6.claim: The four clauses gain force respectively through ellipsis and delicate allusion, the grandeur of definiteness, placing “doubt” before “in it,” and ellipsis plus the indefinite verbal noun “guidance” instead of the adjective “guiding.”
RAZI-FULL:v2p21#2/r6.anchor: ففي الأولى الحذف والرمز إلى الغرض بألطف وجه ، وفي الثانية ما في التعريف من الفخامة

ITQAN:v1p259/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p259/r6.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p259/r6.claim: Ibn al-Jazari reports Hamza's emphatic-negation lengthening on lā of absolute negation, but at an intermediate length because its cause is weaker.
ITQAN:v1p259/r6.anchor: وقد ورد عن حمزة مد المبالغة للنفي في لا التي للتبرئة نحو

RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r5.claim: Razi refers back to Quran 2:2, where the Quran is guidance for the God-fearing, to reconcile that description with calling it guidance for all people here.
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r5.anchor: بينا تفسير الهدى في قوله تعالى
